epics.title: Foundation and schema
epics.goal: A fresh `docker compose down -v && up --build` boots the API, applies the `AddStation` migration to a `Sessions`-bearing schema, binds validated `Station` options, and logs `analysis provider: Stub` — nothing announces yet, but every later epic compiles against these types.

features.title: Packages, StationOptions and Station configuration
features.summary: Fix the package baseline (`Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.Abstractions 10.0.0` and `InternalsVisibleTo AdventureTime.Tests` in `AdventureTime.Infrastructure.csproj`; drop obsolete `MediatR.Extensions.Microsoft.DependencyInjection` from `AdventureTime.csproj`), add `AdventureTime.Application/Config/StationOptions.cs` with `enum AnalysisProvider`, and put the `Station` section into `AdventureTime/appsettings.json` and `Station__AnalysisProvider` into `docker-compose.yml`. Options binding and `.Validate(...).ValidateOnStart()` are written here as the first lines of the `AddInfrastructure` block, but the block's full final shape (store, queue, hosted-service order) is owned by F5.1 under TR-49. Verified by `dotnet build` clean of NU1608 and the app refusing to start on out-of-range Station values.

tickets.title: Fix package baseline in Infrastructure and API project files
tickets.context: This is the first ticket in the backlog. Today the Infrastructure project has no hosting abstractions because nothing in the solution runs in the background, the API project still carries the obsolete MediatR DI extensions package that produces the NU1608 warning on every build, and there is no test project for internals to be visible to.
tickets.motivation: Two hosted services (the sweeper and the worker) and a test project are about to be added. Without the Hosting package they cannot compile in Infrastructure, and without the InternalsVisibleTo the store's SQL and row types would have to be made public just to be tested. The stale warning also hides any new warning later tickets introduce.
tickets.goal: A warning-free solution build with exactly the packages the station needs, and a DbContext registration that explicitly stays scoped with no retry-on-failure strategy.
tickets.value: Every later ticket compiles against a stable, quiet baseline. Leaving retry-on-failure off is not housekeeping: an execution strategy would replay the advisory-locked admission transaction and the post-commit enqueue, which would break the capacity guarantee, so this ticket is the first place that invariant is protected.
tickets.description: Bring the two project files to the baseline the rest of the backlog builds on. In /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/AdventureTime.Infrastructure.csproj add `<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.Abstractions" Version="10.0.0" />` (supplies `BackgroundService` for F5.1/F5.2 and `IHostEnvironment` for F1.2) and a new `<ItemGroup><InternalsVisibleTo Include="AdventureTime.Tests" /></ItemGroup>` so the future test project (F2.4) can reach `StationSql`, `StationRows` and `StubDeepAnalysisService.StubDelay`. In /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.csproj remove the `MediatR.Extensions.Microsoft.DependencyInjection 11.1.0` reference, which is the source of today's NU1608 warning (verified: it pins MediatR < 12 while 13.0.0 is resolved); `services.AddMediatR(cfg => ...)` in AdventureTime.Application/DependencyInjection.cs comes from the MediatR 13 main assembly, which AdventureTime.Application references on its own, so nothing else changes. Do NOT touch `AddDbContext<AppDbContext>` in AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs: it stays scoped and `EnableRetryOnFailure` must never be enabled (TR-51, TR-59), because an execution strategy would re-run the advisory-locked admission block. Verify with a full solution build.
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet build /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.sln` succeeds and `dotnet build AdventureTime.sln 2>&1 | grep NU1608` prints nothing (TR-51)

`AdventureTime.Infrastructure/AdventureTime.Infrastructure.csproj` contains `<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.Abstractions" Version="10.0.0" />` and `dotnet list AdventureTime.Infrastructure/AdventureTime.Infrastructure.csproj package` lists it as a top-level package (TR-51)
`AdventureTime.Infrastructure/AdventureTime.Infrastructure.csproj` contains `<InternalsVisibleTo Include="AdventureTime.Tests" />` inside an `<ItemGroup>` (TR-51)

`grep -c MediatR.Extensions.Microsoft.DependencyInjection AdventureTime/AdventureTime.csproj` prints `0`, and `AdventureTime.Application/DependencyInjection.cs` is unchanged in the diff (`services.AddMediatR(cfg => ...)` still compiles) (TR-51)

`grep -rn --exclude-dir=bin --exclude-dir=obj EnableRetryOnFailure AdventureTime.Infrastructure/` prints nothing, and the `AddDbContext<AppDbContext>` call in `AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` is unchanged in the diff (default scoped lifetime) (TR-51)

tickets.title: Add StationOptions and AnalysisProvider enum in Application/Config
tickets.context: Configuration today is two typed option classes for the LLM keys plus a bare boolean named Claude. The station introduces seven knobs: capacity, sweep interval, processing timeout, three TTL bounds, and the analysis provider.
tickets.motivation: Capacity and the clocks are the parameters of the load-bearing mechanisms. Hard-coding them would make the concurrency tests and operator tuning impossible, and reading them once at startup is what implements the decision that lowering capacity never evicts a live session.
tickets.goal: A StationOptions class carrying the exact defaults of the requirements, bindable from a Station section, with TimeSpan members so the appsettings strings bind without custom converters.
tickets.value: One type defines what the station's limits are, every mechanism reads the same numbers, and tests can construct options in memory. The provider enum replaces a boolean that could not express the stub, which is what makes offline development possible later in this epic.
tickets.description: Create /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Application/Config/StationOptions.cs in namespace `AdventureTime.Application.Config` (next to the existing `AnthropicConfig.cs` and `OpenAiConfig.cs`). It holds `public enum AnalysisProvider { Stub, Claude, OpenAi }` and `public class StationOptions` with `public const string SectionName = "Station";` and the properties, defaults and CLR types of TR-35/TR-63 exactly, as settable auto-properties: `public int Capacity { get; set; } = 3; public TimeSpan SweepInterval { get; set; } = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(15); public TimeSpan ProcessingTimeout { get; set; } = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10); public int TtlDefault { get; set; } = 1800; public int TtlMin { get; set; } = 60; public int TtlMax { get; set; } = 86400; public AnalysisProvider AnalysisProvider { get; set; } = AnalysisProvider.Stub;` (a property named like its enum type is legal C#). Put NO DataAnnotations on the class: the validation package is not referenced and range checking is done by the `.Validate(...)` predicate of F1.1-T3. `TimeSpan` members are what makes the `"00:00:15"` / `"00:10:00"` strings of appsettings bind (TR-55). This type is consumed via `IOptions<StationOptions>` and read once at construction by the store, sweeper, worker and handlers (A4: capacity is read at startup, lowering never evicts); the `AnalysisProvider` enum is what F1.2 binds `Station:AnalysisProvider` to (TR-50).
acceptance_criteria: File `AdventureTime.Application/Config/StationOptions.cs` exists, declares `public const string SectionName = "Station"` and `public enum AnalysisProvider { Stub, Claude, OpenAi }` in namespace `AdventureTime.Application.Config`, and `dotnet build AdventureTime.Application` succeeds (TR-35)

`grep -c -E 'Capacity \{ get; set; \} = 3;|SweepInterval \{ get; set; \} = TimeSpan.FromSeconds\(15\);|ProcessingTimeout \{ get; set; \} = TimeSpan.FromMinutes\(10\);|TtlDefault \{ get; set; \} = 1800;|TtlMin \{ get; set; \} = 60;|TtlMax \{ get; set; \} = 86400;|AnalysisProvider \{ get; set; \} = AnalysisProvider.Stub;' AdventureTime.Application/Config/StationOptions.cs` prints `7`, so `new StationOptions()` yields the TR-35 defaults (Capacity 3, SweepInterval 00:00:15, ProcessingTimeout 00:10:00, TtlDefault 1800, TtlMin 60, TtlMax 86400, AnalysisProvider Stub); F1.1-T5 asserts the same through binding (TR-35, TR-63)
Property CLR types are `int`, `TimeSpan`, `TimeSpan`, `int`, `int`, `int`, `AnalysisProvider` in that order, matching the TR-63 configuration table (TR-63)
`grep -n 'System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations\|\[Range\|\[Required' AdventureTime.Application/Config/StationOptions.cs` prints nothing (TR-35)

tickets.title: Bind and validate StationOptions at the top of AddInfrastructure
tickets.context: The options class exists but nothing binds or checks it. AddInfrastructure is where every service is wired, so it is where configuration must be proven before anything depends on it.
tickets.motivation: A capacity of zero would refuse every announcement, an inverted TTL range would either expire sessions instantly or let them hold slots for a day, and a zero sweep interval would spin the sweeper. Each of those is cheap to catch at startup and expensive to diagnose from a stream of 429s.
tickets.goal: StationOptions bound from configuration and validated by five separate checks at startup, each with its own failure message naming the Station key it covers, so the host refuses to start on out-of-range values and reports exactly which ones are wrong.
tickets.value: Misconfiguration becomes a boot-time error with a clear cause rather than a runtime mystery. Operators and the seed script get immediate feedback, and the rest of the backlog can assume the options are sane.
tickets.description:
In /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs, as the first statement of `AddInfrastructure` (before `AddDbContext<AppDbContext>`), add a fluent `services.AddOptions<StationOptions>().Bind(configuration.GetSection(StationOptions.SectionName))` chain followed by five separate `.Validate(...)` calls, one per rule, each with its own failure message, then `.ValidateOnStart()`:

```csharp
services.AddOptions<StationOptions>().Bind(configuration.GetSection(StationOptions.SectionName))
    .Validate(options => options.Capacity >= 1,
        "Station:Capacity must be greater than or equal to 1")
    .Validate(options => options.TtlMin <= options.TtlDefault,
        "Station:TtlMin must be less than or equal to Station:TtlDefault")
    .Validate(options => options.TtlDefault <= options.TtlMax,
        "Station:TtlDefault must be less than or equal to Station:TtlMax")
    .Validate(options => options.SweepInterval > TimeSpan.Zero,
        "Station:SweepInterval must be greater than 0")
    .Validate(options => options.ProcessingTimeout >= TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1),
        "Station:ProcessingTimeout must be greater than or equal to 1 second")
    .ValidateOnStart();
```

Note the `TtlMin`/`TtlDefault` message reads "less than or equal to", matching the direction of its own condition (`TtlMin <= TtlDefault`) rather than the opposite relation — a message pointing the wrong way is worse than the generic combined message it replaces, since it tells whoever hits it to change the wrong thing.

Each `.Validate` call registers its own `IValidateOptions<StationOptions>`. When more than one condition fails, `ValidateOnStart` aggregates every failing check into one `OptionsValidationException` whose `Failures` collection lists all of them, not just the first — this is the actual benefit of chaining over one combined `&&` predicate: a config with two things wrong is diagnosed in one run instead of by trial and error.

Do not call `ValidateDataAnnotations()` (package not referenced, options carry no annotations). `.Bind` is provided by `Microsoft.Extensions.Options.ConfigurationExtensions` (already transitively resolved at 10.0.0 in AdventureTime.Infrastructure/obj/project.assets.json; `services.Configure<AnthropicConfig>(configuration.GetSection(...))` compiles today for the same reason) and `.ValidateOnStart()` by `Microsoft.Extensions.Options` 10.0.0; both extensions live in the `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection` namespace already imported by the file, and `using AdventureTime.Application.Config;` is already present, so no new usings are needed. This ticket adds ONLY this chain: the remaining registrations of TR-49 (`TryAddSingleton(TimeProvider.System)`, `IStationStore`, `IAnalysisQueue`, hosted-service order) are owned by F5.1, and the `if (configuration.GetValue<bool>("Claude"))` provider block is replaced by F1.2 (TR-50); leave both untouched here. `ValidateOnStart` registers an `IStartupValidator` that the host runs when it starts inside `app.Run()`, before the server listens, so an out-of-range `Station` value surfaces as an `OptionsValidationException` at startup rather than at first use; that is the required behavior (TR-63: `Capacity >= 1`, `SweepInterval > 0`, `TtlMin <= TtlDefault <= TtlMax`). Gotcha for verification: Program.cs still runs the Development `EnsureCreated` block (later `MigrateAsync`, TR-48) before `app.Run()`, so Postgres must be reachable for the startup failure to be attributable to options validation.
acceptance_criteria: `AddInfrastructure` in `AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` begins with `services.AddOptions<StationOptions>().Bind(configuration.GetSection(StationOptions.SectionName))` followed by five chained `.Validate(...)` calls and `.ValidateOnStart()`; each of the five conditions (`Capacity >= 1`, `TtlMin <= TtlDefault`, `TtlDefault <= TtlMax`, `SweepInterval > TimeSpan.Zero`, `ProcessingTimeout >= TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1)`) has its own distinct failure message naming the `Station:` key it checks, and the `TtlMin`/`TtlDefault` message reads "less than or equal to" (matching its condition's direction, not the reverse) (TR-35, TR-63)
`grep -n ValidateDataAnnotations AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` prints nothing, and `dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` succeeds with no NU1608 (TR-35)

With Postgres reachable (`docker compose up -d postgres`), `Station__Capacity=0 dotnet run --project AdventureTime` terminates during startup with an `OptionsValidationException` whose message contains `Station:Capacity must be greater than or equal to 1`, and never prints `Now listening on` (TR-63)

`Station__TtlDefault=30 dotnet run --project AdventureTime` (TtlDefault below the TtlMin default of 60) fails startup with a message containing `Station:TtlMin must be less than or equal to Station:TtlDefault`, and `Station__SweepInterval=00:00:00 dotnet run --project AdventureTime` fails with a message containing `Station:SweepInterval must be greater than 0` (TR-63)

With two conditions violated at once (`Station__Capacity=0 Station__SweepInterval=00:00:00 dotnet run --project AdventureTime`), the single `OptionsValidationException` thrown contains BOTH the Capacity message and the SweepInterval message — proving the chained validators aggregate every failure instead of stopping at the first (TR-63)

With no `Station__*` environment overrides (with or without the appsettings section of F1.1-T4, since the code defaults are valid), `dotnet run --project AdventureTime` starts and `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:5256/health` returns 200 (TR-35)

`git diff AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` shows only the inserted options-binding block (the `AddOptions`/`Bind`/five `Validate` calls/`ValidateOnStart` statement); the `if (configuration.GetValue<bool>("Claude"))` block and the `AddDbContext<AppDbContext>` registration are unchanged (TR-51)

tickets.title: Add Station section to appsettings.json and compose provider variable
tickets.context: appsettings still carries the old Claude boolean and compose passes only API keys through the environment. The Station section has to live somewhere a developer can see and change it.
tickets.motivation: Configuration that exists only as code defaults is invisible. Writing the section into appsettings at the same values documents the knobs without changing behavior, and exposing the provider through compose lets a developer switch to a real LLM without editing files.
tickets.goal: appsettings documents the seven Station values at their defaults with the obsolete key removed, and compose exposes a STATION_PROVIDER variable that defaults to the stub.
tickets.value: A fresh clone runs offline against the stub by default, the knobs are discoverable in the place developers already look, and switching providers is a one-variable change.
tickets.description: In /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime/appsettings.json remove the top-level `"Claude": false` key and add the section `"Station": { "Capacity": 3, "SweepInterval": "00:00:15", "ProcessingTimeout": "00:10:00", "TtlDefault": 1800, "TtlMin": 60, "TtlMax": 86400, "AnalysisProvider": "Stub" }` (TR-55); the values equal the code defaults of TR-35 so the file documents the knobs without changing behavior. Removing `Claude` is safe before F1.2 lands: `configuration.GetValue<bool>("Claude")` in AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs returns false for a missing key, which is the value the file carried (Gpt5 provider stays selected), and F1.2 deletes that read entirely under TR-50. In /Users/steven/AdventureTime/docker-compose.yml add `- Station__AnalysisProvider=${STATION_ANALYSIS_PROVIDER:-Stub}` to the `api` service `environment` list, next to the existing `Anthropic__ApiKey`/`OpenAi__ApiKey` lines; the double underscore is the .NET configuration section separator and the `:-Stub` default keeps a fresh `docker compose up` on the stub provider. `appsettings.Development.json` needs no change. Leave the unrelated working-tree edits alone (`Dockerfile`, `.idea/`, `AdventureTime/Program.cs`, and the untracked `AdventureTime/Episodes/s11*.json` files).
acceptance_criteria: `jq -c .Station AdventureTime/appsettings.json` prints exactly `{"Capacity":3,"SweepInterval":"00:00:15","ProcessingTimeout":"00:10:00","TtlDefault":1800,"TtlMin":60,"TtlMax":86400,"AnalysisProvider":"Stub"}` (key order as in TR-55) (TR-55)
`jq 'has("Claude")' AdventureTime/appsettings.json` prints `false`, and `jq '[.Anthropic.Model, .OpenAi.Model, .ConnectionStrings.DefaultConnection] | all(. != null)'` prints `true` (TR-55, TR-63)

`docker compose config` succeeds and its `api` service environment shows `Station__AnalysisProvider: Stub` when `STATION_ANALYSIS_PROVIDER` is unset, and `Station__AnalysisProvider: Claude` when run as `STATION_ANALYSIS_PROVIDER=Claude docker compose config` (TR-55)

With F1.1-T3 applied and Postgres reachable, `dotnet run --project AdventureTime` starts (no `OptionsValidationException`, `/health` returns 200), while `Station__Capacity=0 dotnet run --project AdventureTime` fails startup with `Station options out of range`, proving the `Station__*` environment variables override the file section under the TR-63 key names (TR-63)
`dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` still succeeds with no NU1608 (TR-51)

tickets.title: Add StationOptions binding and validation tests
tickets.context: These are the first tests in the new test project. They are pure dependency-injection tests: no database, no container, just a ServiceCollection and an in-memory configuration.
tickets.motivation: Option binding bugs are silent. A TimeSpan string that does not parse falls back to the default without complaint, and a typo in the validation predicate would let a bad value through. A handful of theory cases pin every branch.
tickets.goal: Tests proving the defaults, that each key binds from configuration, and that each out-of-range case is rejected at startup.
tickets.value: Configuration is under test like code, and the InternalsVisibleTo wiring from the first ticket is proven at the same time because these tests reach an internal type.
tickets.description: Add `AdventureTime.Tests/Config/StationOptionsTests.cs` to the xunit project created by F2.4-T1 (TR-67). These are pure DI tests, no database and no `PostgresFixture`: build a `ServiceCollection`, add an `IConfiguration` from `new ConfigurationBuilder().AddInMemoryCollection(...)` carrying `ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection` set to a syntactically valid but unused Npgsql string such as `Host=localhost;Database=unused;Username=u;Password=p` (`AddDbContext` does not connect at registration) plus the `Station:*` keys under test, call `services.AddInfrastructure(configuration, environment)` using the TR-50 signature with a minimal `IHostEnvironment` stub whose `EnvironmentName` is `Environments.Development` (F1.2 lands in WP1, before the WP2 test project this ticket needs, so that signature is in place; Development also guarantees the TR-50 fallback to Stub instead of an exception when `Station:AnalysisProvider=Claude` is bound with no API key), then resolve `IOptions<StationOptions>` from `BuildServiceProvider()`. Cover: (1) no `Station` keys, `.Value` equals every TR-35 default including `AnalysisProvider.Stub`; (2) keys `Station:Capacity=5`, `Station:SweepInterval=00:00:05`, `Station:ProcessingTimeout=00:00:30`, `Station:AnalysisProvider=Claude` bind to `5`, `TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)`, `TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30)`, `AnalysisProvider.Claude` (proves the TimeSpan-string and enum-string binding that appsettings and compose rely on); (3) a `[Theory]` over `Capacity=0`, `TtlDefault=30` (below TtlMin), `TtlMax=1000` with `TtlDefault=1800`, `SweepInterval=00:00:00`, `ProcessingTimeout=00:00:00`, where accessing `.Value` throws `OptionsValidationException` whose `Failures` contains `Station options out of range` (the `.Validate` predicate runs on every options creation, so `ValidateOnStart` is not needed to trigger it in-process). Finally prove the `InternalsVisibleTo` of F1.1-T1 (TR-51) without depending on any store type: assert that `typeof(AppDbContext).Assembly.GetCustomAttributes<System.Runtime.CompilerServices.InternalsVisibleToAttribute>()` contains one whose `AssemblyName` is `AdventureTime.Tests`.
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests --filter FullyQualifiedName~StationOptionsTests` passes with at least 8 test cases (defaults, binding, five out-of-range theory cases, InternalsVisibleTo attribute) (TR-35, TR-63)

`Defaults_MatchTr35` asserts Capacity 3, SweepInterval 00:00:15, ProcessingTimeout 00:10:00, TtlDefault 1800, TtlMin 60, TtlMax 86400, AnalysisProvider Stub on the value resolved through `IOptions<StationOptions>` with no `Station` keys in the in-memory configuration (TR-35)

`Binding_ParsesTimeSpanAndEnum` asserts `Station:Capacity=5` binds to 5, `Station:SweepInterval=00:00:05` to `TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)`, `Station:ProcessingTimeout=00:00:30` to `TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30)`, and `Station:AnalysisProvider=Claude` to `AnalysisProvider.Claude` (TR-63)

A `[Theory]` with the five invalid configurations (`Capacity=0`; `TtlDefault=30`; `TtlMax=1000` with `TtlDefault=1800`; `SweepInterval=00:00:00`; `ProcessingTimeout=00:00:00`) asserts `Assert.Throws<OptionsValidationException>(() => options.Value)` and that `ex.Failures` contains `Station options out of range` (TR-63)

`InternalsVisibleTo_TargetsTestProject` asserts an `InternalsVisibleToAttribute` with `AssemblyName == "AdventureTime.Tests"` on `typeof(AppDbContext).Assembly`, which exists only because of `<InternalsVisibleTo Include="AdventureTime.Tests" />` in `AdventureTime.Infrastructure.csproj` (TR-51)
`grep -n 'PostgresFixture\|Testcontainers\|\[Collection' AdventureTime.Tests/Config/StationOptionsTests.cs` prints nothing, and the filtered `dotnet test` run above passes with Docker stopped (TR-35)

review_notes: F1.1-T1 title was 87 characters (limit 80); shortened to 'Fix package baseline in Infrastructure and API project files'.
F1.1-T3 title was 81 characters; shortened to 'Bind and validate StationOptions at the top of AddInfrastructure'.
F1.1-T4 title was exactly 80 characters; shortened for safety.

F1.1-T1 criterion '`grep -c ... returns 0`' is ambiguous because grep exits 1 when the count is 0; reworded to 'prints 0'. The EnableRetryOnFailure grep now excludes bin/obj so stale build output cannot produce a false hit.
F1.1-T2 criterion 'verified by reading the initializers' was not independently verifiable; replaced with a grep for the exact initializer lines of TR-35.

F1.1-T3 stated `ValidateOnStart` fires inside `app.Run()`; verified that Microsoft.Extensions.Options 10.0.0 supplies `ValidateOnStart`/`IStartupValidator` and Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting invokes it at host start, so the claim stands, but the description now also explains why the startup criterion needs Postgres reachable (the pre-existing `EnsureCreated` block, later `MigrateAsync` per TR-48, runs before the host starts). Also confirmed via project.assets.json that `Microsoft.Extensions.Options.ConfigurationExtensions 10.0.0` is already transitively present, so `.Bind` compiles without a new package.
F1.1-T4 criterion used `jq .Station` and demanded an exact single-line output; jq pretty-prints by default, so the command is now `jq -c .Station`.

F1.1-T4 criterion 'Station__Capacity=5 dotnet run starts, showing environment variables override the file' proved nothing (capacity is not observable until F4.1's /api/station); replaced with `Station__Capacity=0` failing startup, which does prove the environment variable overrides the file's value of 3.
F1.1-T4 gotcha about unrelated working-tree edits listed only Dockerfile and .idea/; git status also shows a modified AdventureTime/Program.cs and 20 untracked Episodes/s11*.json files, now listed.

F1.1-T5 depended on F2.1-T1 solely to assert `StationSql.StationLockKey == 4207L` as proof of InternalsVisibleTo, and carried the confusing instruction 'guard with a #if-free direct reference and order this ticket after it'. Replaced with an assertion on the `InternalsVisibleToAttribute` of `typeof(AppDbContext).Assembly`, which proves TR-51 without anything from F2.1; the F2.1-T1 dependency is removed.

F1.1-T5 said to call `AddInfrastructure` 'with the signature current at the time', which is not deterministic. Pinned to the TR-50 signature `(configuration, environment)` with a Development `IHostEnvironment` stub, since the test project (F2.4-T1, WP2) is created after WP1 (which includes F1.2) in the TRD section 12 order; the Development fallback of TR-50 guarantees the Claude/OpenAi binding case cannot throw for a missing API key.
F1.1-T5 said the in-memory connection string may be 'any string'; changed to a syntactically valid Npgsql connection string so no parse exception can masquerade as a validation failure.
F1.1-T5 test count raised from 'at least 7' to 'at least 8' to include the InternalsVisibleTo attribute test.

Note kept, not changed: the feature header says 'Depends on features: (none)', but F1.1-T5 must depend on F2.4-T1 because TR-67 places the xunit project in F2.4. Build tickets T1-T4 remain dependency-free; only the test ticket carries the cross-feature dependency.

Requirement coverage verified: TR-35 (T2, T3, T5), TR-51 (T1, T3, T4, T5), TR-55 (T4), TR-63 (T2, T3, T4, T5); each appears in at least one named acceptance criterion. features.title: Analysis provider selection, stub service and continuity contract
features.summary: Introduce `ContinuityContext`/`PriorEpisodeSummary`/`RelationshipHarmony` in `Application/Models/Continuity/`, add the default interface method `AnalyzeEpisodeAsync(Episode, ContinuityContext, ct)` to `IDeepAnalysisService`, and build the deterministic `StubDeepAnalysisService` (seed `Season*100+EpisodeNumber`, `internal static StubDelay`, continuity note for the first prior). Replace the `Claude` bool in `AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` with `Station:AnalysisProvider` selection via the new `AddInfrastructure(services, configuration, IHostEnvironment)` signature, Development-only fallback to Stub with `AnalysisProviderSelection`, infinite HttpClient timeouts, the missing `CancellationToken` in `Gpt5DeepAnalysisService.CallGpt5Async`, and provider logging in `Program.cs` after `builder.Build()`. Testable by starting the app with each provider value and without API keys.

tickets.title: Add ContinuityContext records and IDeepAnalysisService continuity overload
tickets.context: IDeepAnalysisService has one episode-analysis method and two real implementations that build prompts from the full transcript. There is no way to pass prior-episode knowledge into an analysis.
tickets.motivation: Continuity notes are the one output that only a station can produce, because only the station knew the cast before the episode arrived. The analysis service needs a compact context built from quick-access fields, never the full JSON blobs, and the interface must grow without forcing changes on the Claude and GPT implementations or the stub. A default interface method does exactly that.
tickets.goal: Three positional records describing prior episodes and a default overload on the service that delegates to the existing method until an implementation chooses to override it.
tickets.value: Continuity becomes a first-class input to analysis without touching the providers, and the compact shape keeps prompts within model context so a non-load-bearing feature can never become a source of failed sessions.
tickets.description: Create AdventureTime.Application/Models/Continuity/ContinuityContext.cs (namespace AdventureTime.Application.Models.Continuity) holding three positional records exactly as TR-33: `record ContinuityContext(IReadOnlyList<PriorEpisodeSummary> Priors)`, `record PriorEpisodeSummary(int EpisodeId, int Season, int EpisodeNumber, string Title, string DominantEmotion, double PositivityScore, double IntensityScore, double ComplexityScore, IReadOnlyList<string> ThemeNames, IReadOnlyList<RelationshipHarmony> Relationships)` and `record RelationshipHarmony(string Character1, string Character2, double HarmonyScore)`. The context is deliberately compact (A17): it never carries the ThemesJson/RelationshipDynamicsJson blobs or the transcript; F2.3's LoadContinuityAsync will build it and F5.2's worker will pass it. Then extend AdventureTime.Application/Interfaces/IDeepAnalysisService.cs with the default interface method of TR-34: `Task<EpisodeAnalysis> AnalyzeEpisodeAsync(Episode episode, ContinuityContext context, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) => AnalyzeEpisodeAsync(episode, cancellationToken);` plus `using AdventureTime.Application.Models.Continuity;`. Do NOT edit AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Services/ClaudeDeepAnalysisService.cs or Gpt5DeepAnalysisService.cs: the default method exists precisely so both keep compiling unchanged; overriding them to use the context is out of scope (section 13).

tickets.title: Build deterministic StubDeepAnalysisService with StubDelay and continuity note
tickets.context: Both real providers call paid APIs and need keys. Nothing deterministic exists, so today every run of the analysis costs money and produces different output.
tickets.motivation: Seeding 21 episodes through announce and deliver, and running end-to-end tests, must not cost API calls or vary between runs. Deriving scores from season and episode number makes results identical across processes, which is what lets tests assert on them.
tickets.goal: A parameterless, deterministic IDeepAnalysisService that honors cancellation, produces a complete analysis, and emits one continuity note naming the first prior episode it was given.
tickets.value: Free, fast, reproducible local development and CI. The whole station can be exercised end-to-end with no credentials, and the continuity path has a predictable output to test against.
tickets.description: Create AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Services/StubDeepAnalysisService.cs implementing IDeepAnalysisService with a parameterless constructor and no HttpClient (it is registered as a singleton by F1.2-T4). Compute `int seed = episode.Season * 100 + episode.EpisodeNumber` (integer arithmetic; never string.GetHashCode, which is randomized per process) and populate a full AdventureTime.Application.Models.EpisodeAnalysis.EpisodeAnalysis: `Title = episode.Title`, `Sentiment.PositivityScore = (seed % 100) / 100.0`, `Sentiment.IntensityScore = ((seed / 7) % 100) / 100.0`, `Sentiment.ComplexityScore = ((seed / 13) % 100) / 100.0`, `Sentiment.DominantEmotion` taken from a fixed `static readonly string[]` of six entries by `seed % 6`; one CharacterMood per entry of episode.MajorCharacters (keyed by name in the CharacterMoods dictionary); one RelationshipDynamic for the first two members of the cast, where cast = MajorCharacters followed by MinorCharacters (none when fewer than two); two ThemeAnalysis entries; StoryArc.StoryBeats with exactly one StoryBeat; KeyMoments with exactly one EmotionalMoment. Gotcha: Episode.MajorCharacters, MinorCharacters and Locations are declared `List<string>?` in AdventureTime.Application/Models/Episode.cs, so treat null as empty (`?? []`). Before returning, `await Task.Delay(StubDelay, cancellationToken)` where `internal static TimeSpan StubDelay = TimeSpan.Zero` — tests reach it through the InternalsVisibleTo of TR-51 (F1.1) to hold a job in Working. Override the continuity overload from F1.2-T1: run the same computation, then set `ContinuityNotes` to `[$"follows S{p.Season:D2}E{p.EpisodeNumber:D2} '{p.Title}'"]` for `p = context.Priors[0]` or an empty list when there are no priors. AnalyzeSeasonTrendsAsync returns `new SeasonAnalysis()` and AnalyzeCharacterDynamicsAsync returns `new CharacterDynamicsAnalysis()`. Gotcha: Episode.Id is 0 at analysis time (the Episodes row is inserted only by Complete), so nothing may be seeded from it. The `EpisodeAnalysis.ContinuityNotes` property comes from TR-10, owned by F1.3; this ticket cannot compile until the F1.3 ticket that adds it has merged.
acceptance_criteria: StubDeepAnalysisService : IDeepAnalysisService compiles in AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Services/, has no constructor parameters and no HttpClient field or AddHttpClient registration (TR-47).

For an Episode with Season 11, EpisodeNumber 1 (seed 1101) the returned analysis has PositivityScore 0.01, IntensityScore 0.57, ComplexityScore 0.84 and DominantEmotion equal to the fourth entry (index 3) of the fixed six-entry list; S11E02 yields PositivityScore 0.02 (TR-47).

Two fresh instances given episodes with the same (Season, EpisodeNumber) but different Id values return structurally identical Sentiment scores, DominantEmotion, theme names and relationship pairs (TR-47).

For an episode with MajorCharacters [Finn, Jake] and MinorCharacters [BMO]: CharacterMoods has exactly the keys Finn and Jake; RelationshipDynamics has exactly one entry with Character1 == Finn and Character2 == Jake; Themes.Count == 2; StoryArc.StoryBeats.Count == 1; KeyMoments.Count == 1 (TR-47).
For an episode whose MajorCharacters and MinorCharacters are both null, AnalyzeEpisodeAsync returns without throwing, CharacterMoods is empty and RelationshipDynamics is empty (TR-47).

`StubDeepAnalysisService.StubDelay` is `internal static TimeSpan` defaulting to TimeSpan.Zero; with StubDelay set to 10 s and an already-cancelled CancellationToken, AnalyzeEpisodeAsync throws OperationCanceledException (TR-47).

The three-argument overload is overridden (not inherited from the default): with one prior (Season 11, EpisodeNumber 1, Title "The Unfinished Map") ContinuityNotes equals ["follows S11E01 'The Unfinished Map'"]; with an empty Priors list ContinuityNotes is an empty list (TR-34, TR-47).
AnalyzeSeasonTrendsAsync and AnalyzeCharacterDynamicsAsync return non-null empty objects without throwing (TR-47).

tickets.title: Set infinite HttpClient timeouts and pass CancellationToken in Gpt5 SendAsync
tickets.context: Both typed HttpClients are registered with a five-minute timeout, and the GPT service calls SendAsync without the cancellation token it was handed.
tickets.motivation: The station's processing deadline must be the only clock on an LLM call. With the current setup the HttpClient timeout fires first and surfaces as a cancellation the worker cannot attribute, and on the GPT path the deadline cancels nothing at all because the token never reaches the request.
tickets.goal: HttpClient timeouts set to infinite and the cancellation token passed through, so the worker's deadline is the one thing that can stop a call.
tickets.value: Timeout classification becomes truthful: a session that fails with 'processing timeout' really did exceed the configured deadline, and a hung provider call actually stops instead of holding a slot until the sweeper's backstop.
tickets.description: In AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs both `AddHttpClient<IDeepAnalysisService, ...>` lambdas currently set `client.Timeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5)`; change both to `client.Timeout = Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan`, keeping the `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` default header on the Claude client. In AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Services/Gpt5DeepAnalysisService.cs the private `CallGpt5Async(string prompt, CancellationToken cancellationToken)` calls `_httpClient.SendAsync(httpRequest)` (line 166) without the token — change it to `SendAsync(httpRequest, cancellationToken)`; its two `ReadAsStringAsync(cancellationToken)` calls (lines 171 and 178) already pass the token and stay as they are. `ClaudeDeepAnalysisService.CallClaudeAsync` already passes the token to SendAsync (line 418) and both ReadAsStringAsync calls — verify, do not change. Why: the worker's deadline CancellationTokenSource built from Station:ProcessingTimeout (F5.2, TR-44/TR-45) must be the only clock on the LLM call so that a cancellation is classified unambiguously as shutdown vs. timeout; a competing HttpClient timeout would surface as a TaskCanceledException the worker cannot attribute. Do not introduce any replacement HTTP-timeout configuration key: Station:ProcessingTimeout is the single value for this concept (TR-46). This ticket touches DependencyInjection.cs before F1.2-T4 rewrites the provider selection around these registrations.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -n "FromMinutes(5)" AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` returns nothing, and both AddHttpClient<IDeepAnalysisService, ...> lambdas contain `client.Timeout = Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` (TR-46).
The Claude typed-client lambda still adds the `anthropic-version` = `2023-06-01` default request header (TR-46).

`grep -n "SendAsync(" AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Services/Gpt5DeepAnalysisService.cs` shows exactly one call, `_httpClient.SendAsync(httpRequest, cancellationToken)`, and every ReadAsStringAsync call in that file passes `cancellationToken` (TR-46).
ClaudeDeepAnalysisService.cs has no diff in this ticket and its CallClaudeAsync passes `cancellationToken` to both SendAsync and ReadAsStringAsync (TR-46).
No new configuration key for an HTTP timeout exists in AdventureTime/appsettings.json or in AdventureTime.Application/Config/*; `dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` succeeds (TR-46).

tickets.title: Replace Claude bool with Station:AnalysisProvider selection in AddInfrastructure
tickets.context: Provider selection is a boolean branch in AddInfrastructure. With the stub in place there are three providers to choose from, and the choice has to be safe by default and loud when wrong.
tickets.motivation: Running against a real provider with an empty key fails on the first LLM call, after a slot has been claimed and a transcript accepted. Failing at startup instead, and defaulting to the stub in Development when no key is present, removes a whole class of confusing Failed sessions.
tickets.goal: Station:AnalysisProvider drives registration, the environment is injected so the Development fallback can be applied, and selecting a real provider without a key throws before the host starts.
tickets.value: The application never silently runs against a missing key, local runs are safe by default, and the selection is a recorded fact the next ticket can log.
tickets.description: Change the signature in AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs to `AddInfrastructure(this IServiceCollection services, IConfiguration configuration, IHostEnvironment environment)` (IHostEnvironment and the IsDevelopment() extension come from Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.Abstractions, added by F1.1 under TR-51) and update AdventureTime/Program.cs to call `builder.Services.AddInfrastructure(builder.Configuration, builder.Environment)`. Delete the `if (configuration.GetValue<bool>("Claude"))` branch and implement TR-50: (1) `var configured = configuration.GetValue<AnalysisProvider?>("Station:AnalysisProvider") ?? AnalysisProvider.Stub` (the enum is declared next to StationOptions in AdventureTime.Application/Config/StationOptions.cs, F1.1, TR-35); (2) read `configuration["Anthropic:ApiKey"]` / `configuration["OpenAi:ApiKey"]` for the configured provider — when null or whitespace, in `environment.IsDevelopment()` set `effective = Stub` and `fallbackReason = $"{configured} selected but no API key configured"`, otherwise throw `InvalidOperationException` with that exact text so startup fails; (3) register exactly one implementation for the effective provider: Stub -> `services.AddSingleton<IDeepAnalysisService, StubDeepAnalysisService>()`, Claude/OpenAi -> the existing typed-client registrations with the infinite timeouts from F1.2-T3; (4) create AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/AnalysisProviderSelection.cs with `public sealed record AnalysisProviderSelection(AnalysisProvider Configured, AnalysisProvider Effective, string? FallbackReason)` and register `services.AddSingleton(new AnalysisProviderSelection(configured, effective, fallbackReason))`. No ILogger may be resolved or used inside AddInfrastructure — logging is F1.2-T5's job in Program.cs. Leave AddDbContext (scoped, no retry strategy), the repositories and the Configure<AnthropicConfig>/Configure<OpenAiConfig> calls untouched. Note that an unrecognised provider string makes GetValue throw, which is acceptable (startup fails loudly). The removal of the `"Claude": false` key from appsettings.json is F1.1's TR-55; this ticket only stops reading it.
acceptance_criteria: AddInfrastructure has the signature `(this IServiceCollection services, IConfiguration configuration, IHostEnvironment environment)` and Program.cs calls it with `builder.Configuration, builder.Environment`; `grep -rn 'GetValue<bool>("Claude")' --include=*.cs .` returns nothing (TR-50).

With no Station:AnalysisProvider key configured, resolving IDeepAnalysisService from the built provider yields a StubDeepAnalysisService and the registered AnalysisProviderSelection is (Configured: Stub, Effective: Stub, FallbackReason: null) (TR-50).

With Station:AnalysisProvider=Claude, blank Anthropic:ApiKey and EnvironmentName Development, IDeepAnalysisService resolves to StubDeepAnalysisService and AnalysisProviderSelection is (Claude, Stub, "Claude selected but no API key configured"); the equivalent OpenAi case yields "OpenAi selected but no API key configured" (TR-50).

`ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production Station__AnalysisProvider=OpenAi dotnet run --project AdventureTime` with a blank OpenAi:ApiKey terminates at startup with InvalidOperationException whose message is "OpenAi selected but no API key configured" (TR-50).

With Station:AnalysisProvider=Claude and a non-blank Anthropic:ApiKey, IDeepAnalysisService resolves to ClaudeDeepAnalysisService and `IHttpClientFactory.CreateClient("IDeepAnalysisService").Timeout == Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan`; in every path `services.Count(d => d.ServiceType == typeof(IDeepAnalysisService)) == 1` on the ServiceCollection (TR-50, TR-46).

AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/AnalysisProviderSelection.cs declares `public sealed record AnalysisProviderSelection(AnalysisProvider Configured, AnalysisProvider Effective, string? FallbackReason)` and it is registered as a singleton instance; `grep -n "ILogger" AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` returns nothing (TR-50).

`dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` succeeds and, with the compose Postgres running (Program.cs still calls EnsureCreated in Development), `dotnet run --project AdventureTime` with default appsettings starts and serves GET /health with 200 (TR-50).

tickets.title: Log effective analysis provider and fallback in Program.cs after Build
tickets.context: Selection happens inside dependency injection where nothing observes it. An operator reading logs has no way to know which provider produced the analyses they are looking at.
tickets.motivation: When analysis output looks wrong, the first question is which provider ran. A single Information line at boot answers it, and a Warning when a fallback to the stub occurred explains a run that looks suspiciously fast and free.
tickets.goal: One log line naming the effective provider before the app listens, and one warning line when a fallback happened.
tickets.value: Diagnosability at almost no cost, and the epic's definition of done, a fresh boot that logs the stub provider, becomes something a reviewer can check.
tickets.description: In AdventureTime/Program.cs, immediately after `var app = builder.Build();` and before the Swagger/CORS pipeline configuration, resolve the selection registered by F1.2-T4: `var selection = app.Services.GetRequiredService<AnalysisProviderSelection>();` then `app.Logger.LogInformation("analysis provider: {Effective}", selection.Effective);` and, when `selection.FallbackReason is not null`, `app.Logger.LogWarning("analysis provider fallback: {FallbackReason}", selection.FallbackReason);`. Do not touch the EnsureCreated block or add MigrateAsync/rehydration — F1.3 (TR-13 step 4) and F5.3 (TR-48) own that region, which sits after MapHealthChecks. This is the ticket that makes the feature demonstrable: start the app with each provider value, with and without API keys, and read the log.
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet run --project AdventureTime` with default configuration (Development) logs an Information line `analysis provider: Stub` before the app starts listening and emits no fallback warning (TR-50).

`Station__AnalysisProvider=Claude dotnet run --project AdventureTime` with blank Anthropic:ApiKey logs `analysis provider: Stub` at Information and a Warning line containing `Claude selected but no API key configured` (TR-50).
`Station__AnalysisProvider=OpenAi OpenAi__ApiKey=dummy dotnet run --project AdventureTime` logs `analysis provider: OpenAi` and no warning (TR-50).

In Program.cs the AnalysisProviderSelection resolution and both log calls appear directly after `var app = builder.Build();` and before `app.UseSwagger`/`app.UseCors`; `grep -n "AnalysisProviderSelection" AdventureTime/Program.cs` shows resolution from `app.Services` (TR-50).
GET /health still returns 200 and, in Development, /swagger/v1/swagger.json still lists the existing api/Episodes routes (no regression; TR-50 changes nothing else in Program.cs).

tickets.title: Add provider selection and stub cancellation unit tests
tickets.context: Dependency-injection tests without a database, exercising AddInfrastructure with in-memory configuration.
tickets.motivation: Provider selection has three explicit branches, a Development fallback, and a throw path. The stub's cancellation behavior is equally important: if it ignored the token, the worker's deadline test would pass for the wrong reason.
tickets.goal: A test per selection branch, a test that the missing-key case throws, and a test that the stub honors cancellation.
tickets.value: Guards the boundary between configuration and the LLM path, preventing a regression that would either burn API calls unexpectedly or leave the worker unable to enforce its deadline.
tickets.description: Add AdventureTime.Tests/Infrastructure/AnalysisProviderSelectionTests.cs (the xunit project is created by F2.4 under TR-67) exercising AddInfrastructure without a database: build a `ServiceCollection`, call `services.AddLogging()` (ClaudeDeepAnalysisService and Gpt5DeepAnalysisService take `ILogger<T>` and `IOptions<AnthropicConfig>`/`IOptions<OpenAiConfig>`; the options are registered inside AddInfrastructure), an `IConfiguration` from `new ConfigurationBuilder().AddInMemoryCollection(...)` carrying a dummy `ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection` (AddDbContext does not connect at registration), and a small private `FakeHostEnvironment : IHostEnvironment` whose EnvironmentName is set per test (Development vs Production). Cases: no provider key -> selection (Stub, Stub, null) and IDeepAnalysisService resolves to StubDeepAnalysisService; Claude with blank Anthropic:ApiKey in Development -> (Claude, Stub, "Claude selected but no API key configured"); OpenAi with blank key in Production -> AddInfrastructure throws InvalidOperationException with the exact message; Claude with Anthropic:ApiKey=test-key in Production -> Effective Claude, IDeepAnalysisService resolves to ClaudeDeepAnalysisService and `IHttpClientFactory.CreateClient("IDeepAnalysisService").Timeout == Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan` (the typed-client name is the TClient type name). Add a StubDelay test: set `StubDeepAnalysisService.StubDelay = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)`, call AnalyzeEpisodeAsync with an already-cancelled token, assert OperationCanceledException, and restore StubDelay to zero in a finally block; because StubDelay is a process-wide static, mark the class `[Collection("StubDelay")]` and note in a comment that F3.1's Stub_Deterministic class must join the same named collection (xunit only serializes classes that share a collection). The full determinism and continuity-note assertions of TR-68 Stub_Deterministic remain F3.1's ticket; do not duplicate them here.
acceptance_criteria: AdventureTime.Tests/Infrastructure/AnalysisProviderSelectionTests.cs exists and `dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests --filter FullyQualifiedName~AnalysisProviderSelectionTests` passes without a Postgres container running (TR-50).
A test asserts that with no Station:AnalysisProvider key the registered AnalysisProviderSelection equals (Stub, Stub, null) and IDeepAnalysisService resolves to StubDeepAnalysisService (TR-50).

A test asserts that Station:AnalysisProvider=Claude with blank Anthropic:ApiKey and EnvironmentName "Development" yields (Claude, Stub, "Claude selected but no API key configured") and a StubDeepAnalysisService (TR-50).

A test asserts that Station:AnalysisProvider=OpenAi with blank OpenAi:ApiKey and EnvironmentName "Production" makes AddInfrastructure throw InvalidOperationException whose Message is "OpenAi selected but no API key configured" (TR-50).

`dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests` as a whole remains green after adding the file.

tickets.title: Repair stale migration snapshot and prove it with an empty SnapshotCheck

tickets.motivation: Generating the Sessions migration on top of a stale snapshot would fold unrelated model drift into it. The result would be a migration nobody can review with confidence, and possibly one that fails against the existing schema.
tickets.goal: A snapshot that matches the current model exactly, proven by generating a check migration whose Up and Down are empty, then discarding it.
tickets.value: The AddStation migration will contain precisely the eight intended operations and nothing else. Schema management becomes trustworthy from this point on, which every later data change depends on.
tickets.description: Before any model change, fix the two stale migration files so that EF's diff baseline matches the current entities (TRD TR-13 step 1, https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2dc9531c-3f0b-499f-8ec6-fb2cf3271341#TR-13). In /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Migrations/AppDbContextModelSnapshot.cs and /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Migrations/20250806235645_InitialCreate.Designer.cs replace the quoted CLR name "AdventureTime.Models.Episode" with "AdventureTime.Application.Models.Episode" (2 occurrences per file: the Entity(...) block and the `b.HasOne("AdventureTime.Models.Episode", "Episode")` line) and "AdventureTime.Application.Models.EpisodeAnalysisEntity" with "AdventureTime.Application.Entities.EpisodeAnalysis.EpisodeAnalysisEntity" (2 occurrences per file). tickets.title: Add SessionState enum and Session entity
tickets.context: No station types exist yet. The Session entity is the row that every conditional statement will key on, and SessionState is the vocabulary those statements filter by.
tickets.motivation: The state machine is the heart of the design. Six states, no more, in a fixed order, and a flat entity whose columns match the requirements table one for one are what let raw SQL and EF describe the same row without a mapping layer.
tickets.goal: The SessionState enum and a flat Session entity with no navigation properties, matching the column table exactly.
tickets.value: A single explicit shape for what a slot is. Keeping it flat, rather than an owned manifest type, is what makes the partial index and the conditional updates straightforward to write and to read.

tickets.motivation: A migration with exactly eight known operations is reviewable and reversible. Anything extra means drift crept in despite the snapshot repair, and it is far cheaper to notice that here than after the migration has been applied to a volume.
tickets.goal: The AddStation migration generated by the EF tooling, verified to contain the Sessions table, its three indexes, the Episodes column, index and foreign key, and the analysis column, and nothing else.

tickets.description: From the repo root run `dotnet ef migrations add AddStation --project AdventureTime.Infrastructure --startup-project AdventureTime` (TRD TR-13 step 3, https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2dc9531c-3f0b-499f-8ec6-fb2cf3271341#TR-13), producing /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Migrations/<timestamp>_AddStation.cs, its .Designer.cs and an updated AppDbContextModelSnapshot.cs. `Up()` MUST contain exactly eight operations and nothing else: CreateTable("Sessions"), CreateIndex IX_Sessions_Live_Season_Episode (unique, with the filter), CreateIndex IX_Sessions_State_ExpiresAt, CreateIndex IX_Sessions_State_WorkingDeadlineAt, AddColumn<Guid>("SessionId", "Episodes"), CreateIndex IX_Episodes_SessionId (unique), AddForeignKey with ReferentialAction.Restrict, and AddColumn<string>("ContinuityNotesJson", "EpisodeAnalyses"). epics.title: Station store: atomic admission and conditional transitions
epics.goal: On a real Postgres (Testcontainers), four concurrent announcements at capacity 3 admit exactly three, a delivery racing an expiry has exactly one winner, and Complete either moves Working to Done with the Episodes/EpisodeAnalyses inserts in one transaction or writes nothing.

features.title: IStationStore contract, StationSql and conditional transition statements
features.summary: Define `IStationStore`, `AnnounceOutcome`, `CompleteOutcome` and `StationView` in `Application/Interfaces/IStationStore.cs`, and create `Infrastructure/Station/StationSql.cs` (every raw statement as interpolated `FormattableString`, `StationLockKey = 4207`, `now()` in every clock predicate) and `StationRows.cs` (`LiveRow`, `RetryAfterRow`). Implement the single-autocommit transition methods of `StationStore` — set-based and id-scoped `ExpireOverdue`, `FailOverdueWorking`, `FailInterrupted`, `TryBeginWork`, `Cancel`, `Fail` — each bound to the mandated execution mechanism (`ExecuteSqlAsync` vs `Sessions.FromSql(...RETURNING *)`), with `rows == 1` semantics, no retry on 0 rows, and the `Session {SessionId} {FromState} -> {ToState} ({Reason}); rows={Rows}` log line. This feature realizes the state machine of TR-3/TR-4 and the row-lock resolution of the remaining races of TR-58 (the worker-side rows of that table are exercised in F5.2).

tickets.title: Define IStationStore, AnnounceOutcome, CompleteOutcome and StationView contracts
tickets.context: The Application layer has repository interfaces for episodes and analyses, each of which saves on its own. Nothing exists for sessions, and the station needs a very different kind of interface: conditional operations that report whether they won.
tickets.motivation: The store is the only writer of the Sessions table and the seam that handlers, hosted services and tests all depend on. Defining announce outcomes as a closed set of records forces every caller to handle admitted, live conflict, episode exists and full explicitly, and lets handlers be written against a fake before a line of SQL exists.
tickets.goal: The complete store contract with its outcome types compiling in the Application project.
tickets.value: Parallel work becomes possible: the Application epic can proceed against a fake store while the SQL is built, and the mapping from outcomes to HTTP status codes becomes mechanical rather than interpretive.

tickets.title: Create StationSql with every raw statement as FormattableString and StationRows
tickets.context: No raw SQL exists anywhere in the solution today. The station's conditional statements are the mechanisms themselves, and they need one home.
tickets.motivation: Each race in the design is resolved by a WHERE clause. Keeping every statement in one static class, with the database clock in every time predicate and a fixed advisory lock key, makes them reviewable against the requirements line by line and makes it trivial to grep for the one thing that must never appear, an application-clock timestamp in a predicate.
tickets.goal: Fourteen parameterized statements as FormattableStrings, plus the two row types the announce path reads back.
tickets.value: Every race resolution is visible in one file. A reviewer can lay the requirements document next to it and check each statement, and no caller can accidentally build a subtly different predicate inline.
tickets.description: Create /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationSql.cs as `internal static class StationSql` with `internal const long StationLockKey = 4207;` and one member per statement of the TR-36 SQL block, 14 in total: the six transition statements (ExpireOverdue set-based and id-scoped, FailOverdueWorking, FailInterrupted, TryBeginWork, Cancel), Complete step 1, Fail, the four announce SELECTs (live check, episode check, live count, Retry-After), the announce INSERT ... RETURNING * and the GetAsync projection; the advisory-lock `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock({StationSql.StationLockKey})` of TR-37 is written inline by F2.2 and is not a member. Parameterless statements are `static FormattableString` properties; parameterized ones are static methods (e.g. `TryBeginWork(Guid id, string payloadJson, string flagsJson, double deadlineSecs)`, `ExpireOverdueById(Guid id)`, `Fail(Guid id, string reason)`) whose body is a `$"..."` literal returned as `FormattableString`, so EF turns every `{x}` hole into an Npgsql parameter. Copy the SQL text of TR-36 verbatim, including `now()` in every clock predicate, `CAST(@p AS jsonb)` for every jsonb write, `make_interval(secs => @deadlineSecs)` with a `double` argument, the `AS "Value"` alias on the two scalar SELECTs and `NULL::jsonb AS "DeliveryPayload"` in GetAsync. Add a `/// mechanism:` comment on each member naming the one execution mechanism it is bound to (`ExecuteSqlAsync`, `Sessions.FromSql` or `SqlQuery<T>`) per the TR-36 table. Create StationRows.cs in the same folder with `internal sealed class LiveRow { public Guid Id { get; set; } public string State { get; set; } = ""; }` and `internal sealed class RetryAfterRow { public DateTime? EarliestExpiry { get; set; } public int RetryAfter { get; set; } }`; property names must equal the column aliases because `SqlQuery<T>` composes `SELECT s."Value" FROM (<sql>) AS s`. tickets.title: Implement StationStore single-autocommit transitions and register the store
tickets.context: The contract and the SQL exist; there is no implementation. This ticket builds the six single-statement transitions: expire overdue, fail overdue working, fail interrupted, begin work, cancel and fail.
tickets.motivation: Each transition is one conditional UPDATE keyed on the from-state, executed as an autocommit statement. Returning whether exactly one row changed, and never retrying on zero, is the session state machine made concrete: a slot is released by the state change itself, and losing a race is a normal, reportable outcome rather than an exception.
tickets.goal: A StationStore that implements the six transitions with rows-equals-one semantics, logs every transition with its reason, and is registered scoped.
tickets.value: Callers get a store-level guarantee that a zero-row result means someone else got there first. That single guarantee is what the delivery handler, the worker and the sweeper all build their correctness on.
tickets.description: Create /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationStore.cs as `public sealed class StationStore : IStationStore` with constructor `(AppDbContext context, IOptions<StationOptions> options, ILogger<StationStore> logger)` (TR-37); read `options.Value` once in the constructor (A4) and precompute `_deadlineSecs = ProcessingTimeout.TotalSeconds + 30` as a `double`. Implement the six single-autocommit methods of TR-39 with no `BeginTransactionAsync`: `ExpireOverdueAsync(null)`, `FailOverdueWorkingAsync` and `FailInterruptedAsync` run `_context.Sessions.FromSql(StationSql.X).AsNoTracking().ToListAsync(ct)` with no other LINQ operator (composition would wrap the data-modifying statement in a subquery Postgres rejects), return `rows.Count` and log one line per returned row; `ExpireOverdueAsync(id)`, `TryBeginWorkAsync`, `CancelAsync` and `FailAsync` run `_context.Database.ExecuteSqlAsync(StationSql.X(...), ct)` and return `rows == 1` (the `int`-returning id-scoped ExpireOverdue returns the raw count). tickets.title: Integration-test transitions, terminal invariants and store-side races
tickets.context: The first tests of the store against a real Postgres, seeding rows by direct SQL so each transition is exercised in isolation from admission, which is not built yet.
tickets.motivation: Conditional predicates only prove themselves against real row locking and a real clock. These tests pin that every terminal transition nulls the staged payload and stamps EndedAt in the same statement, and that a second write to the same row hits zero rows.
tickets.goal: Integration tests for each of the six transitions and the invariants they hold.
tickets.value: The state machine's correctness becomes executable. A later refactor of the SQL cannot silently weaken a guard without a test turning red.

features.title: Atomic admission under the advisory lock
features.summary: Implement `StationStore.AnnounceAsync` as one READ COMMITTED transaction: `pg_advisory_xact_lock(4207)`, set-based ExpireOverdue, live check (`SqlQuery<LiveRow>`), Episodes check (`SqlQuery<int>`), live count (`SqlQuery<int>`, the only occupancy computation), Retry-After row, then `INSERT ... RETURNING *` via `Sessions.FromSql`. Refusals COMMIT so step-2 expirations persist; a `23505` on the insert rolls back and re-reads to `LiveConflict`. No `IsolationLevel` argument anywhere and `EnableRetryOnFailure` left off; documents and honors the lock ordering (advisory lock, then Sessions row locks, then Episodes). Testable by concurrent `AnnounceAsync` calls on independent contexts.

tickets.title: Implement AnnounceAsync as one advisory-locked READ COMMITTED transaction
tickets.context: Transitions exist; admission does not. This is the ticket that implements slot admission, the first and most important of the five mechanisms.
tickets.motivation: The advisory lock serializes count-then-insert so that racers for the last slot cannot both win, and running the expiry statement first under that lock makes a full station mean genuinely full, with a Retry-After that is always positive. Every other guarantee in the system assumes this one.
tickets.goal: One READ COMMITTED transaction executing the six statements in the required order and returning one of the four outcomes.
tickets.value: Bounded concurrency and backpressure exist for the first time. A sender learns the station is full before it ships a transcript, and there is never more than the configured number of episodes in flight, not because anything throttles them but because a slot is the only door in.
tickets.description: Implement `AnnounceAsync(Session candidate, int capacity, CancellationToken ct)` on `StationStore` in `/Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationStore.cs` (the class skeleton, `StationSql` and the `LiveRow`/`RetryAfterRow` classes in `StationRows.cs` come from F2.1). Open `await using var tx = await _context.Database.BeginTransactionAsync(ct)` with NO isolation argument (TR-37, TR-59) and execute in order: (1) `ExecuteSqlAsync($"SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock({StationSql.StationLockKey})")` (the interpolated `long` becomes a bigint parameter, which is fine); (2) set-based ExpireOverdue through `Sessions.FromSql(...).AsNoTracking().ToListAsync()`, logging each returned row with the TR-39 template; (3) live check via `Database.SqlQuery<LiveRow>(...).FirstOrDefaultAsync()`, hit means COMMIT and return `LiveConflict(row.Id, Enum.Parse<SessionState>(row.State))`; (4) Episodes check via `SqlQuery<int>(...).FirstOrDefaultAsync()` where 0 means none, hit means COMMIT and `EpisodeExists(id)`; (5) live count via `SqlQuery<int>(...).SingleAsync()` -- the ONLY place occupancy is computed (TR-2) -- and when `count >= capacity` run the Retry-After `SqlQuery<RetryAfterRow>(...).SingleAsync()`, COMMIT and return `Full(count, row.EarliestExpiry, row.RetryAfter)`; (6) the INSERT ... RETURNING * through `Sessions.FromSql(...)`, COMMIT, return `Admitted(inserted.Id, inserted.ExpiresAt, count + 1)`. Gotcha: TR-37 spells step 6 as `.SingleAsync()`, but any operator beyond `AsNoTracking()` makes EF wrap the statement in a subquery with `LIMIT`, which Postgres rejects for INSERT/UPDATE, and TR-36 forbids it; so materialize steps 2 and 6 with `.AsNoTracking().ToListAsync()` and take the single element in memory (the scalar `SqlQuery<T>` SELECTs compose fine because their columns are aliased `AS "Value"`). Serialize `ExpectedCharacters`/`ExpectedLocations`/`RequestedStages` with `JsonSerializer.Serialize(list)` and default options (exactly what `ListToJsonConverter<string>` in `/Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Data/AppDbContext.cs` reads back) and pass them through `CAST(@p AS jsonb)`; never assign `DateTime.UtcNow` to any Session timestamp -- `AnnouncedAt`/`ExpiresAt` come from `now()` in SQL and are read back from RETURNING (TR-12). Refusals (steps 3-5) MUST COMMIT so the step-2 expirations persist and 'full' is true for observers; any exception leaves the transaction uncommitted so `await using` disposal rolls it back (the 23505 branch is F2.2-T2). Log refusals at Information with season/episode, occupancy and retry-after, and the admission with the TR-39 template `Session {SessionId} (new) -> Waiting (announced); rows=1`.
acceptance_criteria: `AnnounceAsync` opens exactly one transaction with `BeginTransactionAsync(ct)` and no `IsolationLevel` argument, and its first statement is `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(4207)` (`StationSql.StationLockKey`), verified by reading the method and by Npgsql command logging in `Admission_RunsReadCommitted_NoRetryStrategy` (F2.2-T4) (TR-37, TR-59)

Steps 2-6 run in the TRD order and each is bound to its TR-36 mechanism: steps 2 and 6 use `Sessions.FromSql(...).AsNoTracking().ToListAsync()` with no other LINQ operator; steps 3-5 use `Database.SqlQuery<LiveRow>` / `SqlQuery<int>` / `SqlQuery<RetryAfterRow>`; no `SqlQuery<T>` is used over an INSERT/UPDATE (TR-36, TR-37)

Against an empty `Sessions` table and Capacity 3, `AnnounceAsync` for S11E01 returns `Admitted` with `Occupancy == 1`, a row exists with `State='Waiting'`, `AnnouncedAt` and `ExpiresAt` set by SQL (`ExpiresAt - AnnouncedAt` equals `TtlSeconds` seconds), `ExpectedCharacters`/`ExpectedLocations`/`RequestedStages` readable through EF as the original lists, and `inserted.ExpiresAt.Kind == DateTimeKind.Utc` -- verified by `Admission_AdmittedRow_TimestampsFromSql` (F2.2-T4) (TR-2, TR-12, TR-37)

With 3 live rows and Capacity 3, `AnnounceAsync` returns `Full(3, earliestExpiry, retryAfter)` where `retryAfter >= 1`; with only Working rows live (no Waiting) `EarliestExpiry == null` and `RetryAfterSeconds == 30`; occupancy in every outcome equals `SELECT count(*)::int FROM "Sessions" WHERE "State" IN ('Waiting','Working')` (TR-2, TR-37)

Given a Waiting row for S11E06, a second announce returns `LiveConflict` naming that row's id and state `Waiting`; given an `Episodes` row for S11E05 (and no live session), announce returns `EpisodeExists(episodeId)`; neither refusal inserts a row -- verified by `Admission_Refusals_LiveConflictAndEpisodeExists` (F2.2-T4) (TR-37)

tickets.title: Map a 23505 on the announce INSERT to LiveConflict after rollback and re-read
tickets.context: Under the advisory lock, admission checks for a live session before inserting, so a duplicate normally never reaches the database. The partial unique index exists for the path that bypasses the lock.
tickets.motivation: If a future code path, a manual SQL insert or a replayed transaction ever skips the lock, the index fires with a unique violation. Left unmapped that surfaces as a 500; mapping only that specific constraint to a live-conflict outcome keeps the client-facing contract intact, a 409 naming the manifest that holds the slot.
tickets.goal: A catch filter matching exactly that constraint, a rollback, a re-read of the conflicting session, and a LiveConflict outcome.
tickets.value: Defense in depth with a clean outcome. The database backstop and the application contract agree even when the primary mechanism is bypassed.
tickets.description: Add the lock-bypass fallback of TR-37 / TR-61 / section 9.4 to `AnnounceAsync` in `/Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationStore.cs`. Wrap only step 6 (the INSERT ... RETURNING *) in `catch (PostgresException ex) when (ex.SqlState == PostgresErrorCodes.UniqueViolation && ex.ConstraintName == "IX_Sessions_Live_Season_Episode")` (`Npgsql.PostgresErrorCodes.UniqueViolation == "23505"`); the exception is a `PostgresException` thrown by the `FromSql` materialization, not a `DbUpdateException`, because no `SaveChangesAsync` is involved. In the handler call `await tx.RollbackAsync(CancellationToken.None)`, log a Warning that the advisory lock was bypassed for the (Season, EpisodeNumber), and record that the insert conflicted; then let the `await using` scope end (or `await tx.DisposeAsync()` explicitly) so that `_context.Database.CurrentTransaction == null`, and only then re-run the live-check `SqlQuery<LiveRow>` for the same (Season, EpisodeNumber) as an autocommit statement, returning `LiveConflict(row.Id, Enum.Parse<SessionState>(row.State))`. This can only happen when another writer inserted a live row for the same episode without taking `pg_advisory_xact_lock(4207)` (section 9.4: the second INSERT waits on the first's uncommitted row on the partial unique index and fails with 23505 once it commits); a re-read that finds no live row (the winner went terminal in between) rethrows the original exception (chosen here). Any other exception, on any step, propagates after the `await using` disposal rolls the transaction back; nothing is retried (TR-3, TR-59). Keep the lock order intact: the fallback re-read takes no locks and never re-enters the advisory lock (TR-60).
acceptance_criteria: The catch filter matches `SqlState == "23505"` AND `ConstraintName == "IX_Sessions_Live_Season_Episode"` only; a 23505 with any other constraint name and every non-23505 exception propagate to the caller with the transaction rolled back (code review) (TR-37, TR-61)

Scenario section 9.4, implemented as `Admission_LockBypassed_MapsUniqueViolationToLiveConflict` (F2.2-T4): on a second `AppDbContext` open a transaction and insert a Waiting row for S11E08 directly (no advisory lock) without committing; call `AnnounceAsync` for S11E08 on the store; commit the direct transaction 500 ms later; the store returns `LiveConflict` whose `ManifestId` equals the directly inserted row's id and whose `State == SessionState.Waiting`, and `SELECT count(*) FROM "Sessions" WHERE "Season"=11 AND "EpisodeNumber"=8` is 1 (TR-37)

After the 23505 path `context.Database.CurrentTransaction == null`, a subsequent `AnnounceAsync` for another episode on the same context returns `Admitted`, and `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_locks WHERE locktype='advisory' AND objid=4207` is 0 once the call returns (TR-37, TR-60)

The re-read of the live row runs outside the transaction: it is issued after `tx` is rolled back and disposed, verified by reading the code and by the Npgsql command log ordering `ROLLBACK` before the `SELECT "Id","State" ...` statement (TR-37)
A Warning log line naming season and episode number is emitted on the 23505 path, captured through an `ILogger<StationStore>` test double in F2.2-T4 (TR-37)
`dotnet build /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.sln` succeeds with no new warnings

tickets.title: Guard READ COMMITTED, keep retry-on-failure off and document the lock ordering
tickets.context: The lock-then-count pattern is correct only at READ COMMITTED and only without an execution strategy that retries transactions. Both are currently the defaults, which is precisely why they are easy to change by accident.
tickets.motivation: A future developer who reads the word race and reaches for a stricter isolation level, or who enables retry-on-failure to handle a flaky connection, would silently break admission: a stale snapshot admits one too many, and a retry replays the enqueue. The assumption has to be written down where it will be seen, and asserted where it will be run.
tickets.goal: A comment at the registration explaining why retry-on-failure is absent, confirmation that no transaction passes an isolation level, and the lock ordering documented in code.
tickets.value: The single most subtle correctness assumption in the system is recorded in the two places a change would have to touch. The admission test in the next ticket then asserts it.
tickets.description: Enforce TR-59 and document TR-60 in code. In `/Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` keep the `UseNpgsql(...)` lambda free of `EnableRetryOnFailure` and add a short comment above `AddDbContext<AppDbContext>` stating why: an execution strategy would re-run the advisory-locked announce block and the post-commit enqueue side effect (TR-59). Confirm no call to `BeginTransactionAsync` in the solution passes an `IsolationLevel` (today there are none; `AnnounceAsync` from F2.2-T1 and `CompleteAsync` from F2.3 must stay that way), and do not use the identifier `IsolationLevel` in the new comments either, so the grep below stays empty. Add a `<remarks>` XML doc on the `StationStore` class in `/Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationStore.cs` and on `StationSql.StationLockKey` in `/Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationSql.cs` spelling out the lock ordering of TR-60: (1) advisory station lock 4207, (2) `"Sessions"` row locks, (3) `"Episodes"`/`"EpisodeAnalyses"` row locks; Announce takes (1) then (2) and reads `"Episodes"` without locking; delivery, cancel, sweeper and Fail take only (2); Complete takes (2) then (3) and never (1); no transaction may take (1) after (2); the advisory lock is transaction-scoped and released on commit or rollback; a `40P01` means this section was violated. This comment is the contract F2.3 (Complete) and F5.1 (sweeper) build against, so reviewers of those features can check them against it.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn --include='*.cs' --exclude-dir=bin --exclude-dir=obj EnableRetryOnFailure /Users/steven/AdventureTime` matches only the explanatory comment in `DependencyInjection.cs`, never a call (TR-59)
`grep -rn --include='*.cs' --exclude-dir=bin --exclude-dir=obj IsolationLevel /Users/steven/AdventureTime` returns nothing (TR-59)
With the configured `AppDbContext` options, `context.Database.CreateExecutionStrategy().RetriesOnFailure == false`, asserted by `Admission_RunsReadCommitted_NoRetryStrategy` in F2.2-T4 (TR-59)

`StationStore` and `StationSql.StationLockKey` carry XML `<remarks>` listing the three lock levels, which store methods take which levels, that Complete never takes (1), that the advisory lock is transaction-scoped, and that a `40P01` indicates a violation (TR-60)

`AnnounceAsync` acquires the advisory lock as its first statement and touches `"Sessions"` rows only afterwards; it issues no `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` and no write against `"Episodes"` (code review of F2.2-T1 against the remarks) (TR-60)
`dotnet build /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.sln` succeeds

tickets.title: Add concurrent admission integration tests for AnnounceAsync
tickets.context: Real Postgres via the Testcontainers fixture, with independent connections per concurrent caller so the lock is actually contended.
tickets.motivation: Four concurrent announcements at capacity three admitting exactly three is the canonical proof of the admission mechanism. The isolation-level assertion catches the misconfiguration the previous ticket warns about, and the refusal tests prove both 409 causes and the Retry-After computation.
tickets.goal: Concurrent admission, live-conflict, episode-exists and full-with-Retry-After scenarios passing, with the transaction isolation asserted.
tickets.value: The capacity invariant is demonstrated rather than argued. This is the test to run first whenever anything near the store changes.
tickets.description: Add `/Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Tests/Station/StationStoreAdmissionTests.cs` using the `PostgresFixture` collection fixture from F2.4-T1 (Testcontainers `postgres:15-alpine`, `MigrateAsync`, `DbContextOptions<AppDbContext>` factory, `TRUNCATE "EpisodeAnalyses", "Episodes", "Sessions" RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE;` before each test). Each test builds a real `StationStore` per call over an independent `AppDbContext` (constructor `(AppDbContext, IOptions<StationOptions>, ILogger<StationStore>)`: use `Options.Create(new StationOptions())` and a `NullLogger<StationStore>` or a capturing logger double), because the advisory lock and `now()` only behave on real Postgres (A31). Cover: (1) the section 9.2 race -- 4 `AnnounceAsync` calls for S11E01..S11E04 with Capacity 3 launched with `Task.WhenAll` on 4 contexts, repeated 10 times with the TRUNCATE between iterations to shake out ordering luck; (2) isolation and retry policy -- inside a transaction opened the way the store opens it, `SELECT current_setting('transaction_isolation') AS "Value"` through `SqlQuery<string>` and `CreateExecutionStrategy().RetriesOnFailure`; (3) refusals commit step-2 expirations; (4) the section 9.4 bypass path from F2.2-T2; (5) `LiveConflict` and `EpisodeExists` refusals; (6) SQL-set timestamps on the admitted row.
