`Admission_RunsReadCommitted_NoRetryStrategy`: inside `await using var tx = await context.Database.BeginTransactionAsync()` (no isolation argument) `SELECT current_setting('transaction_isolation') AS "Value"` returns `read committed`, and `context.Database.CreateExecutionStrategy().RetriesOnFailure` is false (TR-59, TR-69)

`Admission_Refusal_CommitsExpirations`: Capacity 1, one Working row for S11E02 and one Waiting row for S11E03 with `ExpiresAt` set to `now() - interval '1 second'`; `AnnounceAsync` for S11E04 returns `Full(1, null, 30)`; from a fresh context the S11E03 row is `TimedOut`, `Reason='ttl elapsed'`, `EndedAt IS NOT NULL`, `DeliveryPayload IS NULL` (TR-37)

F2.2-T1 description was ~14 sentences (convention: 3-8); condensed while keeping every TRD gotcha (FromSql/no-operator rule, jsonb CAST, no DateTime.UtcNow, refusals commit).

features.title: Complete transaction, continuity load and read projections
features.summary: Implement `CompleteAsync` (conditional Done UPDATE with `rows == 1`, then `Episodes` + `EpisodeAnalyses` inserted through the `entity.Episode` navigation in the same transaction, `ChangeTracker.Clear()` on any failure, `23505 IX_Episode_Season_Number` mapped to `FailAsync(id, "episode exists")` → `EpisodeExists`), plus the read side: `GetAsync` via the `NULL::jsonb AS "DeliveryPayload"` projection, `GetForProcessingAsync`, `GetWorkingIdsAsync`, `FindEpisodeIdBySessionAsync`, `GetStationViewAsync` (live by AnnouncedAt, 20 most recent terminal), and `LoadContinuityAsync` (join, cast intersection, last 10, theme names and harmony triples only). Codifies the Postgres error mapping table so every SqlState has a defined owner. Testable with direct store calls on the container.

tickets.title: Implement GetAsync projection and the id-keyed read methods
tickets.context: Handlers and the worker need to read sessions, but for different purposes: handlers build responses and must never see the staged transcript, while the worker needs the payload exactly once.
tickets.motivation: Reads that track entities are dangerous next to raw conditional updates: a later SaveChanges on a stale tracked Session could silently revert a Working transition and reopen a slot. Reading without tracking, and projecting the payload as null for everyone but the worker, removes that hazard and keeps API responses small.
tickets.goal: GetAsync without the payload, GetForProcessingAsync with it, the working-ids scan the worker uses to adopt orphans, and the episode lookup by session.
tickets.value: API responses never carry transcripts, the worker gets exactly what it needs, and no accidental save can undo a state transition.
tickets.description: Add `GetAsync`, `GetForProcessingAsync`, `GetWorkingIdsAsync` and `FindEpisodeIdBySessionAsync` to `StationStore` in /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationStore.cs (class created by F2.1; contract in /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Application/Interfaces/IStationStore.cs, TR-32). `GetAsync` MUST send the `GetAsync` statement of TR-36 (every column listed explicitly, `NULL::jsonb AS "DeliveryPayload"`, `WHERE "Id"=@id`) as `_context.Sessions.FromSql(StationSql.GetAsync(id)).AsNoTracking().FirstOrDefaultAsync(ct)`, so the payload column is never transferred (TR-40); the statement lives in /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationSql.cs as a `FormattableString` factory (add it if F2.1 did not). `GetForProcessingAsync` is `_context.Sessions.AsNoTracking().FirstOrDefaultAsync(s => s.Id == id, ct)` and does include `DeliveryPayload` (the worker's read, TR-44 step 2). `GetWorkingIdsAsync` selects the ids of rows with `State == SessionState.Working` (LINQ over the `HasConversion<string>()` column translates to `"State" = 'Working'`); `FindEpisodeIdBySessionAsync` selects `Episode.Id` where `Episode.SessionId == id` (column added by F1.3, TR-9) or null, used by `GetManifestQueryHandler` for the TR-17 links. All four use `AsNoTracking()`; the store MUST NOT keep tracked `Session` entities or write `Sessions` through them (TR-40). Gotcha: `FirstOrDefaultAsync` composes a `LIMIT 1` subquery around the `FromSql`, which is fine for this SELECT (TR-36 forbids composition only for data-modifying statements); do not append `Where`, `OrderBy` or `Select` to the `FromSql`.

tickets.title: Implement LoadContinuityAsync (cast intersection, last 10, blob extraction)

Pre-existing rows with `SessionId NULL` are included; because `AppDbContext` maps `EpisodeAnalysisEntity.HasOne(e => e.Episode).WithMany()`, an episode may have several analyses, so keep one row per episode, the one with the highest `EpisodeAnalysisEntity.Id` (chosen here). In memory, keep rows whose cast (`MajorCharacters ∪ MinorCharacters`, both nullable `List<string>` on `Episode`) intersects `expectedCharacters` under `StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase` on trimmed values, take the LAST 10 in (Season, EpisodeNumber) order, and extract only `ThemeAnalysis.Theme` from `ThemesJson` and `(Character1, Character2, HarmonyScore)` from `RelationshipDynamicsJson`. The blobs were written by `EpisodeAnalysisEntity.FromDomainModel` with a private camelCase `JsonSerializerOptions`, so deserialize `List<ThemeAnalysis>` / `List<RelationshipDynamic>` (from /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Application/Models/EpisodeAnalysis/SubModels/) with `PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true`. tickets.title: Add PostgresErrors helper codifying the TR-61 SqlState mapping table
tickets.context: The requirements carry a table of Postgres error codes and what each means to the station. Today those codes would be string literals scattered through catch filters.
tickets.motivation: Unique violations arrive wrapped in DbUpdateException from EF but raw from ExecuteSql; connection failures share a prefix; a deadlock code should never appear. One helper that unwraps and names them keeps every catch filter honest and identical.
tickets.goal: A PostgresErrors class with the named codes, an unwrap helper and the predicates the store uses.
tickets.value: The error map is code, so Complete and Announce classify failures the same way and a reviewer can check the table against one file.
tickets.description: Create /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/PostgresErrors.cs: `internal static class PostgresErrors` with constants `UniqueViolation = "23505"`, `ForeignKeyViolation = "23503"`, `DeadlockDetected = "40P01"`, `SerializationFailure = "40001"`, `LockNotAvailable = "55P03"`, `QueryCanceled = "57014"`, `AdminShutdown = "57P01"`, `static bool IsConnectionError(string sqlState)` (`08` prefix), `static PostgresException? Unwrap(Exception ex)` (returns the exception itself when it is a `PostgresException`, otherwise walks the `InnerException` chain of a `DbUpdateException` or any other exception) and `static bool IsUniqueViolation(Exception ex, string constraintName)` (true iff `Unwrap(ex)?.SqlState == "23505"` and `ConstraintName == constraintName`, ordinal). Constraint-name constants for the station code go here too: `IX_Sessions_Live_Season_Episode`, `IX_Episode_Season_Number`, `IX_Episodes_SessionId`, `FK_Episodes_Sessions_SessionId` (spellings from /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Data/AppDbContext.cs and TR-8/TR-9). The class-level XML doc MUST reproduce the TR-61 table row by row and name the owning code path for each: announce step 6 (`AnnounceAsync`, F2.2) → `LiveConflict`; Complete step 2 `IX_Episode_Season_Number` → `EpisodeExists`; `IX_Episodes_SessionId` and `FK_Episodes_Sessions_SessionId` → cannot occur under I7, propagate to the worker (`Fail 'analysis error: DbUpdateException'`); 40P01/40001 → not expected (TR-59/TR-60), handler 500 / worker `Fail 'analysis error: PostgresException'`; 55P03/57014/08xxx/57P01 → handler 500, sweeper logged and next tick, worker `Fail` once then logged; 0 rows → re-read, not an error (TR-3). This is the single place a reviewer checks that every SqlState has an owner; `CompleteAsync` (F2.3-T5) consumes it and `AnnounceAsync` (F2.2, TR-37) MAY be switched to it in a follow-up. Internals are visible to `AdventureTime.Tests` through `InternalsVisibleTo` (F1.1, TR-51); Npgsql is already referenced by the Infrastructure project.
acceptance_criteria: `PostgresErrors.IsUniqueViolation(new DbUpdateException("x", new PostgresException("m", "ERROR", "ERROR", "23505", constraintName: "IX_Episode_Season_Number")), "IX_Episode_Season_Number")` returns true; the same with constraint `IX_Episodes_SessionId`, or with SqlState `23503`, returns false (TR-61)
`PostgresErrors.Unwrap` returns the inner `PostgresException` from a `DbUpdateException`, the same instance from a bare `PostgresException`, and null for an `InvalidOperationException` (TR-61)

The XML doc on `PostgresErrors` lists all seven TR-61 rows (23505 for each of the three constraints, 23503, 40P01/40001, 55P03/57014/08xxx/57P01, 0 rows) with the mapping and the owning method for each (TR-61)

After F2.3-T5 lands, the `CompleteAsync` path in StationStore.cs contains no `"23505"` or `"IX_Episode_Season_Number"` string literal and calls `PostgresErrors.IsUniqueViolation(ex, PostgresErrors.IX_Episode_Season_Number)` (code review; TR-61)
`dotnet build /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.sln` succeeds with no new warnings (TR-51 internals visible)

tickets.title: Implement CompleteAsync transaction, LostSlot and EpisodeExists mapping
tickets.context: The Done transition plus the Episode and analysis writes. This is the last statement of the happy path and the one that must never leave a half-written result.
tickets.motivation: Updating the session to Done first, and inserting the episode and analysis only when that update changed exactly one row, guarantees that no Episodes row can ever exist for a session that lost its slot to a timeout or a restart. A unique violation on the episode index is turned into a Failed session with a reason rather than an orphaned insert.
tickets.goal: One method, one transaction, with Completed, LostSlot and EpisodeExists outcomes and nothing inserted on any path but Completed.
tickets.value: The Episodes table only ever holds fully analyzed, station-admitted episodes. Failures are recorded on the session where the operator will look, and a wasted LLM call can never become a corrupted record.
tickets.description: Implement `IStationStore.CompleteAsync(Guid id, Episode episode, EpisodeAnalysis analysis, CancellationToken ct)` in /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationStore.cs as one method and one transaction opened with `await using var tx = await _context.Database.BeginTransactionAsync(ct)` and no `IsolationLevel` argument (TR-38, TR-59). Step 1: `rows = await _context.Database.ExecuteSqlAsync(<Complete step 1>, ct)` using the TR-36 statement `UPDATE "Sessions" SET "State"='Done', "EndedAt"=now(), "DeliveryPayload"=NULL WHERE "Id"=@id AND "State"='Working'` from F2.1's `StationSql` (use the factory name F2.1 chose, e.g. `StationSql.Complete(id)`); `rows != 1` → ROLLBACK, log Warning `lost slot` (TR-64), return `CompleteOutcome.LostSlot`, insert nothing and never call `FailAsync` (TR-4 note). Step 2: `episode.SessionId = id; var entity = EpisodeAnalysisEntity.FromDomainModel(analysis, source: _options.AnalysisProvider.ToString(), version: "station-v1"); entity.Episode = episode; _context.Episodes.Add(episode); _context.EpisodeAnalyses.Add(entity); await _context.SaveChangesAsync(ct);` — the FK on /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Application/Entities/EpisodeAnalysis/EpisodeAnalysisEntity.cs is fixed up from the `Episode` navigation (`analysis.EpisodeId` is 0 and unused), and `EpisodeRepository.CreateAsync` / `EpisodeAnalysisRepository.SaveAsync` MUST NOT be composed because each calls `SaveChangesAsync` on its own. Step 3: COMMIT, log the TR-39 line `Session {SessionId} Working -> Done (completed); rows=1`, return `Completed`. On ANY exception after the `Add` calls the store MUST call `_context.ChangeTracker.Clear()` before returning, rethrowing or calling `FailAsync`; when `PostgresErrors.IsUniqueViolation(ex, PostgresErrors.IX_Episode_Season_Number)` (F2.3-T4) → ROLLBACK (the row is Working again), clear the tracker, then `await FailAsync(id, "episode exists", ct)` and return `EpisodeExists`; any other exception → ROLLBACK, clear the tracker, rethrow (TR-38, TR-61). Gotchas: `FailAsync` must run after `tx.RollbackAsync()` (EF clears `Database.CurrentTransaction` on rollback, so the Fail statement autocommits as TR-39 requires; simplest is to leave the transaction's using-block first); `episode.Id` must be 0 so the identity generates; `episode.AirDate`/`CreatedAt` must be `Kind == Utc` (TR-12) — the payload deserialized from `"...Z"` already is, do not touch it; per §9.5, because step 1 precedes the insert in the same transaction, an announce for the same episode sees either the Working row or the `"Episodes"` row, never neither.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Working row, `CompleteAsync` returns `Completed`; `SELECT "State","EndedAt","DeliveryPayload" FROM "Sessions" WHERE "Id"=@id` shows `Done`, non-null, NULL; exactly one `"Episodes"` row has `"SessionId" = id` and exactly one `"EpisodeAnalyses"` row has `"EpisodeId"` equal to that episode's `"Id"`, `"AnalysisSource"` = the configured `AnalysisProvider` name (e.g. `Stub`) and `"AnalysisVersion"` = `station-v1` (TR-38)
Calling `CompleteAsync` a second time for the same id returns `LostSlot`, logs a Warning containing `lost slot`, and the `"Episodes"`/`"EpisodeAnalyses"` counts are unchanged (TR-38, TR-64)

Given a row already Failed (after `FailAsync(id, "working deadline exceeded")`), `CompleteAsync` returns `LostSlot`, both tables stay empty and the row keeps `Reason = 'working deadline exceeded'` (TR-38; TR-61 0-rows row)

Given `"Episodes"` already holds (11, 3) and a Working session for (11, 3), `CompleteAsync` returns `EpisodeExists`, the session is `Failed` with `Reason = 'episode exists'`, `"EndedAt" IS NOT NULL` and `"DeliveryPayload" IS NULL`, there is still exactly one `"Episodes"` row for (11, 3), and a subsequent `SaveChangesAsync` on the same `AppDbContext` inserts nothing (`ChangeTracker.Entries().Count() == 0`) (TR-38, TR-61)

Given a Working session whose payload `Title` is 201 characters (violates `character varying(200)`), `CompleteAsync` throws `DbUpdateException` whose unwrapped `PostgresException.SqlState` is `22001`, the session is still `Working` with its payload intact (rolled back), `ChangeTracker.Entries().Count() == 0`, and a following `FailAsync(id, "analysis error: DbUpdateException")` on the same context returns true (TR-38; TR-61 propagate rows)
`grep -n 'BeginTransactionAsync' StationStore.cs` shows no `IsolationLevel` argument; `grep -n 'EpisodeRepository\|EpisodeAnalysisRepository' StationStore.cs` returns nothing (TR-38, TR-59)
The `LostSlot` branch contains no call to `FailAsync` (code review; TR-4 note under the transition table, TR-44 step 6)
With Information logging captured, the happy path emits exactly one `Session {SessionId} Working -> Done (completed); rows=1` line (TR-39 template)

tickets.title: Add store read, continuity, station view and PostgresErrors tests
tickets.context: Coverage of the F2.3 behaviors that the numbered test scenarios do not name: projections, the continuity window, the station view ordering and the error helper.
tickets.motivation: These are the places where subtle mistakes hide: a case-sensitive cast comparison that misses 'finn', a last-ten window that takes the first ten, a station view that orders by the wrong column. None would fail loudly; all would quietly degrade the product.
tickets.goal: Named tests for each of those behaviors on real Postgres, plus unit tests for the error helper.
tickets.value: The read side is as trustworthy as the write side, so what the API and the worker see is known to match what the database holds.
tickets.description: Add `StationStoreReadTests` and `PostgresErrorsTests` to the `AdventureTime.Tests` project created in F2.4 (uses the `PostgresFixture` collection fixture and the `TRUNCATE "EpisodeAnalyses", "Episodes", "Sessions" RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE;` reset of TR-67). Do NOT duplicate the TR-69 scenarios (c), (h), (i), (j) — those are written under F2.4; this ticket covers the F2.3 behavior TR-69 does not name: `LoadContinuityAsync` (predicate, inner join, cast intersection, last-10 window, `SessionId NULL` rows, blob extraction, wrong-shape blob tolerance, multiple analyses per episode), `GetStationViewAsync` (ordering, the 20-row cap, occupancy from the TR-2 count statement, no payload/flags columns, empty table), `GetWorkingIdsAsync`, `FindEpisodeIdBySessionAsync`, the non-23505 failure path of `CompleteAsync` (rollback, tracker cleared, exception propagates), and unit tests for `PostgresErrors` built with `new PostgresException(...)` wrapped in `DbUpdateException` (internals visible via TR-51). Seed rows directly through `AppDbContext` or raw SQL on the container; for the ordering tests set `"AnnouncedAt"`/`"EndedAt"` with `UPDATE ... SET ... = now() - interval '<n> minutes'` statements rather than assigning `DateTime.UtcNow` in code (TR-12). Gotcha: `ThemesJson`/`RelationshipDynamicsJson` are NOT NULL jsonb, so the 'malformed' seed must be valid JSON of the wrong shape (`'{}'`, `'"oops"'`), never `'[oops'` or an empty string. Capture EF command text with `LogTo` on the `DbContextOptionsBuilder` or a test `ILoggerProvider` on `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command` at Information to assert which columns each SELECT names.
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet test --filter FullyQualifiedName~StationStoreReadTests` passes on the Testcontainers Postgres and has a named test for every acceptance criterion of F2.3-T1, F2.3-T2 and F2.3-T3 except the GetAsync/GetForProcessingAsync projection pair, which is TR-69 (j) under F2.4 (TR-40)

A test seeds 12 prior episodes with analyses (one with `"SessionId" NULL`, one with two analysis rows, one with `ThemesJson = '{}'`) and asserts exactly 10 priors, ascending (Season, EpisodeNumber) order, theme names and `(Character1, Character2, HarmonyScore)` triples equal to the seed, the higher-`Id` analysis used for the duplicated episode, and an empty `ThemeNames` for the wrong-shape row (TR-40)

A test with 3 live and 25 terminal rows (timestamps spread via SQL `now() - interval`) asserts `Live` ordered by `AnnouncedAt`, `Recent.Count == 20` ordered by `EndedAt` desc, `Occupancy == 3`, and that the captured row SELECTs name neither `"DeliveryPayload"` nor `"Flags"` (TR-40)

A test drives `CompleteAsync` with a 201-character title, asserts `DbUpdateException` propagates with SqlState `22001`, the session is still Working with its payload, `ChangeTracker.Entries()` is empty and a following `FailAsync` on the same context returns true (TR-38, TR-61)

`dotnet test --filter FullyQualifiedName~PostgresErrorsTests` passes: `IsUniqueViolation` true only for SqlState 23505 with the exact constraint name, `Unwrap` handles `DbUpdateException`, bare `PostgresException` and unrelated exceptions (TR-61)
No test in this ticket assigns or asserts `DateTime.UtcNow` against a `Sessions` timestamp; all clock setup is SQL `now()` arithmetic (TR-12)

review_notes: F2.3-T1 title was 104 characters (limit 80); shortened.

F2.3-T1 criterion 'grep Sessions.FromSql shows the GetAsync call chained only with AsNoTracking' was not verifiable as written: F2.1's ExpireOverdue/FailOverdueWorking/FailInterrupted/announce statements also use Sessions.FromSql, so the grep returns several lines. Scoped the criterion to the GetAsync call.

F2.3-T1 gotcha claimed FirstOrDefaultAsync does not compose; it does (EF wraps the statement in a subquery with LIMIT 1), which is harmless for a SELECT. TR-36 forbids composition only because it breaks data-modifying statements; reworded so the developer does not add Where/OrderBy/Select but is not misled about the mechanism.

F2.3-T1/T2/T3/T6 said 'EF command logging at Debug'; EF emits executed command text under Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command at Information. Reworded the capture instruction (LogTo or a test ILoggerProvider at Information).
F2.3-T2 said 'neither of the two SELECTs' but the method sends three statements (live rows, recent rows, TR-2 count); reworded to the two row-projection SELECTs.
F2.3-T2 seeded distinct AnnouncedAt/EndedAt values without saying how; TR-12 forbids assigning DateTime.UtcNow to Session timestamps, so the criteria now require SQL now() - interval arithmetic.
F2.3-T3 title was 89 characters; shortened.

F2.3-T3 and F2.3-T6 required tolerating a ThemesJson of '[oops' or empty string. Both columns are NOT NULL jsonb (AppDbContext.HasColumnType("jsonb"), non-nullable string on EpisodeAnalysisEntity), and Postgres rejects non-JSON text for jsonb, so that row cannot be seeded. Replaced with valid-jsonb-but-wrong-shape blobs ('{}', '"oops"', '[1,2]') and kept null/empty tolerance as defensive code only.
F2.3-T3 did not state that the Episodes-EpisodeAnalyses join is an inner join (episodes without an analysis are not priors); added, since TR-40 says 'joined with'.

F2.3-T4 criterion 'grep "23505" shows the literal only in PostgresErrors.cs' contradicted its own description, which lets AnnounceAsync (F2.2, TR-37) keep its literal and only MAY adopt the helper. Scoped the criterion to CompleteAsync/StationStore's Complete path.
F2.3-T5 title was 85 characters; shortened.
F2.3-T5 named a StationSql.Complete(id) factory that F2.1 defines; made explicit that the name follows F2.1's StationSql and that only the statement text is binding (TR-36 'Complete step 1').

F2.3-T5 said FailAsync runs 'OUTSIDE the transaction' while the transaction is held by 'await using var tx'; added the gotcha that FailAsync must run after RollbackAsync/disposal (EF clears Database.CurrentTransaction on rollback) so the Fail statement autocommits as TR-39 requires.
F2.3-T6 title was 82 characters; shortened.

F2.3-T6 criterion 1 required a named test for every criterion of F2.3-T1, including the GetAsync/GetForProcessingAsync projection, while its description forbade duplicating TR-69 (j), which is that exact scenario and belongs to F2.4. Excluded the TR-69 (c)(h)(i)(j) scenarios explicitly.

Cross-feature dependency keys (F1.1-T1, F1.2-T1, F2.1-T1..T3, F2.4-T1) reference features that exist in the feature list; the ticket numbers inside those features could not be verified from this review's inputs and are kept as the first/lowest plausible tickets (contract, StationSql, conditional statements; ContinuityContext; InternalsVisibleTo; PostgresFixture). The orchestrator should reconcile them against the actual F1.1/F1.2/F2.1/F2.4 ticket lists.
Descriptions of T3 and T5 exceeded the 3-8 sentence convention; tightened while keeping every TRD gotcha.

tickets.title: Build PostgresFixture collection fixture with MigrateAsync and TRUNCATE reset
tickets.context: The race tests need real row locking, advisory locks and partial indexes, none of which an in-memory or SQLite provider reproduces.
tickets.motivation: A fixture that starts a real postgres:15-alpine container once per test class, applies the migrations, and truncates between tests gives every scenario the same engine that production uses, with isolation cheap enough to run dozens of iterations.
tickets.goal: A PostgresFixture exposing options, a context factory and a reset, with migrations applied at startup.
tickets.value: Every concurrency claim is tested against the engine that enforces it. This is what makes the phrase 'exactly one winner' a test result instead of a belief.
tickets.description: Add `AdventureTime.Tests/Fixtures/PostgresFixture.cs` implementing xunit 2.x `IAsyncLifetime` (Task-based): `InitializeAsync` builds and starts `new PostgreSqlBuilder().WithImage("postgres:15-alpine").Build()`, then constructs `DbContextOptions<AppDbContext>` via `new DbContextOptionsBuilder<AppDbContext>().UseNpgsql(container.GetConnectionString(), o => o.MigrationsAssembly(typeof(AppDbContext).Assembly.FullName)).Options` (mirroring `AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs`) with NO `EnableRetryOnFailure` (TR-59; scenario (a) asserts `RetriesOnFailure == false` against these options), and runs `Database.MigrateAsync()` once so the `AddStation` migration of F1.3 creates `Sessions`, `Episodes.SessionId` and `EpisodeAnalyses.ContinuityNotesJson` (TR-67). Expose `DbContextOptions<AppDbContext> Options`, `AppDbContext CreateContext()` (a fresh instance per call, so concurrent scenarios get independent connections) and `Task ResetAsync()` which executes exactly `TRUNCATE "EpisodeAnalyses", "Episodes", "Sessions" RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE;` (truncating `Sessions` alone is refused because `FK_Episodes_Sessions_SessionId` references it). Keep a `public static int StartCount` incremented in `InitializeAsync` so the once-per-collection lifetime is assertable. `DisposeAsync` disposes the container. Add `AdventureTime.Tests/Fixtures/PostgresCollection.cs` with `[CollectionDefinition(PostgresCollection.Name)] public sealed class PostgresCollection : ICollectionFixture<PostgresFixture>` and an abstract `AdventureTime.Tests/Fixtures/DatabaseTestBase.cs` (`[Collection(PostgresCollection.Name)]`, `IAsyncLifetime`) whose `InitializeAsync` calls `fixture.ResetAsync()` so every test starts from empty tables. Replace the placeholder of F2.4-T1 with `PostgresFixtureTests` (extends `DatabaseTestBase`). Requires a running Docker daemon; document that in the fixture's XML comment.
acceptance_criteria: `PostgresFixture` starts `postgres:15-alpine` through `Testcontainers.PostgreSql`, calls `Database.MigrateAsync()` once in `InitializeAsync`, and exposes `Options`, `CreateContext()` and `ResetAsync()` (TR-67)

`ResetAsync()` executes the single statement `TRUNCATE "EpisodeAnalyses", "Episodes", "Sessions" RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE;` and `DatabaseTestBase.InitializeAsync` invokes it before every test: `PostgresFixtureTests.Reset_Leaves_Empty_Tables_A` and `..._B` each insert one `Sessions` row via SQL and then assert `SELECT count(*) FROM "Sessions"` is 1, and both pass in the same run (TR-67)

The fixture's `UseNpgsql` call configures no `EnableRetryOnFailure`: `PostgresFixtureTests.NoRetryStrategy` asserts `CreateContext().Database.CreateExecutionStrategy().RetriesOnFailure == false` (precondition of TR-69(a); TR-59 is owned by F2.2)

`PostgresFixtureTests.Migration_Creates_Live_Index` passes: `SELECT indexdef FROM pg_indexes WHERE indexname = 'IX_Sessions_Live_Season_Episode'` returns one row whose text contains both `UNIQUE` and `WHERE`, and `SELECT count(*) FROM "__EFMigrationsHistory" WHERE "MigrationId" LIKE '%AddStation'` returns 1 (TR-67)

tickets.title: Add StationStore test helpers: store factory, row seeding SQL and sample data
