tickets.goal: A base class with a store factory and row seeding, plus sample payloads, episodes and analyses.
tickets.value: Scenario tests stay short and legible, and the same sample data is used everywhere so results are comparable.
tickets.description: Add `AdventureTime.Tests/Station/StoreTestBase.cs` (extends `DatabaseTestBase`) and `AdventureTime.Tests/Station/StationTestData.cs`, both in namespace `AdventureTime.Tests.Station` (F2.4-T7 filters on it), so the TR-69 scenarios read as the TRD describes them. `StoreTestBase.CreateStore(AppDbContext ctx, int capacity = 3)` returns `new StationStore(ctx, Options.Create(new StationOptions { Capacity = capacity, ProcessingTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10) }), NullLogger<StationStore>.Instance)` using the real `AdventureTime.Infrastructure.Station.StationStore` constructor of TR-37 (`AnalysisProvider` stays at its default `Stub`, which scenario (h) relies on). `StationTestData.WaitingCandidate(int season, int episode, int ttlSeconds = 600)` builds a `Session` with `Id = Guid.CreateVersion7()`, `State = Waiting`, `Title = $"S{season}E{episode}"`, `ExpectedCharacters = ["Finn","Jake"]`, `ExpectedLocations = []`, `RequestedStages` = the six stage names of TR-16, `TtlSeconds = ttlSeconds` and never assigns any timestamp (respects TR-12). Seeding goes through direct SQL, not the store, so scenarios can construct states the store would refuse: `Task<Guid> InsertWaitingAsync(ctx, season, episode)` runs the announce INSERT shape of TR-36 with a fresh `Guid.CreateVersion7()`, `now()` and `make_interval`; `SetWorkingAsync(ctx, id, payloadJson)` runs `UPDATE "Sessions" SET "State"='Working', "DeliveredAt"=now(), "WorkingDeadlineAt"=now() + interval '10 minutes', "DeliveryPayload"=CAST({payloadJson} AS jsonb), "Flags"='[]'::jsonb WHERE "Id"={id}`; `SetExpiresAtAsync(ctx, id, TimeSpan offset)` runs `UPDATE "Sessions" SET "ExpiresAt" = now() + {offset} WHERE "Id"={id}` (Npgsql binds `TimeSpan` as `interval`; a string interval would be sent as a text parameter and fail). `SampleEpisode(season, episode)` returns an `Episode` with `Title = $"S{season}E{episode}"`, `AirDate = DateTime.SpecifyKind(new DateTime(2026,9,14), DateTimeKind.Utc)`, `CreatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow`, a non-empty `TranscriptText`, `MajorCharacters = ["Finn","Jake"]`; `SamplePayloadJson(season, episode)` serializes it with the test-local `StationTestData.Json = new JsonSerializerOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web)` (camelCase, the shape of TR-7; `StationJson.Options` belongs to F3.1 and is not referenced here). `SampleAnalysis()` returns an `EpisodeAnalysis` with a populated `Sentiment` (`DominantEmotion`, three scores). `ReadRowAsync(ctx, id)` is `ctx.Sessions.AsNoTracking().SingleAsync(s => s.Id == id)` and `LiveCountAsync(ctx)` runs the TR-2 statement through `Database.SqlQuery<int>` with the column aliased `AS "Value"`. Add `AdventureTime.Tests/Station/StoreTestBaseTests.cs` with the helper self-tests and an `InternalsVisibleTo` proof that reads `StationSql.StationLockKey`.
acceptance_criteria: `StoreTestBase.CreateStore` compiles against the real `StationStore(AppDbContext, IOptions<StationOptions>, ILogger<StationStore>)` constructor and returns an `IStationStore` (consumer of TR-37; TR-69 harness)
`StoreTestBaseTests.InternalsVisibleTo_Exposes_StationLockKey` asserts the internal `StationSql.StationLockKey == 4207`, proving `InternalsVisibleTo("AdventureTime.Tests")` is effective (TR-67)

`StoreTestBaseTests.Helpers_Seed_Waiting_And_Working`: `InsertWaitingAsync` followed by `ReadRowAsync` yields `State == Waiting`, `ExpiresAt > AnnouncedAt`, `DeliveryPayload == null`; `SetWorkingAsync` on that row yields `State == Working`, `DeliveredAt != null`, `WorkingDeadlineAt != null`, `DeliveryPayload != null`; `SetExpiresAtAsync(id, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(-1))` yields `ExpiresAt < DateTime.UtcNow` (TR-69 harness)

`SampleEpisode(...).AirDate.Kind == DateTimeKind.Utc` and `CreatedAt.Kind == DateTimeKind.Utc`, and inserting it through `ctx.Episodes.Add` + `SaveChangesAsync` succeeds on the container (respects TR-12)

`LiveCountAsync` returns 0 on an empty table and 1 after `InsertWaitingAsync`, using `SELECT count(*)::int AS "Value" FROM "Sessions" WHERE "State" IN ('Waiting','Working')` (TR-2 statement as used by TR-69)
`grep -n 'UtcNow' AdventureTime.Tests/Station/StationTestData.cs` matches only the `Episode.CreatedAt` assignment; no helper assigns `DateTime.UtcNow` to any `Session` property (respects TR-12)
`grep -rn 'StationJson' AdventureTime.Tests/` returns nothing (no dependency on F3.1), and all files under `AdventureTime.Tests/Station/` declare `namespace AdventureTime.Tests.Station`

tickets.title: Write TR-69 (b) delivery-vs-expiry race and (d) rehydration store tests
tickets.context: Scenarios for the expiry sweeper and rehydration, mechanisms three and five.
tickets.motivation: The delivery-versus-expiry race with exactly one winner is the design's central concurrency claim, and it can only be observed by running the two statements concurrently on two connections, many times. Rehydration has a simpler but equally important property: it fails Working rows and leaves Waiting rows alone.
tickets.goal: Twenty iterations of the race with never both and never neither winning, and a rehydration test proving the Working-only rule.
tickets.value: The two behaviors that are hardest to reason about from code are demonstrated empirically.
tickets.description: Add `AdventureTime.Tests/Station/TransitionTests.cs` (extends `StoreTestBase`) covering the conditional statements of F2.1 and the invariants I4, I5, I6, I8, I9 of TR-57. Scenario (b), §9.3: per iteration `InsertWaitingAsync(11, n)` with a distinct `EpisodeNumber` (a reused pair would violate the partial unique index once an earlier iteration's row is Working), `SetExpiresAtAsync(id, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(-1))`, then start `TryBeginWorkAsync(id, SamplePayloadJson(11, n), "[]", ct)` on one `AppDbContext`/store and `ExpireOverdueAsync(null, ct)` on a second, independent context, and await both with `Task.WhenAll` (start both tasks before awaiting either so they genuinely overlap); assert `TryBeginWork == false`, `ExpireOverdue == 1`, the row is `TimedOut` with `Reason == "ttl elapsed"` and `DeliveryPayload == null`. Exactly 1 holds without truncating between iterations because earlier iterations' rows are already TimedOut, so the set-based statement matches only the row under test. Variant with `SetExpiresAtAsync(id, TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1))`: `TryBeginWork == true`, `ExpireOverdue == 0` (earlier rows are Working, not Waiting), row `Working`, `DeliveryPayload != null`, `WorkingDeadlineAt != null`. Each variant repeats 20 iterations. Scenario (d): seed one Working row (`InsertWaitingAsync` + `SetWorkingAsync` with a payload) and one Waiting row, capture the Waiting row with `ReadRowAsync`, call `FailInterruptedAsync(ct)`, assert it returns 1, the Working row is `Failed` with `Reason == "interrupted by restart"`, `EndedAt != null`, `DeliveryPayload == null`, and the Waiting row's `State`, `ExpiresAt`, `EndedAt` and `Reason` equal the captured values. Tag tests with `[Trait("Invariant", "I8")]` etc. (I4, I5, I6, I8, I9 must all appear in this file) for the traceability check of F2.4-T7. Assertions read rows with `ReadRowAsync` (`AsNoTracking`) on a separate context, never through the store's context (TR-40).
acceptance_criteria: `TransitionTests.DeliveryVsExpiry_Expired_ExactlyOneWinner` runs 20 iterations, each with `TryBeginWorkAsync` and `ExpireOverdueAsync(null)` started concurrently on two independent `AppDbContext` instances; every iteration asserts `TryBeginWork == false`, `ExpireOverdue == 1`, `State == TimedOut`, `Reason == "ttl elapsed"`, `DeliveryPayload == null` (TR-69(b); I6, I8 of TR-57)

`TransitionTests.DeliveryVsExpiry_Live_ExactlyOneWinner` runs 20 iterations with `ExpiresAt = now() + 1 minute` and asserts `TryBeginWork == true`, `ExpireOverdue == 0`, `State == Working`, `DeliveryPayload != null` and `WorkingDeadlineAt != null` (TR-69(b); I6 of TR-57)

`TransitionTests.FailInterrupted_FailsWorkingOnly` asserts `FailInterruptedAsync` returns 1, the Working row is `Failed` with `Reason == "interrupted by restart"`, `EndedAt != null`, `DeliveryPayload == null`, and the Waiting row's `State`, `ExpiresAt`, `EndedAt`, `Reason` equal the values captured before the call (TR-69(d); I6, I9 of TR-57)
In the same test a second `FailInterruptedAsync` call returns 0 and the Failed row's `EndedAt` and `Reason` are unchanged, demonstrating that a terminal row is never rewritten (I5 of TR-57)
After scenario (d) `LiveCountAsync` returns 1 (only the Waiting row), showing the slot was released by the terminal write itself (I4 of TR-57)
The file carries `[Trait("Invariant", ...)]` values covering each of I4, I5, I6, I8 and I9, and `dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests --filter FullyQualifiedName~TransitionTests` passes (TR-69)

tickets.title: Write TR-69 (a) concurrent admission, (f) refusals and (g) partial index tests
tickets.context: Scenarios for slot admission and the three admission invariants: capacity, one live session per episode, no live session for an existing episode.
tickets.motivation: Concurrent admission at capacity, both kinds of refusal, and the partial index firing on a direct insert that bypasses the store together cover every way admission can be wrong.
tickets.goal: The three scenarios passing on real Postgres.
tickets.value: Capacity and uniqueness are proven at the database level, including the backstop that protects against code the store does not control.
tickets.description: Add `AdventureTime.Tests/Station/AdmissionTests.cs` (extends `StoreTestBase`) demonstrating I1, I2 and I3 of TR-57 against the real `AnnounceAsync` of F2.2. Scenario (a), §9.2: with Capacity = 3 and empty tables, create 4 independent `AppDbContext` instances and 4 stores, build `WaitingCandidate` rows for S11E01..S11E04, and run the four `AnnounceAsync(candidate, 3, ct)` calls with `Task.WhenAll`; assert exactly 3 outcomes are `AnnounceOutcome.Admitted` (each with `Occupancy` between 1 and 3), 1 is `AnnounceOutcome.Full` with `Occupancy == 3`, `RetryAfterSeconds >= 1` and `EarliestExpiry != null`, `LiveCountAsync == 3` and `SELECT count(*) FROM "Sessions"` is 3 (the refused candidate wrote no row). In the same test open a transaction the way the store does (`await using var tx = await ctx.Database.BeginTransactionAsync(ct)` with no isolation argument) and assert `SqlQuery<string>($"SELECT current_setting('transaction_isolation') AS \"Value\"")` returns `read committed`, then assert `ctx.Database.CreateExecutionStrategy().RetriesOnFailure == false`. Scenario (f): insert an `Episodes` row for S11E05 via `ctx.Episodes.Add(SampleEpisode(11,5))` and assert `AnnounceAsync` for S11E05 returns `EpisodeExists` whose `EpisodeId` equals the inserted `Episode.Id`; then `InsertWaitingAsync(11,6)` and assert an announce for S11E06 returns `LiveConflict` with `ManifestId` equal to the seeded id and `State == SessionState.Waiting`. Scenario (g), §9.4: seed a Working row for S11E07 (`InsertWaitingAsync` + `SetWorkingAsync`), then call `InsertWaitingAsync(ctx, 11, 7)` again — this helper is the raw announce INSERT of TR-36 with a fresh id and bypasses both the store and the advisory lock; assert it throws `PostgresException` with `SqlState == "23505"` and `ConstraintName == "IX_Sessions_Live_Season_Episode"` (catch `PostgresException` directly; `ExecuteSqlAsync`/`FromSql` do not wrap it in `DbUpdateException`); then run `UPDATE "Sessions" SET "State"='Done', "EndedAt"=now(), "DeliveryPayload"=NULL WHERE "Id"={id}` and assert the identical `InsertWaitingAsync(11,7)` now succeeds. Row assertions use `ReadRowAsync` on a separate context.
acceptance_criteria: `AdmissionTests.FourConcurrentAnnounces_AdmitThree_RefuseOne` passes: 3 `Admitted` (each `Occupancy` in 1..3), 1 `Full` with `Occupancy == 3`, `RetryAfterSeconds >= 1`, `EarliestExpiry != null`; `SELECT count(*)::int FROM "Sessions" WHERE "State" IN ('Waiting','Working')` returns 3 and `SELECT count(*) FROM "Sessions"` returns 3 (TR-69(a); I1 of TR-57)

Inside a transaction opened with `BeginTransactionAsync(ct)` and no isolation argument, `current_setting('transaction_isolation')` returns `read committed`, and `CreateExecutionStrategy().RetriesOnFailure` is false (TR-69(a))

`AdmissionTests.Announce_EpisodeExists_Refused` returns `AnnounceOutcome.EpisodeExists` with `EpisodeId` equal to the pre-inserted `Episodes.Id` for S11E05 and `SELECT count(*) FROM "Sessions"` stays 0 (TR-69(f); I3 of TR-57)

`AdmissionTests.Announce_LiveConflict_NamesExistingId` returns `AnnounceOutcome.LiveConflict` with `ManifestId` equal to the seeded Waiting row for S11E06 and `State == SessionState.Waiting`; `SELECT count(*) FROM "Sessions"` stays 1 (TR-69(f); I2 of TR-57)

`AdmissionTests.PartialIndex_BlocksSecondLiveRow` catches `PostgresException` with `SqlState == "23505"` and `ConstraintName == "IX_Sessions_Live_Season_Episode"` on a direct second insert for S11E07 while the first is Working, and the same insert succeeds after the first row is set Done (TR-69(g); I2 of TR-57)

Every test in the file carries `[Trait("Invariant", ...)]` for I1, I2 or I3, and `dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests --filter FullyQualifiedName~AdmissionTests` passes 5 consecutive times (`for i in $(seq 5)` loop) without a flake (TR-69)

tickets.title: Write TR-69 (c) Fail-then-Complete, (h) Complete twice and (i) existing-episode tests
tickets.context: Scenarios for Complete's guards: a session that failed before Complete ran, Complete called twice, and an episode that already exists.
tickets.motivation: These are the paths where an LLM call has already been paid for and the temptation is to store something anyway. The invariant is that nothing is inserted unless the session was still Working, and that the second and third cases leave the tables consistent.
tickets.goal: Fail-then-Complete inserts nothing, Complete twice is harmless, and an existing episode fails the session with a reason.
tickets.value: The guarantee that the Episodes table never holds an orphan is tested on every path that could produce one.
tickets.description: Add `AdventureTime.Tests/Station/CompleteTests.cs` (extends `StoreTestBase`) demonstrating I4, I5, I6 and I7 of TR-57 against the real `CompleteAsync` of F2.3 and `FailAsync` of F2.1. Scenario (c): seed a Working row B (`InsertWaitingAsync` + `SetWorkingAsync` with `SamplePayloadJson`), call `FailAsync(B, "working deadline exceeded", ct)` (assert true), then `CompleteAsync(B, SampleEpisode(11,1), SampleAnalysis(), ct)`; assert `CompleteOutcome.LostSlot`, `Episodes` and `EpisodeAnalyses` both have `count(*) == 0`, and B is `Failed` with `Reason == "working deadline exceeded"` and `DeliveryPayload == null`. Scenario (h): seed a Working row for (11,2), call `CompleteAsync` twice with fresh `SampleEpisode(11,2)`/`SampleAnalysis()` instances each time; the first returns `Completed`, `Episodes` holds exactly one row with `SessionId == id`, `EpisodeAnalyses` holds exactly one row whose `EpisodeId` equals that episode's `Id` and whose `AnalysisSource == "Stub"` and `AnalysisVersion == "station-v1"` (TR-38 step 2 with the default `StationOptions.AnalysisProvider`), the session is `Done` with `DeliveryPayload == null` and `EndedAt != null`, and `LiveCountAsync == 0`; the second call returns `LostSlot` and both counts are still 1. Scenario (i): insert `SampleEpisode(11,3)` into `Episodes` first (it has `SessionId == null`, so only `IX_Episode_Season_Number` can collide), seed a Working session for (11,3) by direct SQL (bypassing the I3 admission check on purpose), call `CompleteAsync` on a store built over context C; assert `CompleteOutcome.EpisodeExists`, the session is `Failed` with `Reason == "episode exists"`, `SELECT count(*) FROM "Episodes" WHERE "Season"=11 AND "EpisodeNumber"=3` is 1, `C.ChangeTracker.Entries().Count() == 0`, and a subsequent `C.SaveChangesAsync()` returns 0 and leaves both table counts unchanged (tracker cleared per TR-38). All row assertions use a separate context with `AsNoTracking` so the store's own context state does not mask a missing commit. Tag tests so that I4, I5, I6 and I7 each appear in this file.
acceptance_criteria: `CompleteTests.FailThenComplete_LostSlot_InsertsNothing` asserts `FailAsync` returned true, `CompleteAsync` returns `LostSlot`, `Episodes` and `EpisodeAnalyses` are empty, and row B is `Failed` with `Reason == "working deadline exceeded"` and `DeliveryPayload == null` (TR-69(c); I5, I7 of TR-57)

`CompleteTests.Complete_Twice_FirstCompletedSecondLostSlot` asserts the first call returns `Completed` with exactly one `Episodes` row (`SessionId == id`) and one `EpisodeAnalyses` row (`EpisodeId` == the new episode id, `AnalysisSource == "Stub"`, `AnalysisVersion == "station-v1"`), session `Done`, `DeliveryPayload == null`, `EndedAt != null`; the second call returns `LostSlot` with both counts still 1 (TR-69(h); I5, I6, I7 of TR-57)
After the first `Completed` in (h), `LiveCountAsync` returns 0, demonstrating the slot was released by the same transaction that inserted the episode (I4, I7 of TR-57)

`CompleteTests.Complete_ExistingEpisode_FailsSessionAndClearsTracker` asserts `EpisodeExists`, session `Failed` with `Reason == "episode exists"`, exactly one `Episodes` row for (11, 3), `C.ChangeTracker.Entries().Count() == 0`, and `C.SaveChangesAsync()` returns 0 with `Episodes` and `EpisodeAnalyses` counts unchanged (TR-69(i); I3 of TR-57; consumer of TR-38)

Row assertions are made through a second `AppDbContext` with `AsNoTracking()`; `grep -n 'ReadRowAsync\|AsNoTracking' AdventureTime.Tests/Station/CompleteTests.cs` shows every row read, and none goes through the store's context
The file carries `[Trait("Invariant", ...)]` values covering each of I4, I5, I6 and I7, and `dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests --filter FullyQualifiedName~CompleteTests` passes (TR-69)

tickets.title: Write TR-69 (j) GetAsync projection test and invariant traceability check
tickets.context: The last numbered scenario and a traceability check across the whole invariant table.
tickets.motivation: The projection test proves the payload is hidden from ordinary reads. The traceability check ensures every invariant in the requirements has a named test, so nothing in that table is merely asserted in prose.
tickets.goal: The projection scenario passing and a mapping from each invariant to the test that demonstrates it.
tickets.value: Closes the loop between the requirements and the test suite: every stated invariant has evidence.
tickets.description: Add `AdventureTime.Tests/Station/ProjectionTests.cs` (extends `StoreTestBase`) for scenario (j) against the read projections of F2.3: seed a Working row with `SamplePayloadJson(11,4)` and non-empty `Flags` (run `UPDATE "Sessions" SET "Flags"='[{"code":"TitleMismatch","message":"x"}]'::jsonb WHERE "Id"={id}` after `SetWorkingAsync`), call `GetAsync(id, ct)` and then `GetForProcessingAsync(id, ct)` on the same store; assert the first returns `DeliveryPayload == null` while `Id`, `State`, `Season`, `EpisodeNumber`, `Title`, `ExpectedCharacters`, `ExpectedLocations`, `RequestedStages`, `TtlSeconds`, `AnnouncedAt`, `ExpiresAt`, `DeliveredAt`, `WorkingDeadlineAt` and `Flags` are all non-null/non-empty and equal to the values read with `ReadRowAsync`; the second returns the staged payload, compared with `JsonNode.DeepEquals(JsonNode.Parse(returned), JsonNode.Parse(staged))` so jsonb key reordering and whitespace are ignored (no serializer options and no `StationJson` needed). Also assert `GetAsync(Guid.NewGuid())` returns null and that neither call leaves tracked entries on the store's context (`ctx.ChangeTracker.Entries().Count() == 0`, TR-40). Then close out TR-57 traceability: add `AdventureTime.Tests/Station/InvariantCoverageTests.cs` that reflects over `typeof(InvariantCoverageTests).Assembly`, reads every `Xunit.TraitAttribute` whose first constructor argument is `"Invariant"` via `CustomAttributeData`, and asserts that each of I1..I9 appears at least once, with a comment table mapping I1→(a), I2→(f)(g), I3→(f)(i), I4→(c)(d)(h), I5→(c)(d)(h), I6→(b)(d)(h), I7→(c)(h), I8→(b), I9→(d) so a reviewer can see which test holds each invariant. Finally verify the whole store suite runs green together and add a header comment at the top of `StoreTestBase.cs` stating that Docker must be running and how to run only the store tests.
acceptance_criteria: `ProjectionTests.GetAsync_ProjectsPayloadAsNull` asserts `GetAsync(id)` returns a `Session` with `DeliveryPayload == null` and every other column of TR-8 populated and equal to a `ReadRowAsync` read of the row, including the non-empty `Flags` (TR-69(j); consumer of TR-40)

`ProjectionTests.GetForProcessing_IncludesPayload` asserts `JsonNode.DeepEquals` between the payload returned by `GetForProcessingAsync(id)` and the staged `SamplePayloadJson(11,4)`, and `GetAsync(Guid.NewGuid())` returns null (TR-69(j))
After both calls `ctx.ChangeTracker.Entries().Count() == 0` on the store's context (consumer of TR-40)

`InvariantCoverageTests.EveryInvariantHasATest` passes: the set of `Trait("Invariant")` values across the assembly is a superset of {I1, I2, I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, I9}, and the file's comment table lists the scenario letter(s) for each invariant (TR-57)

`dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests --filter Invariant=I7` selects at least two tests and passes; `dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests` with Docker running passes all scenarios (a)(b)(c)(d)(f)(g)(h)(i)(j) in one run (TR-69, TR-67)

The header comment of `AdventureTime.Tests/Station/StoreTestBase.cs` states the Docker prerequisite and the command `dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests --filter FullyQualifiedName~AdventureTime.Tests.Station`, and that filter selects every test under `AdventureTime.Tests/Station/`

review_notes: F2.4-T3 and F2.4-T7 referenced `StationJson.Options` (Application/Station/StationJson.cs), which is TR-25 and owned by F3.1; F2.4 declares no dependency on F3.1. Replaced with a test-local `StationTestData.Json = new JsonSerializerOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web)` for staging payloads, and the scenario (j) payload comparison now uses `JsonNode.DeepEquals` (no serializer options needed).

F2.4-T3 `SetExpiresAtAsync(ctx, id, string intervalSql)` would not work as described: an interpolated string inside `ExecuteSqlAsync($"...")` becomes a text parameter and `now() + @p` fails in Postgres. Changed the helper to take a `TimeSpan offset`, which Npgsql binds as `interval`.

F2.4-T4 hedged scenario (b) with 'either truncate between iterations or assert >= 1', contradicting TR-69(b) ('ExpireOverdue returned 1'). Because every iteration uses a distinct EpisodeNumber and earlier rows are already TimedOut (expired variant) or Working (live variant), `ExpireOverdueAsync(null)` returns exactly 1 and exactly 0 respectively; the ticket now asserts those exact values.
F2.4-T4 acceptance criterion 'ExpireOverdue counted the row' was not a verifiable value; replaced with `== 1`. 'byte-for-byte unchanged' rephrased as equality against values captured before the call.

F2.4-T2 criterion 'container start appears once in the test output' was not reviewer-verifiable; replaced with a concrete check (a single `postgres:15-alpine` container in `docker ps` during the run, and a static start counter of 1 asserted by the fixture test).
F2.4-T3 had `StationTestData` (a data helper) 'asserting' the lock key; moved that assertion into a real test `StoreTestBaseTests.InternalsVisibleTo_Exposes_StationLockKey`.
F2.4-T7 filters on `FullyQualifiedName~AdventureTime.Tests.Station` but no ticket fixed the namespace; F2.4-T3 now mandates namespace `AdventureTime.Tests.Station` for the Station folder.

F2.4-T7's invariant mapping (I4->(c)(d)(h), I6->(b)(d)(h)) required traits that F2.4-T4 and F2.4-T6 did not require: T4 now mandates traits I4/I5/I6/I8/I9 and T6 mandates I4/I5/I6/I7 so `InvariantCoverageTests` can pass.
F2.4-T3 criteria cited (TR-12) as if satisfied; TR-12 is owned by F1.3. Rewritten as 'respects TR-12' so ownership is not implied; tr_ids unchanged.

F2.4-T5 scenario (g) re-implemented the raw announce INSERT although `InsertWaitingAsync` of F2.4-T3 already is that direct SQL; simplified to reuse the helper (fresh `Guid.CreateVersion7()` id each call) and stated explicitly that it bypasses the store and the advisory lock.
F2.4-T3 estimate raised from S to M: six SQL/data helpers plus helper self-tests and the InternalsVisibleTo test exceed half a day.
Clarified in F2.4-T1/T2 that the `xunit` package is xunit 2.x (Task-based `IAsyncLifetime`), not `xunit.v3`, since TR-67 names the package `xunit`.

epics.title: Application layer: manifest commands and fulfilment
epics.goal: MediatR handlers announce, deliver, cancel and read manifests through `IStationStore`: a delivery is validated (all 422 reasons at once), flagged against the manifest, staged as jsonb by `TryBeginWork`, and enqueued only after that statement committed — proven by unit tests of the pure functions and handler resolution.

features.title: Pure station functions, DTOs and unit tests
features.summary: Add the database-free building blocks under `Application/Station/` and `Application/Dtos/Manifests/`: `SessionTransitions.IsLegal/IsTerminal` with `TransitionTrigger`, `Flag`/`FlagCode` (exactly five codes), `AnnounceManifestRequest` (DataAnnotations + `JsonUnmappedMemberHandling.Disallow`), `DeliverEpisodeRequest` (no annotations, all-nullable so the 21 seed files bind as-is), the response DTOs, `DeliveryValidator.Validate` returning every TR-19 reason plus a `NormalizedDelivery`, `FulfilmentFlags.Compute`, `EpisodeMapper.ToEpisode`, and `StationJson.Options`. Closes with the TR-68 unit test table (transition cross product, flag cases, announce/deliver validation, stub determinism), which needs the test project from F2.4 and the stub from F1.2.

tickets.title: Add SessionTransitions, TransitionTrigger, Flag/FlagCode and StationJson.Options
tickets.context: The first Application-layer pieces that need no database: the transition table as a pure function, the five flag codes, and a single JSON options object.
tickets.motivation: The SQL predicates are the runtime guard, but a pure function over the transition table pins the design in a unit test and documents it as code. Fixing the flag codes as an enum prevents free-text drift, and one shared serializer options object stops camelCase from being applied inconsistently between the staged payload, the flags column and the API.
tickets.goal: Three small files: transitions with their triggers, flags with their codes, and the JSON options.
tickets.value: The state machine is readable as code, flag names are stable for the viewer and the tests, and serialization is consistent everywhere a Session or a flag is written.
tickets.description: Create the first three database-free files under AdventureTime.Application/Station/. SessionTransitions.cs holds `public enum TransitionTrigger { Announce, Deliver, Cancel, Expire, Complete, Fail, WorkingDeadline, Interrupted }` and `public static class SessionTransitions` with `IsLegal(SessionState? from, SessionState to, TransitionTrigger trigger)` (null from = "(new)") and `IsTerminal(SessionState)`; IsLegal is a lookup over exactly the eight rows of the TR-4 transition table (https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2dc9531c-3f0b-499f-8ec6-fb2cf3271341#TR-4): (null→Waiting, Announce), (Waiting→Working, Deliver), (Waiting→Cancelled, Cancel), (Waiting→TimedOut, Expire), (Working→Done, Complete), (Working→Failed, Fail), (Working→Failed, WorkingDeadline), (Working→Failed, Interrupted). Flag.cs holds `public sealed record Flag(string Code, string Message)` and `public static class FlagCode` with exactly five `const string` members whose values equal their names: CharacterAbsent, LocationAbsent, TitleMismatch, UnannouncedCharacter, FocusCharacterMismatch (there is deliberately no runtime flag, TR-7). StationJson.cs exposes `public static readonly JsonSerializerOptions Options` (PropertyNamingPolicy = CamelCase, WriteIndented = false, PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true), the single options instance TR-25 requires for "Flags", "DeliveryPayload" and "ContinuityNotesJson"; model it on the private `JsonOptions` field in AdventureTime.Application/Entities/EpisodeAnalysis/EpisodeAnalysisEntity.cs but do not reference that private field. Because TR-25 names ContinuityNotesJson, change the `ContinuityNotesJson` serialize/deserialize lines that F1.3 added to `EpisodeAnalysisEntity.FromDomainModel`/`ToDomainModel` (TR-10) to pass `StationJson.Options`; leave the entity's other jsonb columns on their existing private options. `SessionState` comes from AdventureTime.Application/Enums/SessionState.cs (F1.3, TR-1). Gotcha: the store never consults SessionTransitions at runtime (the SQL predicates are the runtime guard), so keep it a pure table with no side effects and no dependency on Infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` succeeds with the three new files AdventureTime.Application/Station/SessionTransitions.cs, Flag.cs, StationJson.cs and no new package references in AdventureTime.Application.csproj.

`SessionTransitions.IsLegal` returns true for exactly the eight (from, to, trigger) triples of TR-4 listed in the description and false for every other triple of the 7 x 6 x 8 = 336 cross product of `SessionState?` x `SessionState` x `TransitionTrigger`, including every triple whose from-state is Done, Failed, TimedOut or Cancelled (TR-5).
`SessionTransitions.IsTerminal` returns true for Done, Failed, TimedOut, Cancelled and false for Waiting and Working; `TransitionTrigger` has exactly the eight members named in TR-5 (TR-5).

`FlagCode` exposes exactly five public const string members (CharacterAbsent, LocationAbsent, TitleMismatch, UnannouncedCharacter, FocusCharacterMismatch), each equal to its own name, and no other members (TR-7).

`JsonSerializer.Serialize(new[] { new Flag("TitleMismatch", "x") }, StationJson.Options)` produces exactly `[{"code":"TitleMismatch","message":"x"}]`, i.e. a camelCase array of {code, message} (TR-7, TR-25).
`StationJson.Options` is a single static readonly instance with camelCase naming and no indentation; grep shows no other `new JsonSerializerOptions` under AdventureTime.Application/Station/ (TR-25).

In AdventureTime.Application/Entities/EpisodeAnalysis/EpisodeAnalysisEntity.cs the `ContinuityNotesJson` serialize and deserialize calls reference `StationJson.Options` (grep `StationJson.Options` in that file shows both), and `ToDomainModel` of an entity with `ContinuityNotesJson = "[\"follows S11E03 'Low Battery'\"]"` yields `ContinuityNotes` with that one string (TR-25).

tickets.title: Add manifest request and response DTOs under Application/Dtos/Manifests
tickets.context: Until now the Episode entity has been the API's request and response type. The station needs dedicated DTOs with different rules for the manifest and the delivery.
tickets.motivation: A manifest must reject content fields outright, which the unmapped-member setting enforces at deserialization, while a delivery must accept the 21 seed files exactly as they are. Putting DataAnnotations on the manifest only, and making the delivery all-nullable, gives each door its own contract without touching the entity.
tickets.goal: The six request and response DTOs with the annotations and settings the requirements specify.
tickets.value: The API contract is explicit and versionable, the seed data binds without edits, and the entity stops carrying the burden of being a wire format.
tickets.description: Create the folder AdventureTime.Application/Dtos/Manifests/ with the six DTOs of TR-23. `AnnounceManifestRequest` (TR-16) is a class annotated `[JsonUnmappedMemberHandling(JsonUnmappedMemberHandling.Disallow)]` with `[Range(1, int.MaxValue)] int Season`, `[Range(1, int.MaxValue)] int EpisodeNumber`, `[Required][MaxLength(200)] string Title = string.Empty`, `[Required][MinLength(1)] List<string> ExpectedCharacters = new()`, and nullable `string? FocusCharacter`, `List<string>? ExpectedLocations`, `List<string>? RequestedStages`, `int? TtlSeconds`; the non-nullable members are implicitly required under [ApiController] (TR-15) so a missing title is a framework 400 by design. `DeliverEpisodeRequest` (TR-19) carries NO DataAnnotations and NO unmapped-member attribute: `string? Title`, `int Season`, `int EpisodeNumber`, `string? ProductionCode`, `DateTimeOffset? AirDate`, `double? RuntimeMinutes`, `string? FocusCharacter`, `string? Synopsis`, `string? Plot`, `string? TranscriptText`, `List<string>? MajorCharacters`, `List<string>? MinorCharacters`, `List<string>? Locations`, `int? DialogueLineCount` — the same fourteen camelCase keys as the existing AdventureTime.Application/Commands/Episodes/CreateEpisode/CreateEpisodeCommand.cs, so the 21 files in AdventureTime/Episodes/*.json bind as-is and every content problem reaches the handler as a 422 rather than a 400. Response types are sealed records: `AnnounceManifestResponse(Guid Id, string State, DateTime ExpiresAt, int Occupancy, int Capacity)`; `DeliverEpisodeResponse(Guid SessionId, string State, IReadOnlyList<Flag> Flags, DateTime? WorkingDeadlineAt)`; `ManifestResponse` with every TR-17 member (Id, State, Season, EpisodeNumber, Title, FocusCharacter, ExpectedCharacters, ExpectedLocations, RequestedStages, TtlSeconds, AnnouncedAt, ExpiresAt, DeliveredAt, WorkingDeadlineAt, EndedAt, Reason, Flags, `int? EpisodeId`, `ManifestLinks Links`) with `ManifestLinks(string Self, string? Deliver, string? Episode, string? Analysis)` declared in ManifestResponse.cs and serialized as the nested `links` object; `StationResponse(int Capacity, int Occupancy, IReadOnlyList<StationLiveEntry> Live, IReadOnlyList<StationRecentEntry> Recent)` with the entry records carrying the TR-21 fields. `ManifestResponse` MUST NOT have a DeliveryPayload member; `EpisodeId` and the optional link members carry `[property: JsonIgnore(Condition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull)]` (the `property:` target is mandatory on positional record parameters, otherwise the attribute is silently dropped) so they appear only when set (Done / Waiting), while `Reason`, `DeliveredAt`, `WorkingDeadlineAt`, `EndedAt` serialize as explicit `null` as in the TR-17/TR-21 examples. State is a plain string (`SessionState.ToString()`) so no enum converter has to be registered in Program.cs.
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` succeeds with AdventureTime.Application/Dtos/Manifests/{AnnounceManifestRequest,DeliverEpisodeRequest,AnnounceManifestResponse,DeliverEpisodeResponse,ManifestResponse,StationResponse}.cs present and `ManifestLinks` declared in ManifestResponse.cs (TR-23).

`AnnounceManifestRequest` is decorated with `[JsonUnmappedMemberHandling(JsonUnmappedMemberHandling.Disallow)]` and `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<AnnounceManifestRequest>("{\"season\":11,\"episodeNumber\":1,\"title\":\"x\",\"expectedCharacters\":[\"Finn\"],\"transcriptText\":\"...\"}", StationJson.Options)` throws `JsonException` (TR-16, TR-23).

`Validator.TryValidateObject(req, new ValidationContext(req), results, validateAllProperties: true)` (System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations) on an AnnounceManifestRequest with `Season = 0`, `Title = ""` and `ExpectedCharacters = []` returns false with `results` naming the members Season, Title and ExpectedCharacters, proving the `[Range]`, `[Required]` and `[MinLength(1)]` annotations of TR-16 are present; a 201-character Title adds a MaxLength result (TR-16).

`DeliverEpisodeRequest` carries no attribute from System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations and no JsonUnmappedMemberHandling attribute; every member except `Season` and `EpisodeNumber` is declared nullable (`string?`, `DateTimeOffset?`, `double?`, `int?`, `List<string>?`) (TR-19).

`JsonSerializer.Deserialize<DeliverEpisodeRequest>(File.ReadAllText("AdventureTime/Episodes/s1e8__dungeon.json"), StationJson.Options)` succeeds and yields `Season == 1`, `EpisodeNumber == 18`, non-null `AirDate` with `Offset == TimeSpan.Zero`, and `{}` deserializes to an instance with `TranscriptText == null` and `Season == 0` rather than throwing (TR-19, TR-15).

Serializing a `ManifestResponse` whose `EpisodeId`, `Links.Episode`, `Links.Analysis` and `Links.Deliver` are null with StationJson.Options omits those four members, still emits `"reason":null` and `"endedAt":null`, never emits a `deliveryPayload` member, and serializes `Flags` as `[]` when empty (TR-23, TR-17).

`StationResponse` serializes with camelCase members `capacity`, `occupancy`, `live[]` (id, state, season, episodeNumber, title, announcedAt, expiresAt, deliveredAt, workingDeadlineAt) and `recent[]` (id, state, season, episodeNumber, title, endedAt, reason) and nothing else (TR-23, TR-21).

tickets.title: Add pure AnnounceValidator for the handler-level TR-16 rules
tickets.context: Rules that DataAnnotations cannot express: the focus character must be in the cast, the TTL must lie within configured bounds, and stage names must be known.
tickets.motivation: A sender should fix a bad announcement in one round trip, which means every error must come back together. Normalizing once, in a pure function, also gives the handler a clean input and the tests a clean target.
tickets.goal: A pure validator returning all errors keyed by field, or a normalized announcement.
tickets.value: 400 responses are complete and predictable, and the announce handler stays thin.
tickets.description: Add AdventureTime.Application/Station/AnnounceValidator.cs: `public static class AnnounceValidator` with `Validate(AnnounceManifestRequest request, int ttlMin, int ttlMax, int ttlDefault) : AnnounceValidationOutcome`, where `AnnounceValidationOutcome(IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string[]> Errors, NormalizedAnnouncement? Normalized)` and `NormalizedAnnouncement(int Season, int EpisodeNumber, string Title, string? FocusCharacter, List<string> ExpectedCharacters, List<string> ExpectedLocations, List<string> RequestedStages, int TtlSeconds)`. The TRD names no such type; it is the pure core of the TR-27 announce handler (F3.2 MUST call it and pass `options.TtlMin/TtlMax/TtlDefault` rather than re-implementing the rules) and it makes the TR-68 `Announce_Validation` row testable without a database or a mocked `IStationStore`. It implements exactly the rules TR-16 assigns to the handler: `title` blank after trim → key `title`; any `expectedCharacters` entry blank after trim → key `expectedCharacters`; `focusCharacter` present but not equal (ordinal-ignore-case, trimmed) to an entry of expectedCharacters → key `focusCharacter`; any `requestedStages` entry outside `Sentiment, CharacterMoods, Relationships, Themes, StoryArc, KeyMoments` (ordinal-ignore-case, stored in canonical casing) → key `requestedStages`; `ttlSeconds` outside `[ttlMin, ttlMax]` → key `ttlSeconds` with message `must be between {ttlMin} and {ttlMax}` (the exact TR-16 example text for 60/86400). Every failing rule is collected into `Errors` (not first-failure), and `Normalized` is produced only when `Errors` is empty, with title, every expectedCharacters/expectedLocations entry and focusCharacter trimmed, `expectedLocations` defaulted to `[]`, `requestedStages` defaulted to all six names, and `ttlSeconds` defaulted to `ttlDefault`. The bounds are passed as ints rather than `StationOptions` so this file has no dependency on F1.1. Do not put DataAnnotation-level rules (Range, Required, MaxLength) here — those stay on the DTO and are the framework's 400.
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` succeeds with AdventureTime.Application/Station/AnnounceValidator.cs defining `AnnounceValidator.Validate`, `AnnounceValidationOutcome` and `NormalizedAnnouncement` (TR-27, TR-68).

`Validate` on a request with `focusCharacter = "Marceline"` and `expectedCharacters = ["Finn","Jake"]` returns `Errors["focusCharacter"]` non-empty and `Normalized == null`; with `focusCharacter = " finn "` it returns no errors and `Normalized.FocusCharacter == "finn"` (trimmed, case preserved) (TR-16).

`Validate` with `ttlSeconds = 59` and with `ttlSeconds = 86401` (bounds 60/86400) each returns `Errors["ttlSeconds"] == ["must be between 60 and 86400"]`; `ttlSeconds = null` yields `Normalized.TtlSeconds == ttlDefault` (TR-16).

`Validate` with `requestedStages = ["Sentiment","Weather"]` returns `Errors["requestedStages"]` non-empty; `requestedStages = ["sentiment"]` yields `Normalized.RequestedStages == ["Sentiment"]`; `requestedStages = null` yields the six canonical names in TR-16 order; `expectedLocations = null` yields `Normalized.ExpectedLocations == []` and `expectedLocations = [" Tree Fort "]` yields `["Tree Fort"]` (TR-16).

A single request with blank title, a blank `expectedCharacters` entry, an unknown stage, a bad focus character and `ttlSeconds = 0` returns all five keys (`title`, `expectedCharacters`, `focusCharacter`, `requestedStages`, `ttlSeconds`) in one `Errors` dictionary (TR-16, TR-27).

The function has no dependency on AdventureTime.Infrastructure, `StationOptions`, or any I/O; its only inputs are the request and the three ints, so the TR-68 `Announce_Validation` test can call it with no fixture (TR-68).

tickets.title: Implement DeliveryValidator.Validate with NormalizedDelivery
tickets.context: The 422 rules for a delivery: identity must match the manifest, the transcript must be non-empty, and the DTO must be valid.
tickets.motivation: Rejections have to be cheap and complete. Collecting every reason in one pass avoids a sender discovering problems one at a time, and stripping NUL characters and normalizing the air date to UTC here prevents two failures that would otherwise happen after a paid LLM call, at the jsonb staging insert and at the Episode insert.
tickets.goal: A pure validator returning all reasons or a normalized delivery.
tickets.value: No delivery burns an LLM call only to fail at insert, and a rejected sender knows everything wrong with the request at once.
tickets.description: Add AdventureTime.Application/Station/DeliveryValidator.cs: `public static class DeliveryValidator` with `Validate(Session manifest, DeliverEpisodeRequest request) : ValidationOutcome` (pure, no I/O), plus `public sealed record ValidationOutcome(IReadOnlyList<string> Reasons, NormalizedDelivery? Normalized)` and `public sealed record NormalizedDelivery(string Title, int Season, int EpisodeNumber, string? ProductionCode, DateTimeOffset AirDate, double RuntimeMinutes, string? FocusCharacter, string? Synopsis, string? Plot, string TranscriptText, List<string> MajorCharacters, List<string> MinorCharacters, List<string> Locations, int? DialogueLineCount)`. Evaluate every TR-19 rule independently and append its exact message, so a bad body yields all of its reasons in one result: `title is required` (null/blank after trim), `title exceeds 200 characters`, `season must be >= 1`, `episodeNumber must be >= 1`, `season {r} does not match manifest season {m}`, `episodeNumber {r} does not match manifest episodeNumber {m}`, `airDate is required`, `runtimeMinutes must be > 0` (non-null and <= 0), `focusCharacter exceeds 100 characters`, `synopsis exceeds 2000 characters`, `productionCode exceeds 20 characters` (the three length messages are chosen here; TR-19 fixes only the limits, measured after trim), and for transcriptText strip every `\0` first, then `transcriptText is required` when null/empty after trim. Normalization: all strings trimmed (blank optional strings become null), NUL characters stripped from transcriptText, `runtimeMinutes` null → 11.0, the three list members null → `[]` with entries trimmed and blank entries dropped. `Normalized` is non-null if and only if `Reasons` is empty. `Session` is the entity from AdventureTime.Application/Entities/Station/Session.cs (F1.3, TR-6); only its Season and EpisodeNumber are consulted here. Gotcha: `Reasons` must be an ordered list (rule order as listed above) so the 422 body of TR-20 is deterministic and the F5.4 scenario can assert on `reasons` contents.
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` succeeds with AdventureTime.Application/Station/DeliveryValidator.cs defining `DeliveryValidator.Validate`, `ValidationOutcome` and `NormalizedDelivery`; the file references nothing from AdventureTime.Infrastructure (TR-23).

Given a manifest for S11E01 and a request with `title = null`, `transcriptText = "   "`, `airDate = null`, `runtimeMinutes = 0`, `season = 12`, `episodeNumber = 1`, `Validate` returns `Normalized == null` and `Reasons` equal, as a set, to exactly `title is required`, `season 12 does not match manifest season 11`, `airDate is required`, `runtimeMinutes must be > 0`, `transcriptText is required` in one call (TR-19).
A request with a 201-character title and `transcriptText = "\0\0"` yields both `title exceeds 200 characters` and `transcriptText is required` (NUL-only transcript is treated as empty) (TR-19).

A valid request whose transcript is `"Finn: hi\0 there"` and `runtimeMinutes = null` yields `Reasons.Count == 0` and `Normalized.TranscriptText == "Finn: hi there"`, `Normalized.RuntimeMinutes == 11.0`; `majorCharacters = null` and `locations = [" Tree Fort ", "  "]` yield `Normalized.MajorCharacters == []` and `Normalized.Locations == ["Tree Fort"]` (TR-19).

`season = 0` yields `season must be >= 1`, and `episodeNumber = 2` against manifest episode 1 yields `episodeNumber 2 does not match manifest episodeNumber 1`; `focusCharacter` of 101 characters, `synopsis` of 2001 and `productionCode` of 21 each add their `exceeds N characters` reason (TR-19).

`Validate` never throws for any syntactically valid `DeliverEpisodeRequest` (all-null members included) and never touches a DbContext or clock; `Normalized` is non-null exactly when `Reasons` is empty (TR-23).

tickets.title: Implement FulfilmentFlags.Compute and EpisodeMapper.ToEpisode
tickets.context: The judgment-call half of the fulfilment check, and the one place the Episode is materialized from a delivery.
tickets.motivation: The manifest is a contract, but rejecting a delivery because a minor character was missing would be the wrong call. Flags record every discrepancy without blocking, so the contract is enforced softly where hard rejection would be wrong. Materializing the Episode once ensures what gets staged is exactly what gets stored at Done.
tickets.goal: The five flag rules as a pure function and a mapper from normalized delivery to Episode.
tickets.value: Discrepancies are visible on the session and in the viewer without ever costing a delivery, and stored data always matches what was delivered.
tickets.description: Add AdventureTime.Application/Station/FulfilmentFlags.cs with `public static IReadOnlyList<Flag> Compute(Session manifest, NormalizedDelivery delivery)` implementing the TR-24 table. Let `cast` = distinct (ordinal-ignore-case) union of `delivery.MajorCharacters` and `delivery.MinorCharacters`, `text` = `delivery.TranscriptText`; all comparisons are ordinal-ignore-case on trimmed strings. Emit, in this order (chosen here): one `CharacterAbsent` per `manifest.ExpectedCharacters` entry that is neither in `cast` nor a substring of `text` (`expected character '{c}' not found`); one `LocationAbsent` per `manifest.ExpectedLocations` entry neither in `delivery.Locations` nor a substring of `text` (`expected location '{l}' not found`); `TitleMismatch` when trimmed titles differ case-insensitively (`title '{delivered}' differs from announced '{announced}'`, both rendered trimmed); one `UnannouncedCharacter` per cast member not in `manifest.ExpectedCharacters` (`'{c}' present in delivery but not announced`); `FocusCharacterMismatch` only when `manifest.FocusCharacter` is non-null and the delivery's differs or is null (`focus character '{d}' differs from announced '{a}'`, rendering a null delivered focus as `(none)`, chosen here). Flags never reject and never alter the delivery (A25). Add AdventureTime.Application/Station/EpisodeMapper.cs with `public static Episode ToEpisode(NormalizedDelivery normalized, Guid sessionId)` copying every field of AdventureTime.Application/Models/Episode.cs (Title, Season, EpisodeNumber, ProductionCode, RuntimeMinutes, FocusCharacter, Synopsis, Plot, TranscriptText, MajorCharacters, MinorCharacters, Locations, DialogueLineCount), setting `AirDate = normalized.AirDate.UtcDateTime` (Kind Utc, TR-12), `SessionId = sessionId` (the `Guid? SessionId` property added by F1.3 under TR-9), `CreatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow`, `Id = 0`, `LastModifiedAt = null`. Gotcha: the deliver handler (TR-28) serializes this Episode with `StationJson.Options` into "DeliveryPayload" and the worker deserializes it back (TR-44); `Episode.EpisodeCode` and `HasTranscript` are get-only computed properties that System.Text.Json writes but ignores on read, so the round trip must succeed and must not depend on them.
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` succeeds with AdventureTime.Application/Station/FulfilmentFlags.cs and EpisodeMapper.cs; both are static classes with no Infrastructure dependency (TR-24, TR-25).

Manifest expecting `Finn, Jake, BMO` with delivery cast `Finn, Jake` and a transcript not containing "BMO" yields exactly one flag, `Code == FlagCode.CharacterAbsent`, `Message == "expected character 'BMO' not found"`; if the transcript contains "bmo" (any case) no flag is produced (TR-24).

Manifest title `"the unfinished map "` vs delivery `"The Unfinished Map"` produces no `TitleMismatch`; delivery `"The Unfinished Map (Part 1)"` produces `TitleMismatch` with message `title 'The Unfinished Map (Part 1)' differs from announced 'the unfinished map'` (TR-24).

Delivery minor cast including `Marceline` (not announced) yields exactly one `UnannouncedCharacter` flag with message `'Marceline' present in delivery but not announced`; announced cast members produce none, and a name listed in both major and minor cast is flagged at most once (TR-24).

Manifest focus `Finn` with delivery focus null yields `FocusCharacterMismatch` with message `focus character '(none)' differs from announced 'Finn'`; identical focus (case-insensitive, trimmed) yields none; a manifest with `FocusCharacter == null` never yields `FocusCharacterMismatch` regardless of the delivery; `LocationAbsent` is emitted per missing `manifest.ExpectedLocations` entry with `expected location '{l}' not found` (TR-24, TR-7).

`EpisodeMapper.ToEpisode(normalized, id)` returns an Episode with `Id == 0`, `SessionId == id`, `LastModifiedAt == null`, `AirDate.Kind == DateTimeKind.Utc` and equal to `normalized.AirDate.UtcDateTime`, `CreatedAt` within a few seconds of now with Kind Utc, and every other field equal to the normalized value (TR-25, TR-12).

`JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Episode>(JsonSerializer.Serialize(EpisodeMapper.ToEpisode(n, id), StationJson.Options), StationJson.Options)` reproduces Title, Season, EpisodeNumber, SessionId, TranscriptText, the three lists and AirDate without throwing (TR-25).

tickets.title: Add TR-68 unit tests for transitions, flags and announce/deliver validation
tickets.context: Database-free unit tests for the pure functions built in this feature.
tickets.motivation: These rules are the ones most likely to change as the product evolves, and they are the cheapest to test. Fast, deterministic coverage here means the integration suite can stay focused on concurrency.
tickets.goal: Tests for the transition table, each flag rule, and both validators.
tickets.value: Sub-second feedback on the behavior a developer touches most often.
tickets.description: In the AdventureTime.Tests project created by F2.4 (TR-67), add a `Unit/` folder (namespace `AdventureTime.Tests.Unit`) with database-free xunit tests covering the first seven rows of the TR-68 table (https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2dc9531c-3f0b-499f-8ec6-fb2cf3271341#TR-68): AdventureTime.Tests/Unit/SessionTransitionsTests.cs (`Transitions_Table`), FulfilmentFlagsTests.cs (`Flags_CharacterAbsent`, `Flags_TitleCase`, `Flags_UnannouncedCharacter`, `Flags_FocusCharacter`), AnnounceValidationTests.cs (`Announce_Validation`) and DeliveryValidatorTests.cs (`Deliver_Validation`). `Transitions_Table` enumerates the full cross product `{null} ∪ Enum.GetValues<SessionState>()` x `Enum.GetValues<SessionState>()` x `Enum.GetValues<TransitionTrigger>()` (336 triples) and asserts the set of true results equals exactly the eight TR-4 rows, and `IsTerminal` over all six states. `Announce_Validation` drives `AnnounceValidator.Validate` (F3.1-T3) with bounds 60/86400 for each rejected case (focus not in expectedCharacters; ttl 59 and 86401; unknown stage; blank title; blank expectedCharacters entry) asserting the TR-16 key, and asserts that deserializing a body containing `transcriptText` into `AnnounceManifestRequest` throws `JsonException`. `Deliver_Validation` builds a `Session` manifest for S11E01 in memory and asserts every reason of the TR-68 row appears in one `ValidationOutcome`, plus the normalization assertions (NUL stripped, runtimeMinutes null → 11.0). Also add DeliverEpisodeRequestBindingTests.cs: include the seed files in the test csproj via `<Content Include="..\AdventureTime\Episodes\*.json" Link="Episodes\%(Filename)%(Extension)" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />` and assert all 21 deserialize into `DeliverEpisodeRequest` with StationJson.Options and pass `DeliveryValidator.Validate` against a matching manifest with zero reasons (this is the TR-19 promise that the seed files are valid bodies as-is — every file was checked against the TR-19 limits and passes, so any reason here is a validator bug, not a data problem; note s1e8__dungeon.json carries episodeNumber 18, so build the manifest from the file's own season/episodeNumber, not the filename). These tests need no PostgresFixture and must not be placed in the Postgres collection.
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~AdventureTime.Tests.Unit"` passes; every class under AdventureTime.Tests/Unit/ is in namespace `AdventureTime.Tests.Unit`, the seven TR-68 test names (`Transitions_Table`, `Flags_CharacterAbsent`, `Flags_TitleCase`, `Flags_UnannouncedCharacter`, `Flags_FocusCharacter`, `Announce_Validation`, `Deliver_Validation`) are present, and none of them uses PostgresFixture or Testcontainers (TR-68).

`Transitions_Table` asserts `IsLegal` is true for exactly the eight TR-4 triples out of the 336-triple cross product and false for all others, and that `IsTerminal` is true for Done, Failed, TimedOut, Cancelled and false for Waiting, Working (TR-68, TR-5).

`Flags_CharacterAbsent` asserts exactly one `CharacterAbsent` flag with message `expected character 'BMO' not found` and that a character present only in the transcript is not flagged; `Flags_TitleCase` asserts no `TitleMismatch` for `"the unfinished map "` vs `"The Unfinished Map"` and one for `"The Unfinished Map (Part 1)"`; `Flags_UnannouncedCharacter` asserts `UnannouncedCharacter` for Marceline only; `Flags_FocusCharacter` asserts `FocusCharacterMismatch` for null delivered focus and zero flags for an identical delivery (TR-68, TR-24).

`Announce_Validation` asserts the error keys `focusCharacter`, `ttlSeconds` (for both 59 and 86401), `requestedStages`, `title`, `expectedCharacters` for the respective inputs and that a body containing `transcriptText` throws `System.Text.Json.JsonException` on deserialization into `AnnounceManifestRequest` (TR-68, TR-16).

`Deliver_Validation` asserts that one `Validate` call over a request with whitespace transcript, null title, null airDate, runtimeMinutes 0 and season 12 (manifest 11) returns all of `title is required`, `transcriptText is required`, `airDate is required`, `runtimeMinutes must be > 0`, `season 12 does not match manifest season 11`; a second call covers NUL-only transcript and a >200-character title; a valid request asserts NUL stripped in `Normalized.TranscriptText` and `Normalized.RuntimeMinutes == 11.0` (TR-68, TR-19).

`DeliverEpisodeRequestBindingTests` deserializes all 21 files under the test output's `Episodes/` folder into `DeliverEpisodeRequest` without exception and `DeliveryValidator.Validate` returns zero reasons for each against a manifest built from the file's own season/episodeNumber (TR-19).

AdventureTime.Tests.csproj contains the `<Content Include="..\AdventureTime\Episodes\*.json" ...>` item and `dotnet build AdventureTime.Tests` copies 21 json files into the output `Episodes/` directory (TR-68).

tickets.title: Add Stub_Deterministic unit test for StubDeepAnalysisService
tickets.context: The last row of the unit-test table: the stub must be deterministic.
tickets.motivation: Determinism is what makes end-to-end assertions stable. Two fresh instances given the same episode must produce identical scores and the same continuity note, or seeding results would differ run to run.
tickets.goal: A test constructing two instances and asserting identical output for the same input.
tickets.value: Seeding and end-to-end tests are reproducible, which is the whole reason the stub exists.
tickets.description: Add AdventureTime.Tests/Unit/StubDeepAnalysisServiceTests.cs covering the last row of TR-68 against the `StubDeepAnalysisService` from F1.2 (TR-47, AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Services/StubDeepAnalysisService.cs). Construct two fresh instances and call `AnalyzeEpisodeAsync` with an `Episode` for Season 11, EpisodeNumber 4 (seed = 1104): both must return identical `Sentiment` scores and `DominantEmotion` (`Sentiment` is the `OverallSentiment` sub-model in AdventureTime.Application/Models/EpisodeAnalysis/SubModels/OverallSentiment.cs), and the values must match the TR-47 formulas (`PositivityScore = 1104 % 100 / 100.0 = 4/100.0`, `IntensityScore = (1104/7 % 100) / 100.0 = 57/100.0`, `ComplexityScore = (1104/13 % 100) / 100.0 = 84/100.0`, emotion index `1104 % 6 = 0`, i.e. the first entry of the stub's six-entry list). Call the continuity overload with a `ContinuityContext` whose first `PriorEpisodeSummary` is S11E03 'Low Battery' and assert `ContinuityNotes == ["follows S11E03 'Low Battery'"]`; with `new ContinuityContext(Priors: [])` assert `ContinuityNotes` is empty. For cancellation, set the internal static `StubDeepAnalysisService.StubDelay` to 30 seconds and pass an already-cancelled token, asserting `OperationCanceledException` (or its subclass `TaskCanceledException`) is thrown and the call returns promptly; restore `StubDelay` to `TimeSpan.Zero` in a `finally`. `StubDelay` is reachable only through the `InternalsVisibleTo("AdventureTime.Tests")` of TR-51 (F1.1), which the test project of F2.4-T1 already relies on; if it is missing this file must fail to compile rather than skip.
