features.title: Manifest commands, handlers and the analysis queue
features.summary: Extend `FailureType` with `NotFound, Gone, Unprocessable, StationFull, WrongState` and add `Commands/Manifests/{AnnounceManifest,DeliverEpisode,CancelManifest}` and `Queries/Manifests/{GetManifest,GetStation}` plus `Queries/Episodes/GetAllEpisodesQuery`, following the `CreateEpisodeCommandHandler` result idiom. The deliver handler implements the ordered fulfilment check (id-scoped ExpireOverdue, re-read, validate, flags, `TryBeginWorkAsync`, then `IAnalysisQueue.TryEnqueue` with no request token, then a re-read for the 202 body; 0 rows → re-read and map). Includes `IAnalysisQueue` and the bounded `Channel<Guid>(64, Wait, SingleReader)` `AnalysisQueue` singleton so the handler has a real signal target, and the `GetEpisodeByIdQueryHandler` cleanup. Handlers depend only on `IStationStore`, `IOptions<StationOptions>`, `ILogger` (and the queue).

tickets.title: Extend FailureType and add IAnalysisQueue with the bounded AnalysisQueue singleton
tickets.context: The existing result idiom knows three failure kinds. The station introduces five more, each of which maps to a distinct HTTP status. There is also no queue for the worker.
tickets.motivation: Extending the enum lets the controllers map outcomes mechanically instead of with special cases. The bounded channel is the wake-up signal from a committed delivery to the worker; it is deliberately not the source of truth, which is why a failed enqueue is logged and left for the orphan scan rather than retried.
tickets.goal: Five new failure types and an IAnalysisQueue with its bounded singleton implementation.
tickets.value: Status-code mapping stays uniform across old and new endpoints, and the worker has a low-latency signal without the design depending on it.
tickets.description: Extend the enum in /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Application/Enums/FailureType.cs with `NotFound, Gone, Unprocessable, StationFull, WrongState` after the existing `Conflict, ValidationFailed, InternalError` (TR-26); the existing `CreateEpisodeResult` factories keep compiling. Add `AdventureTime.Application/Interfaces/IAnalysisQueue.cs` declaring exactly `bool TryEnqueue(Guid sessionId);` and `ChannelReader<Guid> Reader { get; }` (TR-31); `System.Threading.Channels` is in the shared framework and `Microsoft.Extensions.Options`/`Logging.Abstractions` already resolve into the Application project transitively via MediatR 13.0.0, so no package change is needed here. Add `AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/AnalysisQueue.cs` (new folder; F2.x also puts `StationSql`/`StationStore` there) as `public sealed class AnalysisQueue : IAnalysisQueue` wrapping `Channel.CreateBounded<Guid>(new BoundedChannelOptions(64) { FullMode = BoundedChannelFullMode.Wait, SingleReader = true })`, with `TryEnqueue` = `_channel.Writer.TryWrite(sessionId)` and `Reader` = `_channel.Reader` (TR-42). Gotcha: `Wait` mode is mandatory because it is the only mode in which `TryWrite` really returns false when the channel is full, which is what makes the Warning path of TR-31 observable; `DropWrite`/`DropOldest`/`DropNewest` return true and discard silently and MUST NOT be used. Register the singleton in `AddInfrastructure` in /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs with `services.AddSingleton<IAnalysisQueue, AnalysisQueue>()` (after the `IStationStore` registration once F2.x adds it) so the deliver handler resolves through MediatR; this is the queue line of TR-49, and F5.1 appends the hosted services after it. The worker that reads the channel is F5.2; this ticket only provides the signal target.
acceptance_criteria: `AdventureTime.Application/Enums/FailureType.cs` contains exactly the members `Conflict, ValidationFailed, InternalError, NotFound, Gone, Unprocessable, StationFull, WrongState` and `dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` succeeds with no new warnings (TR-26)
`AdventureTime.Application/Interfaces/IAnalysisQueue.cs` declares `bool TryEnqueue(Guid sessionId);` and `ChannelReader<Guid> Reader { get; }` and no other members (TR-31)

`AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/AnalysisQueue.cs` constructs the channel with `Channel.CreateBounded<Guid>(new BoundedChannelOptions(64) { FullMode = BoundedChannelFullMode.Wait, SingleReader = true })` and `TryEnqueue` returns the result of `Writer.TryWrite` (TR-42)
`grep -rn "DropWrite\|DropOldest\|DropNewest" AdventureTime.Infrastructure AdventureTime.Application` returns nothing (TR-42)

Calling `TryEnqueue` 65 times on a fresh `AnalysisQueue` returns `true` 64 times and `false` on the 65th, and after one `Reader.TryRead` the next `TryEnqueue` returns `true` again; the permanent form of this check is the test `AnalysisQueue_IsBoundedAt64_WithWaitMode` of F3.2-T6, a temporary test is acceptable until then (TR-42)

`AddInfrastructure` contains `services.AddSingleton<IAnalysisQueue, AnalysisQueue>()`; resolving `IAnalysisQueue` twice from the built `ServiceProvider` returns the same instance (queue registration line of TR-49; F5.1 completes the hosted-service ordering)

tickets.title: Add AnnounceValidator, AnnounceManifestCommand, result and handler
tickets.context: The first MediatR handler for the station, following the existing command, result and handler idiom.
tickets.motivation: Announce is validation, then the store's admission transaction, then mapping the outcome to a result. Keeping to the existing idiom means the controller switch looks like the one that already exists and a reviewer sees nothing novel.
tickets.goal: Command, result with factories for each outcome, and a handler that calls the validator and the store in that order.
tickets.value: Announcing a manifest becomes reachable through the same pattern as everything else in the codebase.
tickets.description: Create `AdventureTime.Application/Commands/Manifests/AnnounceManifest/` with `AnnounceManifestCommand.cs` (`public sealed record AnnounceManifestCommand(AnnounceManifestRequest Request) : IRequest<AnnounceManifestResult>`), `AnnounceManifestResult.cs` and `AnnounceManifestCommandHandler.cs`, following `Commands/Episodes/CreateEpisode/CreateEpisodeResult.cs` (private constructor, `IsSuccess`, `FailureType?`, `ErrorMessage`, `ValidationErrors`, static factories) and `CreateEpisodeCommandHandler.cs` (try/catch -> `InternalError` with an Error log). The result carries `AnnounceManifestResponse? Response` plus the TR-26 extras `ConflictingManifestId`, `ConflictingState`, `ConflictingEpisodeId`, `Occupancy`, `EarliestExpiry`, `RetryAfterSeconds`, with factories `Success(response)`, `ValidationFailed(Dictionary<string,string[]>)` (message `validation failed`, the TR-16 body text), `LiveConflict(Guid manifestId, SessionState state, int season, int episodeNumber)` (message `a live manifest exists for S{season:D2}E{episodeNumber:D2}`), `EpisodeExists(int)` (`episode exists`), `Full(int occupancy, DateTime? earliestExpiry, int retryAfterSeconds)` and `InternalError`. Put the handler-level rules of TR-16 in a pure `public static class AnnounceValidator` with `Validate(AnnounceManifestRequest request, StationOptions options) : Dictionary<string, string[]>` in `AdventureTime.Application/Station/AnnounceValidator.cs`: keys `title`, `expectedCharacters`, `focusCharacter`, `requestedStages`, `ttlSeconds`; ttl message `must be between {TtlMin} and {TtlMax}`; focus character matched ordinal-ignore-case after trim; stage names a subset of `Sentiment, CharacterMoods, Relationships, Themes, StoryArc, KeyMoments`; every failure collected in one call (the `Announce_Validation` test of TR-68 in F3.1 targets it). The handler (constructor `(IStationStore, IOptions<StationOptions>, ILogger<AnnounceManifestCommandHandler>)`, options read once in the constructor per A4) returns `ValidationFailed` when the dictionary is non-empty, otherwise applies defaults (`requestedStages` = all six, `ttlSeconds` = `TtlDefault`, `expectedLocations` = `[]`), trims `title`, every character/location entry and `focusCharacter`, and builds a `Session` candidate with `Id = Guid.CreateVersion7()`, `State = SessionState.Waiting`, `TtlSeconds` set and no timestamp assigned (TR-12: `AnnouncedAt`/`ExpiresAt` come from SQL `now()`). It calls `IStationStore.AnnounceAsync(candidate, options.Capacity, ct)` once and maps `Admitted` -> `Success` (response `{ id, state "Waiting", expiresAt = Admitted.ExpiresAt, occupancy = Admitted.Occupancy, capacity = options.Capacity }`), `LiveConflict`/`EpisodeExists` -> `Conflict` with the extras, `Full` -> `StationFull`; it MUST NOT count occupancy itself (TR-27) and logs 409/429 refusals at Information with occupancy and retry-after (TR-64, owned by F5.3). DTOs come from F3.1 (TR-23), `AnnounceOutcome` from F2.1 (TR-32), `StationOptions` from F1.1 (TR-35).
acceptance_criteria: `AnnounceValidator.Validate` returns, in one call, the keys `title` (blank after trim), `expectedCharacters` (a blank entry), `focusCharacter` (not an entry of expectedCharacters, ordinal-ignore-case, trimmed), `requestedStages` (unknown name), `ttlSeconds` (59 -> `must be between 60 and 86400`; 86401 likewise with the defaults of TR-35) and returns an empty dictionary for the TR-16 example request (TR-27)

`AnnounceManifestCommandHandler.Handle` returns `FailureType.ValidationFailed` with `ErrorMessage == "validation failed"` and `ValidationErrors` containing every failed key when several rules fail, and never calls `IStationStore.AnnounceAsync` in that case (TR-27)

On a valid request the `Session` passed to `AnnounceAsync` has `Id.Version == 7`, `State == Waiting`, trimmed `Title`/`FocusCharacter`/entries, `RequestedStages` equal to the six default names when omitted, `TtlSeconds == options.TtlDefault` when omitted, `ExpectedLocations` empty when omitted, and `AnnouncedAt`/`ExpiresAt` left at `default` (TR-27, TR-12)
The second argument of `AnnounceAsync` equals `StationOptions.Capacity`, and the handler source contains no call to any store method other than `AnnounceAsync` and no `count` query of its own (TR-27)

`Admitted(id, expiresAt, 2)` maps to `IsSuccess == true` with `Response.Occupancy == 2`, `Response.Capacity == options.Capacity`, `Response.ExpiresAt == expiresAt`, `Response.State == "Waiting"`; `LiveConflict` and `EpisodeExists` map to `FailureType.Conflict` with `ConflictingManifestId`/`ConflictingState` or `ConflictingEpisodeId` set and `ErrorMessage` `a live manifest exists for S11E01` / `episode exists`; `Full(3, exp, 412)` maps to `FailureType.StationFull` with `Occupancy == 3`, `EarliestExpiry == exp`, `RetryAfterSeconds == 412` (TR-26, TR-27)

A store that throws yields `FailureType.InternalError` and an Error log entry, and the handler class resolves from the MediatR container with only `IStationStore`, `IOptions<StationOptions>` and `ILogger<AnnounceManifestCommandHandler>` as constructor parameters (TR-26)

tickets.title: Add DeliverEpisodeCommand, result and handler with the ordered fulfilment check
tickets.context: The fulfilment check, the bouncer at the door. This is the most order-sensitive handler in the system.
tickets.motivation: Expire by id, re-read, validate, compute flags, attempt the Waiting-to-Working transition, re-read, and only then enqueue with a token that cannot be cancelled by a departing client. That exact order is what makes the status code depend on the session's real state rather than on timing, and the post-commit enqueue with CancellationToken.None is the first line of defense against a Working row with no worker.
tickets.goal: A handler that executes the sequence exactly, returning every 422 reason at once and building the 202 body from a re-read.
tickets.value: The one door into processing behaves identically whether the sweeper ran a second ago or not, and a delivery that commits is never lost to a client disconnect.
tickets.description: Create `AdventureTime.Application/Commands/Manifests/DeliverEpisode/` with `DeliverEpisodeCommand.cs` (`public sealed record DeliverEpisodeCommand(Guid Id, DeliverEpisodeRequest Request) : IRequest<DeliverEpisodeResult>`), `DeliverEpisodeResult.cs` (private constructor; `IsSuccess`, `FailureType?`, `ErrorMessage`, `DeliverEpisodeResponse? Response`, extras `SessionState? State`, `IReadOnlyList<string> Reasons`, `DateTime? ExpiresAt`; factories `Success(response)`, `NotFound()` = `manifest not found`, `Gone(DateTime expiresAt)` = `manifest expired`, `WrongState(SessionState state)` = `already fulfilled` for Working/Done, `cancelled` for Cancelled, `re-announce` for Failed per TR-20, `Unprocessable(IReadOnlyList<string> reasons)` = `delivery rejected`, `InternalError`) and `DeliverEpisodeCommandHandler.cs` with constructor `(IStationStore, IAnalysisQueue, IOptions<StationOptions>, ILogger<DeliverEpisodeCommandHandler>)`, the whole `Handle` body in try/catch -> `InternalError` with an Error log as in `CreateEpisodeCommandHandler`. `Handle` performs TR-28 strictly in order: (1) `ExpireOverdueAsync(id, ct)`; (2) `GetAsync(id, ct)` -> null `NotFound`, TimedOut `Gone(session.ExpiresAt)`, Working/Done/Cancelled/Failed `WrongState`; (3) `DeliveryValidator.Validate(session, request)` -> any reasons: `Unprocessable` with all of them, nothing written; (4) `EpisodeMapper.ToEpisode(normalized, id)` serialized with `StationJson.Options` to `payloadJson`, `FulfilmentFlags.Compute(session, normalized)` serialized with the same options to `flagsJson`; (5) `TryBeginWorkAsync(id, payloadJson, flagsJson, ct)`. On true: call `_queue.TryEnqueue(id)` (synchronous, no token), log Warning `TryEnqueue returned false for session {SessionId}; orphan scan will adopt it` when it returns false and continue as success, then `GetAsync(id, CancellationToken.None)` and build `DeliverEpisodeResponse { SessionId, State = "Working", Flags = deserialize(session.Flags, StationJson.Options) ?? [], WorkingDeadlineAt = session.WorkingDeadlineAt }` from that re-read. On false: `ExpireOverdueAsync(id, CancellationToken.None)`, `GetAsync(id, CancellationToken.None)`, map null -> `NotFound`, TimedOut -> `Gone`, any other terminal state or Working -> `WrongState`, and Waiting -> `InternalError` logged at Error (unreachable: statement-level `now()` is monotone). Gotchas: MediatR hands the handler `HttpContext.RequestAborted` as `ct`, so every call after `TryBeginWorkAsync` (enqueue, re-reads, fallback expire) MUST use `CancellationToken.None` (TR-31, TR-62); `TryBeginWorkAsync` is a single autocommit statement (TR-39), so the enqueue is after commit by construction; the write is never retried (TR-3). Pure functions and DTOs are from F3.1 (TR-23..TR-25), store methods from F2.1/F2.3, the queue from F3.2-T1; the recording `FakeStationStore` of F3.2-T6 is the intended verification vehicle for the criteria below.
acceptance_criteria: With a recording `IStationStore` fake, a Waiting session and a valid delivery, the recorded call sequence is exactly `ExpireOverdueAsync(id)`, `GetAsync(id)`, `TryBeginWorkAsync(id, payloadJson, flagsJson)`, `GetAsync(id)`, the id is readable from `IAnalysisQueue.Reader` after `TryBeginWorkAsync` returned true, and `Response.WorkingDeadlineAt`/`Response.Flags` equal the values of the second `GetAsync` result (TR-28, TR-31)

`payloadJson` passed to `TryBeginWorkAsync` deserializes with `StationJson.Options` to an `Episode` with `Id == 0`, `SessionId == id` and the delivered (trimmed, defaulted) values; `flagsJson` is a camelCase array of `{code, message}` (TR-28, TR-7)

Pre-read outcomes: `GetAsync` null -> `FailureType.NotFound`; TimedOut -> `FailureType.Gone` with `ExpiresAt` set; Working, Done, Cancelled, Failed -> `FailureType.WrongState` with `State` set and `ErrorMessage` `already fulfilled`/`already fulfilled`/`cancelled`/`re-announce`; in all these cases `TryBeginWorkAsync` is never called and the queue stays empty (TR-28, TR-26)

A delivery with `season = 12` against manifest season 11 and a missing `transcriptText` returns `FailureType.Unprocessable` with `ErrorMessage == "delivery rejected"` and `Reasons` containing both `season 12 does not match manifest season 11` and `transcriptText is required`, and neither `TryBeginWorkAsync` nor `TryEnqueue` is called (TR-28)

When `TryBeginWorkAsync` returns false the recorded calls continue with `ExpireOverdueAsync(id)` then `GetAsync(id)` (no second `TryBeginWorkAsync`), the queue stays empty, and the re-read maps TimedOut -> `Gone`, Working/Done -> `WrongState`, null -> `NotFound`, Waiting -> `FailureType.InternalError` with an Error log entry (TR-28, TR-3)

When `TryEnqueue` returns false (real `AnalysisQueue` pre-filled with 64 ids) the handler still returns `IsSuccess == true` and emits exactly one Warning log entry whose message contains the session id (TR-31)
A store that throws from any step yields `FailureType.InternalError` and an Error log entry, and nothing is enqueued (TR-26)

The handler source passes `CancellationToken.None` to every store call made after `TryBeginWorkAsync` and never passes a token to `TryEnqueue`; the handler resolves from the MediatR container with only `IStationStore`, `IAnalysisQueue`, `IOptions<StationOptions>` and `ILogger<DeliverEpisodeCommandHandler>` (TR-31, TR-26)

tickets.title: Add CancelManifestCommand, result and handler with idempotent 0-row fallback
tickets.context: Cancellation is the only sender-initiated way to release a slot before the TTL runs out.
tickets.motivation: A mistaken announcement should not hold a slot for half an hour. The transition is a single conditional update; the zero-row fallback re-reads and returns idempotent success when the session is already cancelled, so a retried DELETE is harmless.
tickets.goal: Command, result and handler with the idempotent fallback.
tickets.value: The backpressure story is complete: senders can give slots back, and the station recovers capacity without waiting for the janitor.
tickets.description: Create `AdventureTime.Application/Commands/Manifests/CancelManifest/` with `CancelManifestCommand.cs` (`public sealed record CancelManifestCommand(Guid Id) : IRequest<CancelManifestResult>`), `CancelManifestResult.cs` (private constructor; `IsSuccess`, `FailureType?`, `ErrorMessage`, extra `SessionState? State`; factories `Success()`, `NotFound()` with message `manifest not found`, `WrongState(SessionState state)` with message `cannot cancel`, `InternalError`) and `CancelManifestCommandHandler.cs` with constructor `(IStationStore, ILogger<CancelManifestCommandHandler>)` (it needs no options; TR-26 allows the subset). `Handle` implements TR-29: `CancelAsync(id, ct)` true -> `Success`; false -> `ExpireOverdueAsync(id, ct)` (id-scoped, so a Waiting row past its TTL is reported as TimedOut rather than retried), then `GetAsync(id, ct)`: null -> `NotFound`, `Cancelled` -> `Success` (idempotent second DELETE), any other state (Working, Done, Failed, TimedOut) -> `WrongState(state)`. The write is never retried and the handler never inspects the clock itself: `Cancel` has no clock predicate (TR-18), so the expire-then-re-read fallback is the only place TimedOut can surface. Wrap in try/catch -> `InternalError` with an Error log as in `CreateEpisodeCommandHandler`. F4.1 maps `Success` -> 204, `NotFound` -> 404, `WrongState` -> 409 `{ message: "cannot cancel", state }`.
acceptance_criteria: With a recording `IStationStore` fake whose `CancelAsync` returns true, the result is `IsSuccess == true` and the only recorded call is `CancelAsync(id)` (TR-29)
When `CancelAsync` returns false the recorded sequence is `CancelAsync(id)`, `ExpireOverdueAsync(id)`, `GetAsync(id)` with exactly one `CancelAsync` call (TR-29, TR-3)

0-row re-read of `Cancelled` -> `IsSuccess == true` (idempotent); re-read null -> `FailureType.NotFound` with `ErrorMessage == "manifest not found"`; re-read `TimedOut`, `Working`, `Done`, `Failed` -> `FailureType.WrongState` with `State` equal to that state and `ErrorMessage == "cannot cancel"` (TR-29, TR-26)
A store exception yields `FailureType.InternalError` and an Error log entry (TR-26)

The handler resolves from the MediatR container with exactly the constructor parameters `IStationStore` and `ILogger<CancelManifestCommandHandler>`, and `dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` succeeds (TR-26)

tickets.title: Add GetManifest, GetStation and GetAllEpisodes query handlers; clean GetEpisodeByIdQueryHandler
tickets.context: Read paths for the API, plus cleanup of the existing query handler and the episodes controller's direct use of the DbContext.
tickets.motivation: After a 202 the only way a sender learns the outcome is by polling the manifest, so GET must expose state, reason, flags and, once Done, the episode id. Moving GetAll behind MediatR lets the episodes controller stop injecting AppDbContext, and removing the unused analysis service from the existing handler is overdue.
tickets.goal: Three query handlers and a cleaned-up existing handler.
tickets.value: Polling has something meaningful to poll, the operator board is one request away, and the web layer no longer reaches into EF.
tickets.description: Create `AdventureTime.Application/Queries/Manifests/GetManifestQuery/` (`public sealed record GetManifestQuery(Guid Id) : IRequest<ManifestResponse?>`, `GetManifestQueryHandler`), `AdventureTime.Application/Queries/Manifests/GetStationQuery/` (`public sealed record GetStationQuery() : IRequest<StationResponse>`, `GetStationQueryHandler`) and `AdventureTime.Application/Queries/Episodes/GetAllEpisodesQuery/` (`public sealed record GetAllEpisodesQuery() : IRequest<IReadOnlyList<Episode>>`, `GetAllEpisodesQueryHandler`), each folder named after its query exactly like the existing `Queries/Episodes/GetEpisodeByIdQuery/`. `GetManifestQueryHandler` (constructor `(IStationStore, ILogger<GetManifestQueryHandler>)`) calls `GetAsync(id, ct)` (null -> handler returns null; F4.1 maps to 404 `manifest not found`), deserializes `Flags` with `StationJson.Options` (null -> `[]`), and builds the TR-17 shape: every column except `DeliveryPayload` (which `GetAsync` already projects as NULL), `links.self = /api/manifests/{id}` always, `links.deliver = /api/manifests/{id}/episode` only when Waiting, and only when state is Done calls `FindEpisodeIdBySessionAsync(id, ct)` to set `episodeId`, `links.episode = /api/episodes/{episodeId}`, `links.analysis = /api/episodes/{episodeId}/analysis` (TR-30); a null result in the Done case is unreachable under invariant I7, so leave the three fields null and log a Warning rather than throw. `GetStationQueryHandler` (constructor `(IStationStore, IOptions<StationOptions>, ILogger<GetStationQueryHandler>)`) calls `GetStationViewAsync(options.Capacity, ct)` once and maps the view 1:1 into `StationResponse` (`capacity`, `occupancy`, `live`, `recent` per TR-21) without issuing any other store call; `occupancy` is copied from the view's TR-2 SQL count and MUST NOT be derived by the handler (not even as `live.Count`). `GetAllEpisodesQueryHandler` (constructor `(IEpisodeRepository)`) returns `await _episodeRepository.GetAllAsync(null, ct)`; it replaces the direct `_context.Episodes.OrderBy(...)` query in `AdventureTime/Controllers/EpisodesController.cs` `GetAll`, which F4.2 rewires (`EpisodeRepository.GetAllAsync` already orders by season then episode number). Finally edit `AdventureTime.Application/Queries/Episodes/GetEpisodeByIdQuery/GetEpisodeByIdQueryHandler.cs`: the constructor becomes `(IEpisodeRepository episodeRepository)`, and the unused `IDeepAnalysisService` parameter, the `_deepAnalysisService` field, the never-assigned `_episodeAnalysisRepository` field and the commented-out analysis line are removed (TR-26). DTOs `ManifestResponse`/`ManifestLinks`/`StationResponse` come from F3.1 (TR-23); `StationView`, `GetStationViewAsync` and `FindEpisodeIdBySessionAsync` are on the `IStationStore` contract of F2.1 (TR-32) and implemented by F2.3.

tickets.title: Unit-test manifest handlers and AnalysisQueue with a recording fake IStationStore
tickets.context: Handler tests against a recording fake of the store, without Postgres.
tickets.motivation: The deliver handler's call sequence is the behavior most likely to regress in a refactor, and a recording fake can assert it call by call. The same fake proves each handler's outcome mapping and that enqueue happens after, not before, the transition.
tickets.goal: A recording fake store, a list logger, and tests for the four handlers and the queue.
tickets.value: Fast, deterministic coverage of the fulfilment order, so a reordering that would change status-code behavior or lose deliveries is caught before it reaches an integration run.
tickets.description: In the `AdventureTime.Tests` project created by F2.4 (TR-67), add `Application/FakeStationStore.cs` (an `IStationStore` implementation that records every call as a string in `List<string> Calls`, exposes scriptable results — `Queue<Session?> GetResults`, `bool TryBeginWorkResult`, `bool CancelResult`, `AnnounceOutcome AnnounceResult`, `int? EpisodeIdBySession`, `StationView StationViewResult` — and captures the last `payloadJson`/`flagsJson`/`candidate`/`capacity` arguments), `Application/ListLogger.cs` (an `ILogger<T>` that collects `(LogLevel, message)` pairs) and `Application/ManifestHandlerTests.cs`. These tests run without Postgres and pin the handler contracts of TR-27..TR-31 and the queue bound of TR-42; the store's own behavior is covered by F2.4. Tests to write: `Deliver_HappyPath_CallsInOrderAndEnqueuesAfterTryBeginWork` (sequence `ExpireOverdue(id)`, `GetAsync`, `TryBeginWork`, `GetAsync`; id readable from a real `AnalysisQueue.Reader`; response built from the second read); `Deliver_PreRead_NotFound_Gone_WrongState` (theory over null/TimedOut/Working/Done/Cancelled/Failed; no `TryBeginWork`, queue empty); `Deliver_Unprocessable_ReturnsAllReasonsAndWritesNothing`; `Deliver_ZeroRows_RereadsOnce` (theory: TimedOut -> Gone, Done -> WrongState, null -> NotFound, Waiting -> InternalError; exactly one `TryBeginWork` call, queue empty); `Deliver_EnqueueFalse_IsWarningNotFailure` (real `AnalysisQueue` pre-filled with 64 ids); `AnalysisQueue_IsBoundedAt64_WithWaitMode` (64 true, 65th false, true again after one read); `Cancel_TrueIsSuccess`, `Cancel_ZeroRows_Cancelled_IsIdempotentSuccess`, `Cancel_ZeroRows_TimedOut_IsWrongState`, `Cancel_ZeroRows_Null_IsNotFound`; `Announce_CollectsEveryValidationKey`, `Announce_BuildsCandidateWithVersion7IdAndDefaults`, `Announce_MapsOutcomes` (Admitted/LiveConflict/EpisodeExists/Full) and `Announce_PassesOptionsCapacityAndNeverCounts`; `GetManifest_LinksByState` and `GetStation_MapsViewOnce`. Use `Options.Create(new StationOptions())` for options. Gotcha: `Session` timestamps in fixtures are arbitrary `DateTime`s; the handlers never read the clock, so no `TimeProvider` is needed here.

epics.title: HTTP surface: manifests API and direct-ingestion removal
epics.goal: With curl against the running API, every status code of section 7 is reproducible — 201/400/409/429 on announce, 404/410/409/422/202 on delivery, 204/409 on cancel, the operator view at `GET /api/station` — while `POST api/Episodes` answers 410 and the external React viewer still works against the two episode GETs.

features.title: Manifests and station controllers
features.summary: Add `AdventureTime/Controllers/ManifestsController.cs` (`api/manifests`: Announce, Get, Cancel, Deliver with `{id:guid}` routes and `[RequestSizeLimit(4_194_304)]`) and `StationController.cs` (`api/station`), injecting only `IMediator` and `ILogger`. Map `FailureType` to status per TR-52, emit `CreatedAtAction`/`AcceptedAtAction` Location headers, set `Retry-After` on 429, and shape every body exactly as sections 7.1–7.5 specify (links present only in the right states, `flags` `[]` before delivery, `DeliveryPayload` never returned). Owns the API conventions of TR-15, including keeping `[ApiController]` automatic 400 so that announce DTO faults are 400 while every delivery content problem is a 422. Verified by curl/Swagger against a compose stack.

tickets.title: Add ManifestsController Announce/Get actions and FailureType status map
tickets.context: The first controller for the station. The existing episodes controller injects the DbContext and the analysis service directly; the new controllers inject only the mediator and a logger, which is the layering rule the whole HTTP epic enforces.
tickets.motivation: The HTTP surface is how announcers experience the admission mechanism. The status map is where backpressure becomes visible: a 429 with Retry-After is the cheap no the design promises, and a 409 naming the manifest that holds the slot is what lets a sender act instead of guess. Keeping the controller thin means every outcome the handler can produce has exactly one status.
tickets.goal: Announce and Get actions with the complete failure-type to status mapping, a Location header on 201, and Retry-After on 429.
tickets.value: A sender learns the station is full before it ships a transcript, as a real HTTP signal it can back off on. The web layer stays a thin, replaceable adapter over the handlers.
tickets.description: Create `AdventureTime/Controllers/ManifestsController.cs` (`[ApiController] [Route("api/manifests")]`, constructor `(IMediator, ILogger<ManifestsController>)` only; never `AppDbContext`, `IStationStore`, `IDeepAnalysisService` or `IOptions<StationOptions>`). Implement `[HttpPost] Announce([FromBody] AnnounceManifestRequest)` sending `AnnounceManifestCommand` and `[HttpGet("{id:guid}")] Get(Guid id)` sending `GetManifestQuery` (handlers from F3.2: `AnnounceManifestCommandHandler`, `GetManifestQueryHandler`), plus one private `ToStatus(FailureType?)` used by every action: ValidationFailed 400, NotFound 404, Conflict/WrongState 409, Gone 410, Unprocessable 422, StationFull 429, InternalError/null 500 (TR-52). Follow the `EpisodesController.CreateEpisode` switch idiom but shape bodies exactly per TRD 7.1/7.2: 201 via `CreatedAtAction(nameof(Get), new { id = result.Response.Id }, result.Response)` (this yields an absolute `Location` ending in `/api/manifests/{id}`); 400 `{ message = "validation failed", errors = result.ValidationErrors }`; 409 `{ message = result.ErrorMessage, manifestId = result.ConflictingManifestId, state = result.ConflictingState }` when `ConflictingManifestId` is set, else `{ message = "episode exists", episodeId = result.ConflictingEpisodeId }`; 429 sets `Response.Headers.RetryAfter = result.RetryAfterSeconds.ToString()` and returns `{ capacity = result.Capacity, occupancy = result.Occupancy, earliestExpiry = result.EarliestExpiry }` — the controller never computes occupancy or reads options, so `AnnounceManifestResult` (in `AdventureTime.Application/Commands/Manifests/AnnounceManifest/`, F3.2) must expose `Capacity` set by the handler's `StationFull` factory from `IOptions<StationOptions>`; add that property if F3.2 did not (TR-26 lists `Occupancy`, `EarliestExpiry`, `RetryAfterSeconds` but the 7.1 body also needs capacity). Get returns 200 with the `ManifestResponse` or 404 `{ message = "manifest not found" }`. Gotchas: in `AdventureTime/Program.cs` extend `builder.Services.AddControllers()` with `.AddJsonOptions(o => o.JsonSerializerOptions.Converters.Add(new JsonStringEnumConverter()))` so `state` serializes as `"Waiting"` not `0` (no enum exists in today's `Episode`/`EpisodeAnalysis` responses, so the viewer's payloads are unchanged); do NOT set a global `DefaultIgnoreCondition` (TR-17 keeps `reason: null` present) — instead ensure `ManifestResponse.EpisodeId` and `ManifestLinks.Episode/Analysis/Deliver` (in `AdventureTime.Application/Dtos/Manifests/`, from F3.1) carry `[JsonIgnore(Condition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull)]`, adding them if F3.1 did not. Do NOT touch `ApiBehaviorOptions` (`SuppressModelStateInvalidFilter` stays false) or `SuppressImplicitRequiredAttributeForNonNullableReferenceTypes` (TR-15).
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` succeeds and `AdventureTime/Controllers/ManifestsController.cs` injects exactly `IMediator` and `ILogger<ManifestsController>` (`grep -n "AppDbContext\|IStationStore\|IDeepAnalysisService\|IOptions<" AdventureTime/Controllers/ManifestsController.cs` returns nothing) (TR-52)

`POST /api/manifests` with the TRD 7.1 example body returns 201 with a `Location` header ending in `/api/manifests/{id}` and body `{ id, state: "Waiting", expiresAt: "...Z", occupancy: 1, capacity: 3 }` — `state` is a string, `expiresAt` ends in `Z` (TR-16, TR-15)

`POST /api/manifests` with `ttlSeconds: 59` returns 400 `{ "message": "validation failed", "errors": { "ttlSeconds": ["must be between 60 and 86400"] } }`; a body with an extra `transcriptText` member or a missing `title` returns a framework 400 `ValidationProblemDetails` (TR-16, TR-15)

A second announce for the same (season, episodeNumber) returns 409 `{ message: "a live manifest exists for S11E01", manifestId, state: "Waiting" }` where `manifestId` equals the first announce's id; an announce for an episode already present in `"Episodes"` returns 409 `{ message: "episode exists", episodeId }` (TR-16)

With three live manifests (Capacity 3 from `appsettings.json`), a fourth `POST /api/manifests` returns 429 with header `Retry-After: <integer >= 1>` and body `{ capacity: 3, occupancy: 3, earliestExpiry: "...Z" }`, and no fourth row appears in `"Sessions"` (TR-16, TR-52)

`GET /api/manifests/{id}` on a Waiting manifest returns 200 whose JSON contains `flags: []`, `reason: null`, `links.self` and `links.deliver`, and does NOT contain the keys `episodeId`, `links.episode`, `links.analysis` or `deliveryPayload`; on a Done manifest (reached either with the F5.2 worker running, or by SQL `UPDATE "Sessions" SET "State"='Done', "EndedAt"=now(), "DeliveryPayload"=NULL WHERE "Id"='<id>'` plus `UPDATE "Episodes" SET "SessionId"='<id>' WHERE "Id"=<n>` on an existing episode) it contains `episodeId: n`, `links.episode: "/api/episodes/{n}"`, `links.analysis: "/api/episodes/{n}/analysis"` and no `links.deliver` (TR-17)
`GET /api/manifests/{unknown-guid}` returns 404 `{ "message": "manifest not found" }`; `GET /api/manifests/not-a-guid` returns 404 via the `{id:guid}` constraint (TR-17, TR-15)

`grep -n "SuppressModelStateInvalidFilter\|SuppressImplicitRequiredAttribute\|DefaultIgnoreCondition" AdventureTime/Program.cs` returns nothing and `grep -n "JsonStringEnumConverter" AdventureTime/Program.cs` returns one line (TR-15)

tickets.title: Add Cancel and Deliver actions to ManifestsController with 4 MB body limit
tickets.context: Extends the manifests controller with the sender-side release and the one door into processing. Delivery bodies carry full transcripts, so this is also where request size is bounded.
tickets.motivation: Five distinct outcomes on delivery, 404, 409, 410, 422 and 202, must each map to exactly one status regardless of whether the sweeper ran a second ago, or clients cannot be written correctly. Cancel must be idempotent so a retried DELETE is harmless. A four-megabyte limit protects Kestrel and the jsonb staging column from a pathological body.
tickets.goal: Cancel and Deliver actions with exact status and body shapes, and the request-size limit on delivery.
tickets.value: The whole manifest lifecycle is now reachable over HTTP with one code per cause. Senders can give slots back, and oversized deliveries are refused before they cost anything.
tickets.description: Extend `AdventureTime/Controllers/ManifestsController.cs` with `[HttpDelete("{id:guid}")] Cancel(Guid id)` sending `CancelManifestCommand(id)` and `[HttpPost("{id:guid}/episode")] [RequestSizeLimit(4_194_304)] Deliver(Guid id, [FromBody] DeliverEpisodeRequest request)` sending `DeliverEpisodeCommand(id, request)` (handlers `CancelManifestCommandHandler` and `DeliverEpisodeCommandHandler` from F3.2) (TR-52, TR-65). Cancel: success → `NoContent()` (the handler already treats an already-Cancelled re-read as success, so the second DELETE is 204 too); NotFound → 404 `{ message = "manifest not found" }`; WrongState → 409 `{ message = "cannot cancel", state = result.State }`; InternalError → 500 `{ message }` (TR-18). Deliver, using the shared `ToStatus` from F4.1-T1: NotFound → 404 `{ message = "manifest not found" }`; Gone → 410 `{ message = "manifest expired", state = "TimedOut", expiresAt = result.ExpiresAt }`; WrongState → 409 `{ message = result.ErrorMessage, state = result.State }` (handler supplies `already fulfilled` / `cancelled` / `re-announce`); Unprocessable → 422 `{ message = "delivery rejected", reasons = result.Reasons }`; success → `AcceptedAtAction(nameof(Get), new { id }, result.Response)` where the `DeliverEpisodeResponse` `{ sessionId, state: "Working", flags, workingDeadlineAt }` came from the handler's post-commit re-read (TR-20); the `Location` it emits is absolute and ends in `/api/manifests/{id}`. Gotchas: `DeliverEpisodeRequest` must stay annotation-free with nullable members (TR-19, owned by F3.1) so a body missing `transcriptText` reaches the handler and is a 422, never a framework 400 — do not add `[Required]` or `[BindRequired]` to it; malformed JSON is still a framework 400. Do not declare a `CancellationToken` parameter on either action and never pass `HttpContext.RequestAborted`; the action simply awaits `_mediator.Send(command)` (the handler owns the `CancellationToken.None` enqueue rule, TR-31/TR-62). Exceeding the 4 MB limit surfaces as a Kestrel 413 with an empty body before the action runs.
acceptance_criteria: `DELETE /api/manifests/{id}` on a Waiting manifest returns 204 with an empty body; repeating the same DELETE returns 204 again (idempotent) and `GET /api/manifests/{id}` shows `state: "Cancelled"`, `reason: "cancelled by announcer"` (TR-18)

`DELETE /api/manifests/{id}` on a Working or Done manifest returns 409 `{ "message": "cannot cancel", "state": "Working" }` (or `"Done"`); on an unknown GUID returns 404 `{ "message": "manifest not found" }` (TR-18)

`POST /api/manifests/{id}/episode` with `AdventureTime/Episodes/s11e01__the_unfinished_map.json` against a Waiting S11E01 manifest returns 202 with a `Location` header ending in `/api/manifests/{id}` and body `{ sessionId, state: "Working", flags: [...], workingDeadlineAt: "...Z" }` where `sessionId` equals `{id}` (TR-20)
The same delivery repeated returns 409 `{ "message": "already fulfilled", "state": "Working" }` (or `"Done"` when the F5.2 worker is running) (TR-20)

A delivery whose `season` is 12 against a season-11 manifest and whose `transcriptText` member is omitted returns 422 `{ "message": "delivery rejected", "reasons": [...] }` containing both `season 12 does not match manifest season 11` and `transcriptText is required`, and a subsequent `GET /api/manifests/{id}` still shows `state: "Waiting"` (TR-20, TR-15)

A delivery to a Waiting manifest whose `"ExpiresAt"` was set in the past by SQL (`UPDATE "Sessions" SET "ExpiresAt" = now() - interval '1 second' WHERE "Id"='<id>'`) returns 410 `{ "message": "manifest expired", "state": "TimedOut", "expiresAt": "...Z" }` without any sweeper running (TR-20)
A delivery to an unknown GUID returns 404 `{ "message": "manifest not found" }`; a delivery to `/api/manifests/abc/episode` returns 404 (route constraint) (TR-20, TR-15)

`Deliver` carries `[RequestSizeLimit(4_194_304)]` (grep) and a syntactically valid JSON body of 4.5 MB (the seed file with `transcriptText` padded) against a Waiting manifest is refused with 413 and the row stays Waiting, while a 3 MB padded body against a Waiting manifest is accepted with 202 (TR-65)

tickets.title: Add StationController exposing GET api/station
tickets.context: The operator's view of the station as a single GET, backed by the station-view query built in the store epic.
tickets.motivation: The visibility promise is that anyone can answer what is on the air, what is expected, and what went wrong without opening a database console. This is also how the seed script and a curious developer watch slots fill, expire and drain.
tickets.goal: GET /api/station returning capacity, derived occupancy, live sessions in announcement order, and the most recent terminal sessions with their reasons.
tickets.value: Operability from the API alone. During seeding and testing this endpoint is the running commentary on the mechanisms.
tickets.description: Create `AdventureTime/Controllers/StationController.cs` with `[ApiController] [Route("api/station")]`, constructor `(IMediator, ILogger<StationController>)`, and a single `[HttpGet] Get()` action that sends `GetStationQuery()` (handler `GetStationQueryHandler` from F3.2) and returns `Ok(response)` (TR-53). The `StationResponse` (from `AdventureTime.Application/Dtos/Manifests/`, F3.1) carries `capacity`, `occupancy`, `live[]` (Waiting/Working rows ordered by `announcedAt`, fields `id, state, season, episodeNumber, title, announcedAt, expiresAt, deliveredAt, workingDeadlineAt`) and `recent[]` (20 most recent terminal rows by `endedAt` desc, fields `id, state, season, episodeNumber, title, endedAt, reason`) — the handler builds it from `IStationStore.GetStationViewAsync`, so the controller adds nothing and must not inject `IStationStore` or `IOptions<StationOptions>`. Wrap the send in the same try/catch → `StatusCode(500, new { message = "An error occurred while reading the station" })` idiom as `EpisodesController.GetAll`; every other path is 200. Metadata only: no `flags`, no `deliveryPayload` in either array (TR-21, TR-65). This is the operator view named in TR-64; `/health` stays untouched. `state` serializes as a string through the `JsonStringEnumConverter` added in F4.1-T1.
acceptance_criteria: `GET /api/station` on an empty database returns 200 `{ "capacity": 3, "occupancy": 0, "live": [], "recent": [] }` (TR-53, TR-21)

After announcing two manifests, `GET /api/station` returns `occupancy: 2` and `live` with two entries ordered by `announcedAt` ascending, each containing exactly the keys `id, state, season, episodeNumber, title, announcedAt, expiresAt, deliveredAt, workingDeadlineAt` with `state: "Waiting"` and `deliveredAt`/`workingDeadlineAt` null (TR-21)

After cancelling one of them, `recent[0]` has `state: "Cancelled"`, `reason: "cancelled by announcer"`, non-null `endedAt`, and contains exactly the keys `id, state, season, episodeNumber, title, endedAt, reason`; `occupancy` drops to 1 (TR-21)
No element of `live` or `recent` contains a `flags` or `deliveryPayload` key, and after announcing and cancelling 21 manifests `recent` has exactly 20 entries (TR-21, TR-65)

`AdventureTime/Controllers/StationController.cs` injects only `IMediator` and `ILogger<StationController>` (`grep -n "IStationStore\|IOptions<\|AppDbContext" AdventureTime/Controllers/StationController.cs` returns nothing) (TR-53)

tickets.title: Annotate manifest/station actions for Swagger and enforce controller layering
tickets.context: Swagger is already enabled in Development. The new actions need typed response documentation, and the controllers need the layering rule enforced rather than remembered.
tickets.motivation: A self-describing contract lets a client author read the status codes and body types without opening the requirements. Asserting that controllers never inject the DbContext, the store or the analysis service prevents a quiet regression to the old style where the controller did the work itself.
tickets.goal: Typed response attributes on every action matching the requirements tables, XML summaries, and a layering check.
tickets.value: The API documents itself, and the architectural boundary between web and application is enforced by a test rather than by review vigilance.
tickets.description: On every action in `AdventureTime/Controllers/ManifestsController.cs` and `StationController.cs` add typed `[ProducesResponseType(typeof(...), StatusCodes.StatusNNN)]` attributes matching the status tables of TRD 7.1–7.5 (Announce: 201 `AnnounceManifestResponse`/400/409/429/500; Get: 200 `ManifestResponse`/404; Cancel: 204/404/409/500; Deliver: 202 `DeliverEpisodeResponse`/400/404/409/410/422/500; Station: 200 `StationResponse`/500) and `[Produces("application/json")]`, plus `/// <summary>` XML comments in the style of `EpisodesController` (style only: `AdventureTime.csproj` does not enable `GenerateDocumentationFile` and `AddSwaggerGen()` in `AdventureTime/Program.cs` does not call `IncludeXmlComments`, so the comments do not reach swagger.json and wiring them is out of scope). tickets.title: Add verify-manifests-api.sh curl status matrix for the compose stack
tickets.context: The definition of done for the HTTP epic: every status code in the API specification reproducible with curl against the running compose stack.
tickets.motivation: In-process tests prove the handlers; a curl script proves the container behaves the same way with real configuration, real ports and real JSON. It also becomes living documentation of how a client is expected to talk to the station.
tickets.goal: A script that walks every status code against a fresh stack, prints each check, and exits zero.
tickets.value: Repeatable acceptance for the HTTP surface in one command, and a worked example of the announce, deliver, poll and cancel flow for anyone writing a client.
tickets.description: Create the `scripts/` directory (it does not exist yet; F6.1 later adds `scripts/seed.sh` beside it) and `scripts/verify-manifests-api.sh` (bash, `set -euo pipefail`, requires `curl` and `jq`, `BASE_URL` default `http://localhost:5256` matching `docker-compose.yml` port `5256:8080`) that reproduces every status code of TRD §7 against a fresh stack started with `docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d --build`, using `AdventureTime/Episodes/s11e01__the_unfinished_map.json` and `s11e02__jake_s_nap.json` as delivery bodies and `docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U admin -d adventuretime -c ...` for the one SQL nudge (expiry in the past). The script asserts status and selected body fields with `jq -e`, asserts `Location` by suffix (`CreatedAtAction` emits an absolute URL), and exits non-zero on the first mismatch; it is the reviewer's evidence for TR-15/16/17/18/20/21/65 and is re-runnable. Sequence: 201 announce S11E01 (Location suffix, `occupancy 1`, `capacity 3`); 400 handler validation (`ttlSeconds 59`) and 400 unmapped member (`transcriptText` in the announce); 409 live conflict (`manifestId` equals the first id); 404 unknown GUID and 404 non-GUID on GET/DELETE/deliver; `GET /api/manifests/{id}` Waiting shape (`flags == []`, `links.deliver`, no `episodeId`/`links.episode`/`links.analysis`/`deliveryPayload`); 422 for season 12 plus missing `transcriptText` with the row still Waiting; 413 for the s11e01 file with `transcriptText` padded to 4.5 MB (row still Waiting); 202 for the s11e01 file padded to 3 MB (Location suffix, `sessionId == id`, `flags` array, `workingDeadlineAt`); 409 `already fulfilled` on the retried delivery with `state` in {Working, Done}; `/api/station` (`capacity`, `occupancy`, `live[]`/`recent[]` keys, no `flags`/`deliveryPayload`); announce S11E02, S11E03, S11E04, S11E05 in turn until the first 429 (expected on the 3rd or 4th announce depending on whether S11E01 is still live) asserting integer `Retry-After >= 1` and `capacity == 3, occupancy == 3`; 204 cancel S11E02 twice, then `recent[0].reason == "cancelled by announcer"`; 409 `cannot cancel` on S11E01 with `state` in {Working, Done}; 410 delivery of s11e02 to S11E03 after the SQL expiry nudge. Gotcha: this feature does not depend on the worker (F5.2), so the delivered row may stay Working — the script must accept `state` in {Working, Done} wherever TRD 7 allows it and must not poll for Done. With `--with-worker` it additionally polls S11E01 to Done (≤ 10 s), asserts the Done shape (`episodeId`, `links.episode`, `links.analysis`, no `links.deliver`) and asserts that re-announcing S11E01 returns 409 `{ message: "episode exists", episodeId }`.
acceptance_criteria: `scripts/verify-manifests-api.sh` exists, is executable, and exits 0 against a freshly built compose stack (`docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d --build`); its output lists each check with the observed status (TR-15)

The script asserts 201 with a `Location` ending in `/api/manifests/{id}`, 400 for `ttlSeconds: 59` with `errors.ttlSeconds`, 400 for an announce carrying `transcriptText`, 409 with `manifestId` equal to the first id on the duplicate announce, and 429 with integer `Retry-After >= 1` and body `capacity == 3, occupancy == 3` once three manifests are live; with `--with-worker` it also asserts 409 `message == "episode exists"` with `episodeId` on re-announcing the Done episode (TR-16)

The script asserts `GET /api/manifests/{id}` on a Waiting manifest has `flags == []`, `reason == null`, `links.deliver` present, and `episodeId`, `links.episode`, `links.analysis`, `deliveryPayload` absent (`jq -e 'has("episodeId") | not'`); with `--with-worker` it asserts the Done shape (`episodeId`, `links.episode`, `links.analysis` present, `links.deliver` absent) (TR-17)

The script asserts 204 for the first and second DELETE of a Waiting manifest, 409 `{ message: "cannot cancel", state }` with `state` in {Working, Done} for the delivered manifest, and 404 for an unknown GUID and for `/api/manifests/abc` (TR-18)

The script asserts the delivery outcomes 404 (unknown id), 404 (`/api/manifests/abc/episode`), 422 with both `season 12 does not match manifest season 11` and `transcriptText is required` in `reasons` (row still Waiting afterwards), 202 with `Location` suffix, `sessionId == id` and `workingDeadlineAt`, 409 `already fulfilled` on retry, and 410 `manifest expired` with `state == "TimedOut"` after `UPDATE "Sessions" SET "ExpiresAt" = now() - interval '1 second' WHERE "Id"='<id>'` (TR-20)

The script asserts `GET /api/station` returns 200 with `capacity`, `occupancy`, `live[]` and `recent[]`, every `live`/`recent` entry lacking `flags`/`deliveryPayload`, and `recent[0].reason == "cancelled by announcer"` after the cancel (TR-21)
The script asserts 413 for the 4.5 MB delivery body (row still Waiting) and 202 for the 3 MB body (padded `transcriptText`) (TR-65)

review_notes: F4.1-T1 title was 84 characters (limit 80); shortened.
F4.1-T5 title was 83 characters (limit 80); shortened.

F4.1-T1: the 429 body needs `capacity` but TR-26 lists no `Capacity` extra on the announce result and TR-52 forbids the controller injecting `IOptions<StationOptions>`; the description said only 'capacity from the response/result'. Made explicit: read `result.Capacity`, populated by the handler's `StationFull` factory, and add the property to `AnnounceManifestResult` if F3.2 did not.

F4.1-T1/T2/T5: criteria asserted `Location: /api/manifests/{id}` literally, but `CreatedAtAction`/`AcceptedAtAction` (mandated by TR-52) emit an absolute URL (`http://host/api/manifests/{id}`). Criteria now assert the header ends with `/api/manifests/{id}`.
F4.1-T1 AC5 asserted the `earliestExpiry: null` / `Retry-After: 30` case, which needs every live row Working and is unreachable before F4.1-T2 (and is store behaviour owned by F2.2); removed from T1.

F4.1-T1 AC6 asserted the Done-state body but nothing in this feature's dependencies can reach Done (the worker is F5.2 and legacy `POST api/Episodes` is removed by F4.2); the criterion now names the two ways to obtain a Done row (worker present, or SQL nudge) so it is verifiable.

F4.1-T3 AC3 cited '(TR-2 via F2.3)', a requirement this feature does not own and the criterion does not verify; tag removed. The description's 'wrap in try/catch only if the query can throw' was indeterminate; made definite (always wrap, like `EpisodesController.GetAll`). TR-65 (recent = 20 rows) appeared in an AC but not in tr_ids; added.

F4.1-T4: the reflection test used `typeof(Program).Assembly`, which needs the `public partial class Program {}` that TR-48 (F5.3) adds; switched to `typeof(ManifestsController).Assembly`. The 'reflection test OR documented grep' either/or was vague; made the test mandatory with a dependency on F2.4-T1 (test project). Cancel's status list omitted 500 although `CancelManifestCommand` has `InternalError` (TR-26); added. The AC referenced missing-XML-comment warnings under `GenerateDocumentationFile`, which `AdventureTime.csproj` does not enable and Swashbuckle is not configured to read; clause removed and XML comments kept as style only. `[ProducesResponseType]` must be typed so the swagger schema check for `deliveryPayload` is meaningful; stated.

F4.1-T5: the description mentioned an SQL nudge 'reading the Episodes id' that no step used, while the 409 `episode exists` outcome of TR-16 was never exercised; the nudge is dropped and the 409 `episode exists` check is added under `--with-worker` (the only configuration in which an `Episodes` row can exist). The 429 step assumed S11E01 stays Working; when the worker (F5.2) is present it goes Done and frees the slot, so the script now announces S11E02..S11E05 until the first 429. Cancel-on-Working now accepts Done for the same reason. The 3 MB-accepted check is now the S11E01 delivery itself (padded `s11e01` file) so it does not consume an extra manifest. `scripts/` does not exist in the repo; the ticket now says to create it.

F4.1-T1 and F4.1-T3 depend on `F3.2-T1` only; the controllers need `AnnounceManifestCommandHandler`, `GetManifestQueryHandler`, `CancelManifestCommandHandler`, `DeliverEpisodeCommandHandler` and `GetStationQueryHandler`, which F3.2 may deliver in later tickets. Kept `F3.2-T1` (the only F3.2 key knowable from the feature list) and named the required handlers in the descriptions so the planner can substitute the exact F3.2 ticket keys.

features.title: Episodes controller rewrite and legacy ingestion removal
features.summary: Rewrite `AdventureTime/Controllers/EpisodesController.cs` to inject `(IMediator, ILogger, IEpisodeAnalysisRepository)`: `GetAll` sends `GetAllEpisodesQuery`, `CreateEpisode` becomes the 410 action pointing at `/api/manifests` without touching MediatR or the LLM, `CreateEpisodeAnalysis`/`QuickEpisodeAnalysis` are deleted along with `Commands/Episodes/CreateEpisode/*` and `CreateEpisodeAnalysis/*`, and `GetEpisodeAnalysis` moves to `[HttpGet("{id:int}/analysis")]`. tickets.title: Rewrite EpisodesController: MediatR GetAll, 410 POST, re-routed analysis GET
tickets.context: The legacy episodes controller is the old door: an unguarded POST that stores an episode, two analysis actions that call the LLM with no slot, a mis-composed route that doubles the path, and direct use of the DbContext.
tickets.motivation: Nothing arrives that was not announced only holds if the old door is closed. Returning 410 with a pointer at the manifests endpoint tells the one client that used it where to go. The two direct-analysis actions bypass capacity entirely and have to go, and the analysis GET finally gets the route its author intended.
tickets.goal: A controller that injects only the mediator, a logger and the analysis repository, serves GetAll through a query, answers the old POST with 410, and exposes the analysis GET at a sane route.
tickets.value: The capacity claim becomes real: there is no slot-free path left into analysis. The viewer keeps working unchanged, and the route bug that has been there since the project began is gone.
tickets.description: Rewrite `/Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime/Controllers/EpisodesController.cs` so its constructor is exactly `(IMediator mediator, ILogger<EpisodesController> logger, IEpisodeAnalysisRepository episodeAnalysisRepository)`; remove the `AppDbContext` and `IDeepAnalysisService` fields and the `using AdventureTime.Infrastructure.Data;`, `using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;`, `using System.Diagnostics;` and the two `AdventureTime.Application.Commands.Episodes.*` usings (TR-54; §3.1 layering rule: controllers never inject `AppDbContext` or `IDeepAnalysisService`). `GetAll` keeps `[HttpGet]` and its try/catch → 500 `{ message }` shape but obtains the list via `await _mediator.Send(new GetAllEpisodesQuery(), ct)`; the query/handler is delivered by F3.2 (TR-26/TR-30) and wraps `IEpisodeRepository.GetAllAsync(null)`, which already orders by Season then EpisodeNumber, so the order the viewer sees is unchanged. `CreateEpisode` stays `[HttpPost]` but takes no parameters and makes no MediatR call: it returns `StatusCode(410, new { message = "removed; announce a manifest at POST /api/manifests, then deliver to POST /api/manifests/{id}/episode", manifests = "/api/manifests" })` with `[ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status410Gone)]` (TR-22); add `[ApiExplorerSettings(IgnoreApi = true)]` so Swagger lists only the five manifest/station routes and the three kept GETs (WP4 definition of done) — the tombstone is discoverable by its body, not by the API explorer. Delete the `CreateEpisodeAnalysis` and `QuickEpisodeAnalysis` actions outright; their `[Route("api/[controller]/analysis…")]` templates composed to the doubled paths `api/Episodes/api/Episodes/analysis[/quick|/{id:int}]`, which are not preserved (A24). Change `GetEpisodeAnalysis` to `[HttpGet("{id:int}/analysis")]` with no `[Route]` attribute (effective `GET api/episodes/{id:int}/analysis`; routing is case-insensitive) and its body unchanged: `_episodeAnalysisRepository.GetByEpisodeIdAsync(id)` → `Ok(analysis)`; a 404 for a missing analysis stays out of scope (§13). `GetEpisodeById` is untouched. Keep the class-level `[Route("api/[controller]")]` so `GET api/Episodes` and `GET api/Episodes/{id:int}` keep their exact paths; the kept GET bodies gain only `episode.sessionId` (TR-9, F1.3) and `analysis.continuityNotes` (TR-10, F1.3) through the entity changes — add no DTOs here.
acceptance_criteria: `EpisodesController` has exactly one constructor with parameters `(IMediator, ILogger<EpisodesController>, IEpisodeAnalysisRepository)`; `grep -n "AppDbContext\|IDeepAnalysisService\|Infrastructure.Data\|EntityFrameworkCore\|Commands.Episodes" AdventureTime/Controllers/EpisodesController.cs` prints nothing (TR-54)

`GetAll` contains no `_context` usage and sends `GetAllEpisodesQuery` through `_mediator`; `curl -s localhost:5256/api/episodes` returns 200 with a JSON array ordered by `season` then `episodeNumber`, each element carrying a `sessionId` member (null for pre-existing rows) (TR-22, TR-54)

`curl -s -i -X POST localhost:5256/api/episodes -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'` returns `HTTP/1.1 410` with body exactly `{"message":"removed; announce a manifest at POST /api/manifests, then deliver to POST /api/manifests/{id}/episode","manifests":"/api/manifests"}`; the action body contains no `_mediator.Send` and the file contains no reference to `IDeepAnalysisService` (TR-22, TR-54)

The file contains no method named `CreateEpisodeAnalysis` or `QuickEpisodeAnalysis`; `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST localhost:5256/api/Episodes/api/Episodes/analysis`, the same with `-X POST .../api/Episodes/api/Episodes/analysis/quick`, and `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' localhost:5256/api/Episodes/api/Episodes/analysis/1` all print `404` (TR-22, TR-54)

`GetEpisodeAnalysis` is decorated `[HttpGet("{id:int}/analysis")]` and has no `[Route]` attribute; for an episode id that has an analysis row, `curl -s localhost:5256/api/episodes/{id}/analysis` returns 200 with an `EpisodeAnalysis` body whose `continuityNotes` member is a JSON array (TR-22, TR-54)

`curl -s localhost:5256/api/Episodes/{id} | jq -S 'keys'` prints exactly the camelCase property names of `AdventureTime.Application/Models/Episode.cs` plus `sessionId`, and `curl -s localhost:5256/api/episodes | jq -S '.[0] | keys'` prints the same set — no member other than `sessionId` was added to either kept GET response (TR-22)
`dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` succeeds with zero warnings originating from `EpisodesController.cs`

epics.title: Hosted services, rehydration and end-to-end proof
epics.goal: The station runs unattended: the sweeper times out overdue manifests and fails overdue Working rows each tick, the worker analyses delivered episodes and adopts orphans within 30 s, a restart fails interrupted work and nothing else, and the `WebApplicationFactory` end-to-end scenario (TR-70) passes with a fake clock.

features.title: StationSweeper and hosted-service registration
features.summary: Implement `Infrastructure/Station/StationSweeper.cs` as a `BackgroundService` driven by `PeriodicTimer(SweepInterval, TimeProvider)` that, per tick and inside a fresh scope, runs `ExpireOverdueAsync(null)` then `FailOverdueWorkingAsync` with try/catch so no exception stops the host. Finalize the `AddInfrastructure` registration block of TR-49: options validation, `TryAddSingleton(TimeProvider.System)`, scoped `IStationStore`, singleton `IAnalysisQueue`, and `AddHostedService<AnalysisWorker>()` strictly before `AddHostedService<StationSweeper>()` so the sweeper stops first. Verified by forcing `WorkingDeadlineAt`/`ExpiresAt` into the past and observing terminal rows within one tick.

tickets.title: Implement StationSweeper BackgroundService with PeriodicTimer and per-tick scope
tickets.context: The expiry sweeper, mechanism three, the janitor that walks the waiting slots on a timer.
tickets.motivation: A claimed slot must always come back. The two conditional statements the sweeper runs each tick are what reclaim slots when a sender never delivers and when a Working row outlives its deadline because the wake-up was lost or the worker faulted. Running each tick in a fresh scope with a catch around it is what keeps a transient database error from stopping the host.
tickets.goal: A background service driven by a periodic timer on the injected time provider, running expire-overdue then fail-overdue-working each tick, never exiting on an exception.
tickets.value: Liveness. No slot can be held forever, and the durable backstop for orphaned Working rows that the design review demanded now exists.
tickets.description: Create `AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationSweeper.cs` as `public sealed class StationSweeper : BackgroundService` with constructor `(IServiceScopeFactory scopeFactory, IOptions<StationOptions> options, TimeProvider timeProvider, ILogger<StationSweeper> logger)`; read `options.Value.SweepInterval` once in the constructor (A4, TR-35). `ExecuteAsync` must follow TR-41 literally: `using var timer = new PeriodicTimer(interval, timeProvider); while (await timer.WaitForNextTickAsync(stoppingToken)) { try { using var scope = scopeFactory.CreateScope(); var store = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<IStationStore>(); await store.ExpireOverdueAsync(null, stoppingToken); await store.FailOverdueWorkingAsync(stoppingToken); } catch (OperationCanceledException) when (stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested) { break; } catch (Exception ex) { logger.LogError(ex, "sweeper tick failed"); } }`. This is mechanism 3 of the TRD (section 1, section 3.5): each tick moves Waiting rows past `ExpiresAt` to TimedOut and Working rows past `WorkingDeadlineAt` to Failed, using only the store's single autocommit statements (TR-39); the sweeper takes no advisory lock, opens no explicit transaction and never constructor-injects `AppDbContext` or `IStationStore` (they are scoped; the sweeper is a singleton). The `TimeProvider` overload of `PeriodicTimer` is what lets the E2E test (TR-70 step 11) tick the sweeper with `FakeTimeProvider.Advance(16 s)`, so do not use `Task.Delay` or the parameterless `PeriodicTimer` constructor. `BackgroundService` comes from `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.Abstractions 10.0.0`, which F1.1 adds to `AdventureTime.Infrastructure.csproj` (TR-51; today the project has only EF Core, `Microsoft.Extensions.Http` and Npgsql); `IServiceScopeFactory` and `GetRequiredService` come from `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions`, already transitive. If the Hosting.Abstractions package is not yet present when you start, add it to `AdventureTime.Infrastructure.csproj`, nowhere else. Do not register the service in this ticket; registration order is F5.1-T2. Reference: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2dc9531c-3f0b-499f-8ec6-fb2cf3271341#TR-41
acceptance_criteria: `AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationSweeper.cs` exists, declares `public sealed class StationSweeper : BackgroundService` with exactly the constructor `(IServiceScopeFactory, IOptions<StationOptions>, TimeProvider, ILogger<StationSweeper>)`, and `dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` succeeds with no new warnings (TR-41)

`ExecuteAsync` constructs `new PeriodicTimer(<SweepInterval read once in the ctor>, timeProvider)` and loops on `while (await timer.WaitForNextTickAsync(stoppingToken))`; `grep -n "Task.Delay\|DateTime.UtcNow\|new PeriodicTimer([^,)]*)" AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationSweeper.cs` returns nothing (TR-41)

Inside every tick a fresh scope is created via `scopeFactory.CreateScope()` (disposed at the end of the tick), `IStationStore` is resolved from that scope, and `ExpireOverdueAsync(null, stoppingToken)` is awaited before `FailOverdueWorkingAsync(stoppingToken)`, in that order (TR-41)

The tick body is wrapped in try/catch: `catch (OperationCanceledException) when (stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested)` breaks the loop; any other exception, including an `OperationCanceledException` not tied to the stopping token, is logged with `LogError` and the loop continues to the next tick (TR-41, TR-64)

`grep -n "AppDbContext\|IStationStore" AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationSweeper.cs` shows `IStationStore` only in the `GetRequiredService<IStationStore>()` call and `AppDbContext` nowhere; `grep -n "BeginTransaction\|pg_advisory" AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationSweeper.cs` returns nothing (TR-41)

`grep -rn "AddHostedService<StationSweeper>" AdventureTime AdventureTime.Infrastructure --include=*.cs` returns nothing after this ticket; registration is deferred to F5.1-T2 so the ordering constraint of TR-49 is applied in one place (TR-49)

tickets.title: Finalize AddInfrastructure station registration and hosted-service order
tickets.context: Several tickets have each added lines to AddInfrastructure. This ticket consolidates the station registration block into one place with one order.
tickets.motivation: Hosted services stop in reverse registration order, so the order of two AddHostedService calls decides whether the sweeper stops before the worker on shutdown, which the design requires. The store must be scoped, the queue a singleton, and the time provider registered so tests can replace it. Exactly once each, or the behavior depends on which ticket landed last.
tickets.goal: The registration block in the exact required order with each registration present once.
tickets.value: Startup and shutdown behave as designed rather than by accident of merge order, and the next person reading the DI file sees the whole station in one block.
tickets.description: Consolidate the station registration block in `AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` (`AddInfrastructure(this IServiceCollection services, IConfiguration configuration, IHostEnvironment environment)` after F1.2's TR-50 signature change; today the method still takes two parameters) so it contains, in this order and exactly once each: `services.AddOptions<StationOptions>().Bind(configuration.GetSection(StationOptions.SectionName)).Validate(o => o.Capacity >= 1 && o.TtlMin <= o.TtlDefault && o.TtlDefault <= o.TtlMax && o.SweepInterval > TimeSpan.Zero && o.ProcessingTimeout >= TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1), "Station options out of range").ValidateOnStart();` then `services.TryAddSingleton(TimeProvider.System);` then `services.AddScoped<IStationStore, StationStore>();` then `services.AddSingleton<IAnalysisQueue, AnalysisQueue>();` then `services.AddHostedService<AnalysisWorker>();` and finally `services.AddHostedService<StationSweeper>();`. Earlier features (F1.1 options, F2.1 store, F3.2 queue, F5.2 worker) may have dropped partial registrations into this file; remove the duplicates so the block reads as one unit. This ticket needs the concrete `StationStore` (F2.1), `AnalysisQueue` (F3.2) and `AnalysisWorker` (F5.2) classes to exist, whichever ticket in those features adds them. Why the details matter: `ValidateOnStart` makes a misconfigured `Station` section fail the host at boot instead of at first use (do NOT call `ValidateDataAnnotations()`: the package is not referenced and `StationOptions` has no annotations); `TryAddSingleton` (needs `using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Extensions;`) lets tests `RemoveAll<TimeProvider>()` and substitute `FakeTimeProvider` without the app re-registering the system clock on top; and hosted services stop in reverse registration order, so registering the worker before the sweeper means the sweeper stops first at shutdown (A19), leaving in-flight worker jobs to finish under the host's 30 s `ShutdownTimeout` (TR-43). Keep `AddDbContext<AppDbContext>` scoped and do not add `EnableRetryOnFailure` (TR-51, TR-59). Add a registration unit test in `AdventureTime.Tests/Infrastructure/AddInfrastructureTests.cs` that builds a `ServiceCollection` with an in-memory `IConfiguration` (`ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection` placeholder plus a `Station` section; `Station:AnalysisProvider` left at its `Stub` default so no API key is needed) and a stub `IHostEnvironment` with `EnvironmentName = "Development"`, calls `AddInfrastructure`, and inspects the descriptors; for the failure cases build the provider and call `provider.GetRequiredService<Microsoft.Extensions.Options.IStartupValidator>().Validate()`, which is exactly what the host runs at startup. Reference: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2dc9531c-3f0b-499f-8ec6-fb2cf3271341#TR-49
acceptance_criteria: `AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` contains the `AddOptions<StationOptions>().Bind(configuration.GetSection(StationOptions.SectionName)).Validate(...).ValidateOnStart()` chain with the exact predicate and message `"Station options out of range"` of TR-49, and `grep -n ValidateDataAnnotations AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` returns nothing (TR-49)

`services.TryAddSingleton(TimeProvider.System)` is used (not `AddSingleton`): the test registers a `FakeTimeProvider` instance before calling `AddInfrastructure` and asserts that afterwards exactly one `ServiceDescriptor` for `TimeProvider` exists and its `ImplementationInstance` is that same `FakeTimeProvider` (TR-49)

The test asserts `IStationStore` is registered exactly once with `ServiceLifetime.Scoped` and `ImplementationType == typeof(StationStore)`, and `IAnalysisQueue` exactly once with `ServiceLifetime.Singleton` and `ImplementationType == typeof(AnalysisQueue)` (TR-49)

The test asserts the `IHostedService` descriptors' `ImplementationType`s, in registration order, are exactly `[typeof(AnalysisWorker), typeof(StationSweeper)]`; `grep -c "AddHostedService" AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` prints 2 and `grep -n AddHostedService AdventureTime/Program.cs` prints nothing (TR-49)

With `Station:Capacity = 0` (and, in a separate test, `Station:TtlDefault = 10` with `Station:TtlMin = 60`) the test builds the provider and both `provider.GetRequiredService<IStartupValidator>().Validate()` and reading `IOptions<StationOptions>.Value` throw `OptionsValidationException` whose message contains `Station options out of range`; with the TR-55 defaults `Validate()` does not throw and `.Value` has `Capacity == 3` and `SweepInterval == TimeSpan.FromSeconds(15)` (TR-49)
`grep -n "EnableRetryOnFailure\|IsolationLevel" AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` returns nothing and `AddDbContext<AppDbContext>` remains scoped (TR-49; per TR-51/TR-59)

Manual check with the compose database up and the `adventuretime-api` container stopped (TR-66): `Station__AnalysisProvider=Stub dotnet run --project AdventureTime` starts, `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:5256/health` (or the launch profile port) prints 200, and the process stays up for at least 30 s (two sweep intervals) with no Error-level log line; the same command with `Station__Capacity=0` terminates during startup with an `OptionsValidationException` whose message contains `Station options out of range` (TR-49)

tickets.title: Test StationSweeper: fake-store loop resilience and one-tick sweep on Postgres
tickets.context: Unit tests with a fake time provider and a recording fake store, plus one real tick against Postgres.
tickets.motivation: Three things need proof: the tick runs the two statements in order, an exception inside a tick does not end the loop, and a real tick actually moves real overdue rows. The second is the one that keeps the API alive through a database blip.
tickets.goal: Both test classes green: loop resilience with fakes, and a one-tick sweep on the container.
tickets.value: The janitor's resilience is tested, so the most common operational failure, a brief database outage, cannot take the station down.
tickets.description: Add two test classes to the `AdventureTime.Tests` project created by F2.4 (TR-67). (1) `AdventureTime.Tests/Station/StationSweeperTests.cs`, pure unit tests with `FakeTimeProvider` (`Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing`) and a hand-written `IStationStore` fake that records calls and can be told to throw: build a `ServiceCollection` with `AddScoped<IStationStore>(_ => fake)`, construct `new StationSweeper(provider.GetRequiredService<IServiceScopeFactory>(), Options.Create(new StationOptions { SweepInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(15) }), fakeTime, NullLogger<StationSweeper>.Instance)`, call `StartAsync(CancellationToken.None)` (which runs `ExecuteAsync` up to the first `WaitForNextTickAsync`, so the timer exists before you advance), then `fakeTime.Advance(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(15))` per tick. Gotchas: `PeriodicTimer` on a `FakeTimeProvider` fires synchronously inside `Advance`, but the continuation of `WaitForNextTickAsync` runs on the thread pool, so poll the fake's call count with a short bounded wait (up to 2 s) rather than asserting immediately; advance exactly one full interval per intended tick, never less (no tick) and never two intervals at once (`PeriodicTimer` coalesces missed ticks into one). (2) `AdventureTime.Tests/Station/StationSweeperIntegrationTests.cs` in the `PostgresFixture` collection, using the real `StationStore` over `AppDbContext` on the container (this needs F2.1's `StationStore` class, whichever ticket adds it): after the `TRUNCATE "EpisodeAnalyses", "Episodes", "Sessions" RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE;` reset, insert four rows by raw SQL supplying every NOT NULL column of TR-8 (`Id`, `State`, `Season`, `EpisodeNumber`, `Title`, `ExpectedCharacters`/`ExpectedLocations`/`RequestedStages` as `'[]'::jsonb`, `TtlSeconds`, `AnnouncedAt`, `ExpiresAt`): a Waiting row with `"ExpiresAt" = now() - interval '1 second'`, a Working row with `"WorkingDeadlineAt" = now() - interval '1 second'` and a non-null `"DeliveryPayload"` (`'{}'::jsonb` is enough), plus a Waiting and a Working control row with those clocks one minute in the future. Host the sweeper through a `ServiceCollection` (`AddLogging()`, `Configure<StationOptions>` with `SweepInterval = 15 s`, `AddDbContext<AppDbContext>` on the fixture's connection string or `DbContextOptions` factory, `AddScoped<IStationStore, StationStore>`, `AddSingleton<TimeProvider>(fakeTime)`, `AddHostedService<StationSweeper>`), resolve the `IHostedService`, `StartAsync`, `Advance(16 s)` once, poll the table for up to 5 s (mirroring TR-70 step 11: the sweep runs asynchronously on the hosted service), and `StopAsync` in a `finally`. This is the WP5 definition-of-done check "a forced WorkingDeadlineAt in the past is swept to Failed within one tick" and proves section 3.5's loop end to end. Reference: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2dc9531c-3f0b-499f-8ec6-fb2cf3271341#35-sequence-expiry-working-deadline-rehydration
acceptance_criteria: Unit test `Tick_RunsExpireThenFailOverdue`: after one `Advance(15 s)` the fake records exactly `ExpireOverdueAsync(null)` followed by `FailOverdueWorkingAsync`, each once, and the `IStationStore` was resolved from a scope created for that tick (the `AddScoped` factory delegate was invoked exactly once per tick) (TR-41)

Unit test `Tick_ExceptionDoesNotStopLoop`: the fake throws `InvalidOperationException` from `ExpireOverdueAsync` on tick 1; after a second `Advance(15 s)` the fake records a second tick with both calls, and `sweeper.ExecuteTask` is neither faulted nor completed (TR-41)

Unit test `Tick_ForeignCancellationDoesNotStopLoop`: the fake throws `new OperationCanceledException()` (unrelated to the stopping token) on tick 1; tick 2 still runs and `sweeper.ExecuteTask` is neither faulted nor completed (TR-41)

Unit test `Stop_CompletesPromptly`: `await sweeper.StopAsync(cts.Token)` with a 5 s timeout completes; afterwards `sweeper.ExecuteTask.IsFaulted` is false (the task is Canceled or RanToCompletion, since the stopping token leaves the loop through the `while` condition) (TR-41)

Integration test `Sweep_ForcedPastClocks_TerminalWithinOneTick`: within 5 s of `Advance(16 s)` the overdue Waiting row is `TimedOut` with `Reason = 'ttl elapsed'`, the overdue Working row is `Failed` with `Reason = 'working deadline exceeded'`, both have `"EndedAt" IS NOT NULL` and `"DeliveryPayload" IS NULL`, and the two control rows are unchanged (still Waiting/Working, `"EndedAt" IS NULL`, the Working control's payload intact) (TR-41)

The integration test asserts that after `StartAsync` and a 1 s real-time wait, but before `Advance`, all four rows are unchanged, proving the sweep is driven by the `TimeProvider` timer rather than wall-clock time (TR-41)

`dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~StationSweeper"` passes with Docker available, and `dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~StationSweeperTests"` passes without a container (TR-41)
