features.title: AnalysisWorker with orphan scan and timeout classification
features.summary: Implement `Infrastructure/Station/AnalysisWorker.cs`: a `BackgroundService` reading the queue and, every 30 s, adopting `GetWorkingIdsAsync` ids not in `_inFlight` (`ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, Task>`, `TryAdd` as the single admission point), one tracked Task per session, `WhenAll` of in-flight jobs in `finally`. `RunJobAsync` resolves store and `IDeepAnalysisService` from a scope, requires Working, deserializes `DeliveryPayload`, loads continuity, runs the LLM call under a deadline CTS linked to the stopping token, then `CompleteAsync` with `CancellationToken.None`; exceptions are classified stopping-token first, then deadline → `processing timeout`, else `analysis error: <Type>`. Covers the worker-side rows of the remaining-races table (orphan scan vs job, lost enqueue). Verified by a Working row inserted by SQL being adopted within 30 s and by `StubDelay` holding a job past the timeout.

tickets.title: Add AnalysisWorker BackgroundService with queue loop, orphan scan and in-flight tracking
tickets.context: The consumer of the Working state: the service that turns a delivered episode into an analysis. This ticket builds its loops and bookkeeping; the job body comes next.
tickets.motivation: One tracked task per session means in-flight analyses equal Working rows, so processing concurrency is bounded by admission rather than by the worker, which is the design's whole point. A thirty-second scan that adopts Working rows nobody is working on recovers a lost enqueue without a restart, and making the in-flight dictionary the single admission point prevents the queue and the scan from starting the same job twice.
tickets.goal: A background service with a queue loop, an orphan-scan loop, in-flight tracking, and a graceful drain on shutdown.
tickets.value: Processing concurrency is exactly the station's capacity, and a lost wake-up costs at most thirty seconds instead of a slot until the next deploy.

tickets.title: Implement RunJobAsync: scoped load, continuity, deadline CTS and CompleteAsync
tickets.context: The body of a job: what happens between dequeuing a session id and writing its outcome.
tickets.motivation: Each step exists for a reason. A scope per job means no captured DbContext or HttpClient outlives its use. Requiring the row to still be Working before starting means a swept or restarted session is never analyzed. Loading continuity here is what makes the manifest's cast announcement pay off. The deadline token on the time provider is the fast path that stops a hung provider call.
tickets.goal: The six-step job implemented exactly, wholly inside a catch so nothing escapes to the loops.
tickets.value: The LLM call runs with the right context, under a real deadline, and its result can only land if the slot is still held. Every paid call either produces a stored analysis or a recorded reason.
tickets.description: Replace the placeholder body of `internal virtual Task RunJobAsync(Guid id, CancellationToken stoppingToken)` in /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/AnalysisWorker.cs with the six-step job of TR-44, wholly inside an outer try/catch that logs at Error so nothing escapes to the loops. Step 1 creates `using var scope = scopeFactory.CreateScope()` and resolves `IStationStore` and `IDeepAnalysisService` from `scope.ServiceProvider` (scope per job, A14-A16). Step 2 calls `store.GetForProcessingAsync(id, CancellationToken.None)`; null or `State != SessionState.Working` logs `dropped {SessionId}` and returns without writing; a null `DeliveryPayload` calls `FailAsync(id, "missing payload", CancellationToken.None)` and returns (defensive: invariant I6 of TR-57 makes it unreachable, and the fixed reason is distinct from the `analysis error: <Type>` family). Step 3 deserializes `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Episode>(s.DeliveryPayload, StationJson.Options)`, sets `episode.SessionId = id`, and loads `context = await store.LoadContinuityAsync(s.Season, s.EpisodeNumber, s.ExpectedCharacters, CancellationToken.None)`. Step 4 builds `using var deadlineCts = new CancellationTokenSource(options.ProcessingTimeout, timeProvider)` and `using var jobCts = CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(stoppingToken, deadlineCts.Token)`; step 5 calls the three-argument `service.AnalyzeEpisodeAsync(episode, context, jobCts.Token)` (the TR-34 continuity overload) with every store read already materialized, so no DbContext connection or transaction is open across the LLM call. Step 6 calls `store.CompleteAsync(id, episode, analysis, CancellationToken.None)`; `LostSlot` and `EpisodeExists` are logged at Warning and `FailAsync` is NOT called for either (the row is already terminal, TR-4/TR-38). Log `job start {SessionId}` and `job end {SessionId} outcome={Outcome} elapsedMs={ElapsedMs}` (the lines TR-64, owned by F5.3, relies on); exception classification for steps 5-6 is F5.2-T3, so here any exception reaching the outer catch is logged only. Also add /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Tests/Station/WorkerHarness.cs: builds a ServiceCollection with `AddLogging` plus a capturing logger provider, `AddDbContext<AppDbContext>(o => o.UseNpgsql(fixture.ConnectionString))`, `AddScoped<IStationStore, StationStore>()`, `AddSingleton(Options.Create(new StationOptions { ProcessingTimeout = ... }))`, `AddSingleton<IAnalysisQueue, AnalysisQueue>()`, a `FakeTimeProvider`, and `AddSingleton<IDeepAnalysisService>` defaulting to `StubDeepAnalysisService` but overridable per test; it constructs `AnalysisWorker` directly and exposes `StartAsync`/`StopAsync`, `ExecuteTask`, the queue, the time provider, the captured log lines and `OpenStore()` (a fresh `StationStore` on its own AppDbContext for out-of-band writes). Include two reusable doubles in the same file: `HeldAnalysisService` (`TaskCompletionSource Started`, `TaskCompletionSource<EpisodeAnalysis> Release`; awaits `Release.Task.WaitAsync(ct)` so the stopping token still cancels it) and `ThrowingAnalysisService(Exception)`.

tickets.title: Classify LLM-call exceptions: stopping token, deadline timeout, analysis error
tickets.context: What the word Failed means. Three different things can interrupt the LLM call and each needs a different outcome.
tickets.motivation: Shutdown must leave the row Working so rehydration can fail it with the right reason on the next boot. The deadline must become 'processing timeout'. Anything else must become an analysis error carrying the exception type. The order of the catch clauses is what makes the classification correct when both tokens are cancelled.
tickets.goal: Three catch clauses in the required order and a pure classification helper that tests can call directly.
tickets.value: Failed reasons are truthful, so an operator reading the board can tell a slow provider from a broken one from a restart, and act accordingly.
tickets.description: In /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/AnalysisWorker.cs put steps 5 and 6 of `RunJobAsync` (the `AnalyzeEpisodeAsync` call and the `CompleteAsync` call, not the reads of steps 2-3) inside one try with the three catch clauses of TR-45 in this exact order. First `catch (OperationCanceledException) when (stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested)`: write nothing, log `job {SessionId} cancelled by shutdown; row left Working` at Information and return, leaving the row for rehydration (`FailInterrupted`, F5.3) or the sweeper's working deadline (F5.1). Second `catch (OperationCanceledException) when (deadlineCts.IsCancellationRequested)`: `await store.FailAsync(id, "processing timeout", CancellationToken.None)`. Third `catch (Exception ex)`: `await store.FailAsync(id, $"analysis error: {ex.GetType().Name}", CancellationToken.None)`; this clause is the only one reachable from step 6 (it uses `CancellationToken.None`), so a `DbUpdateException` or `PostgresException` propagating from `CompleteAsync` per TR-61 becomes `analysis error: DbUpdateException` / `analysis error: PostgresException`, attempted once; if that `FailAsync` itself throws, the outer catch of TR-44 logs it at Error and the row is left for the sweeper deadline. The stopping-token clause must come first because the linked `jobCts` cancels for both sources when the host stops mid-deadline. Every store write here and in step 6 uses `CancellationToken.None`; the stopping token cancels only the LLM call, and nothing under /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station ever references `HttpContext.RequestAborted` (TR-62). Add `internal static string? ClassifyReason(Exception ex, CancellationToken stoppingToken, CancellationToken deadlineToken)` (null = write nothing; only an `OperationCanceledException` can map to null or `processing timeout`, any other exception maps to the `analysis error:` family regardless of token state) and have the catch clauses delegate to it so the ordering is unit-testable without a database.
acceptance_criteria: Unit test `AnalysisWorkerTests.Classify_StoppingTokenFirst`: with both tokens cancelled and an `OperationCanceledException`, `ClassifyReason` returns null; with only the deadline cancelled it returns `processing timeout`; with an `InvalidOperationException` (tokens in any state) it returns `analysis error: InvalidOperationException`; with a `TaskCanceledException` and neither token cancelled it returns `analysis error: TaskCanceledException` (TR-45).

Reviewer confirms in /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/AnalysisWorker.cs that the catch clauses appear in the order stopping-token, deadline, generic; that the try covers steps 5 and 6 only; and that `FailAsync`/`CompleteAsync` are invoked with `CancellationToken.None` in every branch (TR-45, TR-62).
`grep -rn "RequestAborted" /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Application/Commands` returns nothing (TR-62).

`grep -n "client.Timeout" /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs` shows only `Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan`, confirming the deadline CTS is the only clock for the LLM call (TR-46 is owned by F1.2; verified here because TR-62 depends on it).

Unit test `AnalysisWorkerTests.Complete_StoreExceptionFailsOnce`: `FakeStationStore` holds a Working session with a valid payload and its `CompleteAsync` throws `new DbUpdateException("boom")`; after the job the fake recorded exactly one `FailAsync(id, "analysis error: DbUpdateException", CancellationToken.None)`, `ExecuteTask` is still running and `InFlightCount == 0`; a variant whose `FailAsync` also throws produces an Error log and no unhandled exception (TR-45, TR-61 worker rows).

Unit test `AnalysisWorkerTests.Shutdown_LogsCancelledByShutdown`: `HeldAnalysisService` in flight, `StopAsync` called; the fake store records no `FailAsync` call and the logs contain `cancelled by shutdown` for the id (TR-45, TR-62).
`dotnet build /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.sln` and `dotnet test /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Tests --filter AnalysisWorkerTests` pass.

tickets.title: Integration-test orphan adoption, lost enqueue and TryAdd dedupe on Postgres
tickets.context: The worker-side races from the requirements' race table, run on the real container with the worker harness.
tickets.motivation: Adoption of a Working row inserted by SQL with no enqueue, recovery from a lost enqueue, and proof that the scan and the queue cannot start the same job twice are the three behaviors that turn the liveness fix from the design review into something demonstrated.
tickets.goal: Three integration tests green.
tickets.value: The durable-deadline-plus-adoption design that closed the 'slot leaks forever' hole is proven rather than argued.
tickets.description: Add the worker-side race tests of the remaining-races table (TR-58 rows 'Worker job vs orphan scan adopting the same id' and 'Enqueue lost'; TR-58 itself is owned by F2.1) to /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Tests/Station/AnalysisWorkerTests.cs using the `WorkerHarness` and `HeldAnalysisService` from F5.2-T2 on the PostgresFixture, with `TRUNCATE "EpisodeAnalyses", "Episodes", "Sessions" RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE` before each test. The lost-enqueue scenario is modelled by inserting a Working row (every NOT NULL column of TR-8, a valid `DeliveryPayload`, `WorkingDeadlineAt` in the future) directly by SQL and never calling `TryEnqueue`; the worker must adopt it on the next 30 s orphan scan (`FakeTimeProvider.Advance(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30))`). Gotcha: F5.2-T1 creates the `PeriodicTimer` before the first await in `ExecuteAsync`, so it exists once `StartAsync` returns; never call `Advance` before `StartAsync` has returned, and never expect a tick from an `Advance` smaller than the remaining period. The dedupe scenario holds a queued job in flight with `HeldAnalysisService` (await its `Started` task before advancing the clock) while a scan runs, then releases it and asserts a single completion; do not use `StubDeepAnalysisService.StubDelay` here (it is a static TimeSpan read once by `Task.Delay` and cannot be released; F5.2-T5 uses it for the timeout case). Each assertion on a row state polls the database for up to 5 s of real time, because the scan and the job run asynchronously on the worker. These tests are the automated form of the WP5 definition of done 'a Working row inserted by SQL is adopted within 30 s'.
acceptance_criteria: Test `OrphanScan_AdoptsSqlInsertedWorkingRow`: a Working row inserted by SQL (valid payload, `WorkingDeadlineAt = now() + interval '10 minutes'`) with no enqueue; after `Advance(30 s)` the row becomes Done within 5 s of real time, an `Episodes` row with `SessionId = id` exists, and the logs contain `adopted orphaned session {id}` (TR-43; TR-58 lost-enqueue row).

Test `OrphanScan_DoesNotAdoptBeforeThirtySeconds`: same setup but `Advance(29 s)`; after 1 s of real time the row is still Working and no `adopted orphaned session` log exists; a further `Advance(1 s)` adopts it and the row becomes Done within 5 s (TR-43).

Test `OrphanScan_SkipsInFlightJob`: `HeldAnalysisService` registered; `TryEnqueue(X)`, await `Started`; `Advance(30 s)` runs a scan whose `GetWorkingIdsAsync` returns X; `InFlightCount` stays 1 and no `adopted orphaned session` log for X exists; after `Release.SetResult(analysis)` the row is Done exactly once (one `Episodes` row for X, exactly one `job end` log for X) (TR-43; TR-58 orphan-scan-vs-job row).

Test `Queue_DuplicateEnqueueIsNoOp_Postgres`: `TryEnqueue(X)` twice while X is held by `HeldAnalysisService` yields one job (`InFlightCount == 1`, exactly one `job start` log for X); after release the row is Done with one `Episodes` row (TR-43).

Test `OrphanScan_AdoptsOnlyWorkingRows`: Waiting, Done and Failed rows inserted alongside one Working row; after `Advance(30 s)` only the Working id is adopted (one `adopted orphaned session` log, naming it), it becomes Done, and the other three rows are byte-for-byte unchanged (TR-43).

All tests in the class pass with `dotnet test /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Tests --filter AnalysisWorkerTests` and the class runs in the PostgresFixture collection (no parallel execution against the shared database).

tickets.title: Integration-test timeout, analysis-error and shutdown classification with StubDelay
tickets.context: Classification scenarios using the stub's internal delay to hold a job past its deadline while the fake clock advances.
tickets.motivation: The deadline path has to be verified end to end: the timer fires, the token cancels the call, the classifier names it correctly, and the row ends Failed with that reason. The analysis-error and shutdown paths need the same treatment so the three outcomes are each observed once.
tickets.goal: Timeout, analysis error and shutdown scenarios green.
tickets.value: The processing timeout, the one clock the station promises on an LLM call, is verified from timer to database row.
tickets.description: Add the TR-45/TR-62 scenario tests to /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Tests/Station/AnalysisWorkerTests.cs using the `WorkerHarness` (F5.2-T2) on the PostgresFixture. The timeout case holds the job past `Station:ProcessingTimeout` by setting `StubDeepAnalysisService.StubDelay` (an `internal static TimeSpan`, reachable via the TR-51 InternalsVisibleTo) to a long value: the stub's `Task.Delay(StubDelay, ct)` runs on the real clock while the deadline CTS is built on the harness `FakeTimeProvider`, so advancing the fake clock by `ProcessingTimeout` cancels `deadlineCts`, the linked token cancels the delay, the stub throws `OperationCanceledException`, and the worker must classify it as `processing timeout`, not as an analysis error and not as a shutdown. The analysis-error case registers `ThrowingAnalysisService` in the harness. The shutdown case calls `StopAsync` while a job is held and asserts the row is left Working with its payload intact so that rehydration (F5.3) or the sweeper deadline (F5.1) finishes it. The precedence case needs both tokens cancelled before the catch clause runs, which the real stub cannot arrange, so define a local `GatedCancelAnalysisService` double: on `ct` cancellation it awaits a test-owned `Gate` TaskCompletionSource and only then throws `new OperationCanceledException(ct)`. Because `StubDelay` is static, reset it to `TimeSpan.Zero` in a `finally` in every test that sets it; the class already runs serially in the PostgresFixture collection. These tests are the automated form of the WP5 definition of done 'StubDelay holding a job past the timeout'.
acceptance_criteria: Test `Timeout_FailsWithProcessingTimeout`: harness `ProcessingTimeout = 00:00:05`, `StubDelay = 10 minutes`; after `TryEnqueue(id)`, a `job start` log for the id, and `FakeTimeProvider.Advance(5 s)`, the row is Failed with `Reason = 'processing timeout'`, `"EndedAt" IS NOT NULL`, `"DeliveryPayload" IS NULL`, and `Episodes` is empty, within 5 s of real time (TR-45, TR-62).

Test `Timeout_NotMisclassifiedAsShutdown`: same setup; afterwards `ExecuteTask` is not completed, the logs contain no `cancelled by shutdown` line for the id, and the reason is exactly `processing timeout` rather than `analysis error: OperationCanceledException` or `analysis error: TaskCanceledException` (TR-45).

Test `AnalysisError_FailsWithExceptionTypeName`: `ThrowingAnalysisService(new InvalidOperationException())` yields a Failed row with `Reason = 'analysis error: InvalidOperationException'`, `"DeliveryPayload" IS NULL` and no `Episodes` row; a second run with `new HttpRequestException()` yields `analysis error: HttpRequestException` (TR-45).

Test `Shutdown_LeavesRowWorking`: `StubDelay = 10 minutes`; after the `job start` log, `StopAsync(CancellationToken.None)` completes within 5 s (the stopping token cancelled the stub's delay), the row is still Working with `"DeliveryPayload" IS NOT NULL` and `"Reason" IS NULL`, the logs contain `cancelled by shutdown` for the id and no `Session {id} Working -> Failed` line (TR-45, TR-62).

Test `Shutdown_TakesPrecedenceOverDeadline`: `ProcessingTimeout = 00:00:05` and `GatedCancelAnalysisService` registered; start `StopAsync` without awaiting it, wait until the double reports its `ct` cancelled, then `Advance(5 s)` (deadline token now also cancelled), then set `Gate`; `StopAsync` completes, the row remains Working with its payload, and no `FailAsync` transition line exists for the id (TR-45).

`dotnet test /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Tests --filter AnalysisWorkerTests` passes and, after the run, a final test or fixture check observes `StubDeepAnalysisService.StubDelay == TimeSpan.Zero`.

tickets.title: Verify worker adoption and timeout against the compose stack
tickets.context: The real compose stack rather than the test harness, with a Working row inserted by hand and the logs watched.
tickets.motivation: Fake time providers cannot prove the real periodic timer or the real clock. A manual adoption check and a manual timeout check against the container, with the commands and log excerpts recorded, close the gap between the harness and production.
tickets.goal: Recorded evidence that adoption happens within thirty seconds and that an overdue job fails with a timeout reason on the running stack.
tickets.value: Confidence that the hosted services behave outside the test host, which is where they will actually run.
tickets.description: Run the WP5 definition-of-done checks for the worker against the real stack, not the test harness, and record the exact commands and log excerpts in the PR description so a reviewer can repeat them. Start the stack with `docker compose up -d --build` (Stub provider, `Station:ProcessingTimeout` default 00:10:00). Orphan-adoption check: with `docker compose exec postgres psql -U admin -d adventuretime` (user and database from /Users/steven/AdventureTime/docker-compose.yml) insert a Working row supplying every NOT NULL column of TR-8 (`Id` = a fresh uuid, `State='Working'`, `Season`/`EpisodeNumber` for an episode not yet in `Episodes`, `Title`, `ExpectedCharacters` and `ExpectedLocations` and `RequestedStages` as jsonb arrays, `TtlSeconds=600`, `AnnouncedAt=now()`, `ExpiresAt=now()+interval '10 minutes'`) plus `DeliveredAt=now()`, `WorkingDeadlineAt=now()+interval '10 minutes 30 seconds'`, `Flags='[]'` and a `DeliveryPayload` that is a valid camelCase `Episode` JSON with `id: 0`, matching `season`/`episodeNumber`, a non-empty `transcriptText` and `sessionId` equal to the row id; then watch `docker compose logs -f api` for `adopted orphaned session` followed by the TR-39 line `Session <id> Working -> Done`. Timeout check, with no product code: `ClaudeDeepAnalysisService` hardcodes `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`, so write a throwaway compose override in the scratchpad (not committed) for the `api` service with environment `Station__AnalysisProvider=Claude`, `Anthropic__ApiKey=timeout-check` (any non-blank value; the request never reaches Anthropic, and a blank key would fall back to Stub in Development per TR-50), `Station__ProcessingTimeout=00:00:10`, and `extra_hosts: ["api.anthropic.com:10.255.255.1"]` so the TCP connect hangs on a non-routable address while the HttpClient timeout is infinite (TR-46); recreate with `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f <override> up -d api`, announce and deliver an episode through the API (F4.1), and confirm the row ends Failed 'processing timeout' about 10 s after `job start` and the slot is released in `GET /api/station`. Shutdown check: repeat with `Station__ProcessingTimeout=00:02:00`, deliver, and within the window run `docker compose stop api`; the in-flight call is cancelled by the stopping token and the row stays Working. Note the single-instance rule (TR-66): do not run `dotnet run` against the compose database while the container is up. This ticket produces evidence, not code; restore the stack with the plain `docker compose up -d` afterwards.
acceptance_criteria: PR description contains the psql INSERT used and a `docker compose logs api` excerpt showing `adopted orphaned session <id>` no later than 30 s after the insert, followed by `Session <id> Working -> Done`, and `GET /api/manifests/<id>` returning `state: "Done"` with `episodeId` set (TR-43).

review_notes: F5.2-T1 depended on F1.1/F1.2/F3.2/F5.1 but its acceptance criteria are xunit tests using FakeTimeProvider in AdventureTime.Tests, which only exists after F2.4 (TR-67). Added F2.4 to depends_on.

F5.2-T1 cited A8 (a StationSweeper decision) as the source of the worker's loop-survival rule; the binding requirement is TR-43. Corrected the citation.

F5.2-T1 criterion used a relative grep path and a bare `dotnet run` against the compose database, which TR-66 forbids while the api container is up. Gave the full path and required the api container to be stopped.

F5.2-T4 worked around a lost first tick by polling with Task.Yield; the real fix is that the PeriodicTimer must be created before the first await in ExecuteAsync so a FakeTimeProvider.Advance issued after StartAsync is observed. Moved that rule into F5.2-T1 and removed the polling workaround.

Defined the worker's `cancelled by shutdown` line in T3 and asserted its absence in T5.

F5.2-T3 left its fake-store DbUpdateException criterion unnamed and did not say what happens when FailAsync itself throws (TR-61: attempted once, then logged). Named it `Complete_StoreExceptionFailsOnce` and specified the log-and-swallow. Re-estimated S to M.

F5.2-T4 `OrphanScan_SkipsInFlightJob` held the job with `StubDelay = 30 s` and then 'released' StubDelay; StubDelay is a static TimeSpan read once by Task.Delay and cannot be released, and a 30 s real-time hold makes the suite slow. features.title: Rehydration at boot and observability
features.summary: Add the unconditional boot block to `AdventureTime/Program.cs` after `MapHealthChecks` and before `app.Run()`: `MigrateAsync`, then `FailInterruptedAsync` with the rehydration count logged, and append `public partial class Program {}` for the test host. Waiting rows are never touched and no hosted service is involved. Audit the whole logging surface against TR-64: transition lines per affected row, announce refusals with occupancy/retry-after, worker job start/end with elapsed ms, orphan adoptions, `TryEnqueue` false and `LostSlot` at Warning, sweeper/worker errors, provider/fallback lines; `/health` must not query `Sessions`. Verified by killing the process mid-analysis and restarting.

tickets.title: Add unconditional MigrateAsync + FailInterrupted boot block to Program.cs
tickets.context: Mechanism five, rehydration, wired into Program.cs between migration and the first request.
tickets.motivation: Failing interrupted Working rows has to happen after the schema is current and before Kestrel accepts a request or a hosted service starts. A hosted service cannot guarantee that ordering because the host starts listening at its first await; a synchronous block in Program.cs can. The partial Program class is what lets the test host boot the real startup.
tickets.goal: Migrate, then fail interrupted with the count logged, before app.Run, plus the partial class declaration.
tickets.value: A restart never changes what is on the air except to fail work that was genuinely interrupted, and the end-to-end tests boot the same startup path production uses.
tickets.description: In /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime/Program.cs replace the block that sits between `app.MapHealthChecks("/health")` and `app.Run()` (today an `if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())` scope calling `context.Database.EnsureCreated()`; if the F1.3 ticket for TR-13 step 4 already swapped it for a bare `await db.Database.MigrateAsync()`, extend that block) with the exact code of TR-48: one `using (var scope = app.Services.CreateScope())`, `await db.Database.MigrateAsync()` on the scoped `AppDbContext`, then `var failed = await store.FailInterruptedAsync(CancellationToken.None)` on the scoped `IStationStore`, then `app.Logger.LogInformation("rehydration: {Count} Working sessions failed as 'interrupted by restart'", failed)`. The block is unconditional (no environment gate), is not a hosted service, leaves `HostOptions.ServicesStartConcurrently` at its default false, and never touches Waiting rows; because hosted services only start inside `app.Run()`, it runs strictly before `StationSweeper` and `AnalysisWorker` (A18/A19, invariant I9 of TR-57). Append `public partial class Program {}` as the last line so `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` (TR-67/TR-70) can reference the entry point. Add `using AdventureTime.Application.Interfaces;` and `using AdventureTime.Infrastructure.Data;` at the top instead of the fully-qualified `AdventureTime.Infrastructure.Data.AppDbContext` used today. Gotchas: `FailInterruptedAsync` is the `Sessions.FromSql(... RETURNING *)` statement of TR-36/TR-39 and already logs one `Session {SessionId} Working -> Failed (interrupted by restart); rows=1` line per row, so the summary line is in addition to those; the `AddStation` migration (TR-13 step 3) must already exist or `MigrateAsync` has nothing to apply; if Postgres is unreachable at boot the exception must propagate and end the process (compose `restart: unless-stopped` retries it) rather than being swallowed. Reference: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2dc9531c-3f0b-499f-8ec6-fb2cf3271341#TR-48
acceptance_criteria: `grep -n "EnsureCreated\|IsDevelopment()" AdventureTime/Program.cs` shows no `EnsureCreated` call and the only `IsDevelopment()` hit is the Swagger block; the schema/rehydration block has no environment gate, appears after `app.MapHealthChecks("/health")` and before `app.Run()`, and its statements are in the order MigrateAsync -> FailInterruptedAsync -> LogInformation (TR-48)
The last line of AdventureTime/Program.cs is `public partial class Program {}` and `dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` succeeds with zero errors (TR-48)

Against an empty database (`docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d --build`), `docker compose logs api` shows EF's `Applying migration '<timestamp>_AddStation'` line, then `rehydration: 0 Working sessions failed as 'interrupted by restart'`, and no `StationSweeper`/`AnalysisWorker` line precedes the rehydration line; `SELECT "MigrationId" FROM "__EFMigrationsHistory"` returns a row ending in `_AddStation` (TR-48)

Given one row inserted by SQL with `"State"='Working'` and a non-null `"DeliveryPayload"` and one row with `"State"='Waiting'` (both `row_to_json` snapshots saved), `docker compose restart api` logs `rehydration: 1 Working sessions failed as 'interrupted by restart'`; the Working row now has `"State"='Failed'`, `"Reason"='interrupted by restart'`, `"EndedAt" IS NOT NULL`, `"DeliveryPayload" IS NULL`; the Waiting row's `row_to_json` is identical to its snapshot (TR-48)
`grep -n "ServicesStartConcurrently\|AddHostedService" AdventureTime/Program.cs` returns nothing: rehydration is not a hosted service and no host option is changed in Program.cs (TR-48)

Immediately after the restart of the previous criterion, `SELECT count(*)::int FROM "Sessions" WHERE "State" IN ('Waiting','Working')` returns 1 (the Waiting row only), proving the failed Working row released its slot without any sweeper tick (TR-48, TR-2)

tickets.title: Test restart mid-analysis fails the Working row as 'interrupted by restart'
tickets.context: Two consecutive test hosts over the same container database, the first stopped with a job in flight.
tickets.motivation: The crash story has to be demonstrated at host level: a session mid-analysis at shutdown is Failed with 'interrupted by restart' when the next host boots, and a Waiting session in the same table is untouched. This is the invariant that makes restarts safe.
tickets.goal: A rehydration test that passes on a clean container.
tickets.value: The one behavior an operator will rely on during a deploy is proven, not described.
tickets.description: Add /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Tests/Hosting/RehydrationTests.cs (xunit, in the `PostgresFixture` collection of TR-67) that proves invariant I9 at the host level, which is the WP5 definition of done 'kill mid-analysis and restart yields interrupted by restart'. Use two consecutive `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` instances against the same container database, each configured like TR-70(e): `RemoveAll<IDeepAnalysisService>()` + `AddSingleton<IDeepAnalysisService, StubDeepAnalysisService>()`, `RemoveAll<TimeProvider>()` + `FakeTimeProvider`, `ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection` pointed at the container, `Station:Capacity = 2`. Before building the first factory set `StubDeepAnalysisService.StubDelay = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5)` (internal static, reachable through `InternalsVisibleTo`, TR-47/TR-51) so the job blocks inside `AnalyzeEpisodeAsync`; through HTTP announce S11E01, deliver a valid body (202), announce S11E02 and leave it Waiting, capture `GET /api/manifests/{S11E02 id}` as the baseline, then `Dispose()` the first factory: the host's stopping token cancels the stub's `Task.Delay` and TR-45 row 1 writes nothing, so S11E01 is still Working in the database (assert this with a direct `AppDbContext` query before the second boot). Build the second factory: its Program.cs boot block (F5.3-T1) runs `FailInterruptedAsync` before the worker's orphan scan can adopt the row. Reset `StubDelay` to `TimeSpan.Zero` in a `finally` because the field is static and shared with every other test in the process. Gotchas: the second host's `MigrateAsync` is a no-op against the already-migrated container; with `FakeTimeProvider` the second host's orphan scan never fires unless the test advances time, which the last criterion does deliberately. Reference: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2dc9531c-3f0b-499f-8ec6-fb2cf3271341#TR-48
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests --filter FullyQualifiedName~RehydrationTests` passes on a clean Testcontainers Postgres (TR-48)

After the first factory is disposed and before the second is built, the test asserts via `AppDbContext` that S11E01 is `Working` with `DeliveryPayload IS NOT NULL` (the shutdown wrote nothing, TR-45) and S11E02 is `Waiting` (TR-48)

After the second factory is built, `GET /api/manifests/{S11E01 id}` returns 200 with `state == "Failed"`, `reason == "interrupted by restart"` and non-null `endedAt`; a direct query shows `"DeliveryPayload" IS NULL` (TR-48)

After the second factory is built, `GET /api/manifests/{S11E02 id}` returns `state == "Waiting"` with `expiresAt`, `announcedAt` and `ttlSeconds` equal to the values captured from `GET /api/manifests/{S11E02 id}` on the first host, and `SELECT count(*)::int FROM "Sessions" WHERE "State" IN ('Waiting','Working')` returns 1 (TR-48, TR-2)

After `FakeTimeProvider.Advance(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(35))` on the second host (one orphan-scan period) and a 2 s grace wait, S11E01 is still `Failed` with the same `endedAt`: the worker never adopts a row that rehydration already failed (TR-48)
The test resets `StubDeepAnalysisService.StubDelay` to `TimeSpan.Zero` in a `finally`, and the full `dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests` run stays green with this test included (TR-48)

tickets.title: Audit and complete the station logging surface against TR-64
tickets.context: An audit of every station component against the logging requirements, fixing gaps in place.
tickets.motivation: Every transition, refusal, tick, job start and end, adoption, lost enqueue and lost slot needs a line in one uniform format, or the logs cannot be grepped when something goes wrong at three in the morning. The health endpoint must stay a liveness check that never queries the Sessions table, or a slow database makes the app look dead.
tickets.goal: A consistent logging surface across the store, handlers, sweeper and worker, and a query-free health check.
tickets.value: The station is operable from logs alone, and what the logs say agrees with what the board shows.
tickets.description: Walk every station component and make the logging surface match TR-64 exactly, fixing gaps in place rather than adding a new abstraction. (1) /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationStore.cs: every transition path (`ExpireOverdueAsync` set-based and id-scoped, `FailOverdueWorkingAsync`, `FailInterruptedAsync`, `TryBeginWorkAsync`, `CancelAsync`, `FailAsync`, `CompleteAsync` step 1, and inside `AnnounceAsync` the step 2 expirations plus the step 6 insert logged as `(new) -> Waiting`) emits one Information line per affected row with the TR-39 template `Session {SessionId} {FromState} -> {ToState} ({Reason}); rows={Rows}`; `FailAsync` with 0 rows logs at Information; `CompleteAsync` returning `LostSlot` logs `lost slot` at Warning (TR-38). (2) AdventureTime.Application/Commands/Manifests/AnnounceManifest/AnnounceManifestCommandHandler.cs: log each refusal at Information with the outcome (`LiveConflict`/`EpisodeExists` -> 409, `Full` -> 429) and, for `Full`, the `Occupancy` and `RetryAfterSeconds` placeholders. (3) AdventureTime.Application/Commands/Manifests/DeliverEpisode/DeliverEpisodeCommandHandler.cs: `TryEnqueue` returning false is `LogWarning` with the session id and is not an error path (TR-31). (4) AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/AnalysisWorker.cs: `RunJobAsync` logs `job {SessionId} started` and, in a `finally`, `job {SessionId} ended outcome={Outcome} elapsedMs={ElapsedMs}` measured with `Stopwatch.GetTimestamp()`/`Stopwatch.GetElapsedTime` so timeout and error paths also get an end line; the TR-44 step 2 `dropped` line for a missing/non-Working row; the orphan scan logs `adopted orphaned session {SessionId}` (TR-43); `LostSlot`/`EpisodeExists` outcomes at Warning (TR-44); both loops log caught exceptions with `LogError(ex, ...)` and continue. (5) AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationSweeper.cs: the per-tick catch is `LogError(ex, "sweeper tick failed")` and never rethrows (TR-41). (6) AdventureTime/Program.cs: confirm the TR-50 lines after `builder.Build()` (`analysis provider: {Effective}` at Information, `FallbackReason` at Warning) and the rehydration count line from F5.3-T1 exist. (7) `/health`: `builder.Services.AddHealthChecks()` stays with no registered checks (no `AddDbContextCheck`/`AddNpgSql`), so the Docker `HEALTHCHECK` in /Users/steven/AdventureTime/Dockerfile keeps hitting a query-free liveness endpoint. Gotchas: use structured message templates (named placeholders), never string interpolation; never log `DeliveryPayload`, transcript text or API keys; do not change log levels the TRD fixes (Warning for `TryEnqueue` false and `LostSlot`, Error for loop exceptions, Information for transitions and refusals). Reference: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2dc9531c-3f0b-499f-8ec6-fb2cf3271341#TR-64
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn "Session {SessionId} {FromState} -> {ToState} ({Reason}); rows={Rows}" AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationStore.cs` returns at least one hit (a literal or a single shared constant), the reviewer can trace each of the nine transition paths (set-based expire, id-scoped expire, fail-overdue-working, fail-interrupted, try-begin-work, cancel, fail, complete step 1, announce insert) to a call that logs with that template at Information, and `dotnet build AdventureTime.sln` reports no CA2254 (non-constant template) warning in any file under `AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station` (TR-64, TR-39)

With the compose stack up (default `Station:Capacity` 3, Stub provider) and `curl` used to announce S11E01, deliver a valid body and poll to Done, `docker compose logs api` shows, in order: `analysis provider: Stub`, the rehydration count line, `Session <id> (new) -> Waiting`, `Session <id> Waiting -> Working`, `job <id> started`, `Session <id> Working -> Done`, `job <id> ended outcome=Completed elapsedMs=<int>` (TR-64)

Then announcing S11E02, S11E03, S11E04 (three Waiting) and S11E05 returns 429 for S11E05 and `docker compose logs api` contains one Information line for that refusal naming occupancy 3 and a retry-after value equal to the integer in the response's `Retry-After` header; announcing S11E02 again returns 409 and logs a refusal line naming the live conflict (TR-64)

Inserting a Working row by SQL and waiting up to 30 s logs `adopted orphaned session <id>` at Information; `grep -n "LogWarning" AdventureTime.Application/Commands/Manifests/DeliverEpisode/DeliverEpisodeCommandHandler.cs` shows the `TryEnqueue` false line with a `{SessionId}` placeholder; `grep -n "LogWarning" AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/StationStore.cs` shows the lost-slot line in `CompleteAsync` (TR-64, TR-31, TR-38)

`docker compose stop postgres` while the api runs produces `sweeper tick failed` lines at Error once per `Station:SweepInterval` and the process stays alive (`curl -i http://localhost:5256/health` still 200); `docker compose start postgres` resumes error-free ticks without an api restart (TR-64, TR-41)

`curl -i http://localhost:5256/health` returns 200 and, with `Logging__LogLevel__Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore=Information` (already set in docker-compose.yml), `docker compose logs api` shows no `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command` entry timestamped during the call; `grep -n "AddHealthChecks" AdventureTime/Program.cs` shows the bare call with no `.Add*Check` chained (TR-64)

`grep -rn "DeliveryPayload\|TranscriptText\|ApiKey" --include=*.cs AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station AdventureTime.Application/Commands | grep -i "Log"` returns no logging call: no payload, transcript or secret reaches a log line (TR-64)

tickets.title: Add host-level tests asserting TR-64 log lines and a query-free /health
tickets.context: A capturing logger provider registered into the test host so log lines can be asserted.
tickets.motivation: Log formats drift silently. Asserting that the transition, refusal and job lines exist with their expected shape keeps them stable for anyone who has built a grep or a dashboard on them. Asserting that health does not touch Sessions keeps liveness cheap.
tickets.goal: Tests for the required log lines and for a query-free health endpoint.
tickets.value: Observability becomes a tested contract rather than a convention.
tickets.description: Add /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Tests/Hosting/ObservabilityTests.cs (xunit, `PostgresFixture` collection of TR-67) plus a small `CapturingLoggerProvider : ILoggerProvider` in /Users/steven/AdventureTime/AdventureTime.Tests/Hosting/CapturingLoggerProvider.cs that records `(Category, LogLevel, Message)` into a `ConcurrentQueue` (hosted services log from other threads; `IsEnabled` returns true for every level). Register it through `WithWebHostBuilder(b => b.ConfigureLogging(l => l.AddProvider(provider)))` on a `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` configured as in TR-70(e) (stub provider, `FakeTimeProvider`, container connection string, `Station:Capacity = 2`), and additionally set `Logging:LogLevel:Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command` to `Information` through `ConfigureAppConfiguration` (in-memory collection) so EF command text is captured. Drive the station through `POST/GET/DELETE /api/manifests` and assert the captured lines rather than inspecting internals: the boot lines (`analysis provider: Stub`, `rehydration: 0 Working sessions failed as 'interrupted by restart'`), the per-row transition lines of TR-39, the 429 refusal line with occupancy and retry-after, the worker job start/end lines with an integer `elapsedMs`, the sweeper's `Waiting -> TimedOut (ttl elapsed)` line after `UPDATE "Sessions" SET "ExpiresAt" = now() - interval '1 second'` and `FakeTimeProvider.Advance(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(16))`, and that `GET /health` emits no EF command touching `"Sessions"`. Poll with a bounded timeout wherever the line is produced by a hosted service (10 s for worker lines, 5 s for the sweeper line, as in TR-70 steps 8 and 11). Gotchas: run the fixture's `TRUNCATE` before building the factory or the `rehydration: 0` assertion depends on test order; snapshot the queue count before the `/health` call and inspect only entries appended after it; compare the refusal line against the `Retry-After` header value returned by the 429, not a hard-coded number; boot lines are only captured because `ConfigureLogging` runs before the host is built. Reference: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2dc9531c-3f0b-499f-8ec6-fb2cf3271341#TR-64
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests --filter FullyQualifiedName~ObservabilityTests` passes on a clean Testcontainers Postgres (TR-64)

After factory creation the captured log contains an Information entry matching `analysis provider: Stub` and one matching `rehydration: 0 Working sessions failed as 'interrupted by restart'` (TR-64, TR-48)

After announce + deliver + polling `GET /api/manifests/{id}` to Done (<= 10 s), the captured log contains Information entries `Session <id> (new) -> Waiting`, `Session <id> Waiting -> Working`, `Session <id> Working -> Done` each ending in `rows=1`, and worker entries `job <id> started` and `job <id> ended outcome=Completed elapsedMs=<n>` where `<n>` parses as a non-negative integer (TR-64)

With two live manifests at `Capacity = 2`, a third announce returns 429 and the captured log contains an Information entry naming occupancy 2 and a retry-after value equal to the integer in the response's `Retry-After` header (TR-64)

After `UPDATE "Sessions" SET "ExpiresAt" = now() - interval '1 second'` on a Waiting row and `FakeTimeProvider.Advance(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(16))`, within 5 s the captured log contains `Session <id> Waiting -> TimedOut (ttl elapsed); rows=1` at Information (TR-64)

`GET /health` returns 200 and, among entries captured after the call, no entry with category `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command` contains the text `"Sessions"` (the expected count of such entries is zero) (TR-64)

review_notes: F5.3-T1 AC 6 verified slot release through `GET /api/station`, which needs the StationController (F4.1) that the ticket does not depend on; replaced with the TR-2 occupancy query (`SELECT count(*)::int FROM "Sessions" WHERE "State" IN ('Waiting','Working')`) so the criterion is verifiable with only the declared dependencies.

F5.3-T1 AC 1 was self-contradicting: the grep for `IsDevelopment()` will always hit the Swagger block in Program.cs; reworded so the only permitted hit is the Swagger block and the schema/rehydration block itself has no gate.

F5.3-T1 AC 3 named the migration as `AddStation`; the EF migration id is `<timestamp>_AddStation` and the visible evidence is EF's `Applying migration '<timestamp>_AddStation'` line (EF is at Information in docker-compose.yml) plus the `__EFMigrationsHistory` row; criterion made precise.

F5.3-T1 did not spell out that the F1.3 ticket implementing TR-13 step 4 (the `MigrateAsync` replacement) and the `AddStation` migration must exist first; this is covered transitively through F2.1-T3 (StationStore needs `DbSet<Session>`), so no key was added, but the description now says which block to extend and that `AddStation` must already be generated.

F5.3-T2 and F5.3-T4 drive the station through `POST/GET /api/manifests`, which is the ManifestsController of F4.1 (TR-52), yet neither ticket depended on F4.1; added `F4.1-T1` (assumed to be the ManifestsController ticket; reconcile the number against F4.1's actual list).

F5.3-T2 AC 4 claimed `announcedAt` and `ttlSeconds` could be captured from the 201 body; TR-16 says the 201 body carries only id/state/expiresAt/occupancy/capacity, so the baseline is now captured from `GET /api/manifests/{id}` on the first host. Its `GET /api/station` occupancy check was replaced with the TR-2 SQL count to avoid a second undeclared controller dependency.
F5.3-T2 embedded a compose-based manual procedure inside a test ticket with no acceptance criterion; it duplicates F5.3-T1 AC 4 (SQL-inserted Working row + restart) and was removed from T2.
F5.3-T2 AC 6 required the full test run to stay green 'alongside the E2E test' (F5.4, a downstream feature); reworded to the full `dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests` run at the time of the ticket.

F5.3-T3 description used project-relative paths without the project prefix (`Infrastructure/Station/StationStore.cs`, `Application/Commands/...`); corrected to `AdventureTime.Infrastructure/Station/...` and `AdventureTime.Application/Commands/Manifests/...` (the TR-26 per-command folder idiom), matching the paths in its own acceptance criteria.

F5.3-T3 AC 2 was verified by 'running the F5.4 end-to-end scenario', i.e. by a ticket of a feature that depends on F5.3; replaced with a self-contained curl sequence against the compose stack (default Capacity 3) that produces the same log ordering and the 429 refusal line.

F5.3-T3 AC 1 assumed a grep would prove the TR-39 template is used on every transition path; a single shared template constant is the likely implementation and grep cannot prove per-path use. Reworded to grep for the template once plus a reviewer trace of the nine call sites, keeping the CA2254 build check.
F5.3-T3 omitted the TR-44 step 2 `dropped` line (worker sees a non-Working or missing row) from the AnalysisWorker audit list; added.
F5.3-T3 AC 6 grep would also match comments containing the words; reworded to 'no logging call' and kept the command as the screening step.

F5.3-T4 did not state that the `PostgresFixture` TRUNCATE must run before the factory is built, otherwise the `rehydration: 0 ...` assertion is order-dependent; added as a gotcha. features.title: End-to-end station scenario
features.summary: Write the TR-70 test in `AdventureTime.Tests` using `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` with `RemoveAll<IDeepAnalysisService>` + stub, `RemoveAll<TimeProvider>` + `FakeTimeProvider`, the Testcontainers connection string and `Station:Capacity = 2`. It walks all twelve steps: 201/409/400 on announce, 422 for season mismatch and missing transcript, 202 with `TitleMismatch` and `UnannouncedCharacter`, 409 on redelivery, polling to Done and checking `sessionId`/`continuityNotes`/`/api/station`, 429 with `Retry-After`, idempotent 204 cancel, sweeper-driven TimedOut via `FakeTimeProvider.Advance`, lazy 410, and the 410 from `POST /api/episodes`. tickets.title: Add StationWebApplicationFactory test host with stub, FakeTimeProvider and Capacity 2
tickets.context: A shared test host: the real application with the stub provider, a fake time provider, the container connection string and a capacity of two.
tickets.motivation: One factory means the end-to-end scenario and every other host-level test configure the application identically, so a difference in results is a difference in behavior rather than in setup.
tickets.goal: A factory class that boots the real startup path against the container with the test substitutions applied.
tickets.value: The full stack boots in-process, reproducibly, in a few seconds.
tickets.description: Create `AdventureTime.Tests/EndToEnd/StationWebApplicationFactory.cs`, a `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` (the `Program` type exists because F5.3 appends `public partial class Program {}` to `AdventureTime/Program.cs`, TR-48) whose constructor takes the F2.4 `PostgresFixture` and exposes `public FakeTimeProvider Time { get; } = new();` (package `Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing`, TR-67). tickets.title: Write Station_EndToEnd_Scenario steps 1-8: announce, reject, deliver, poll to Done
tickets.context: The one demo every epic composes: real HTTP calls through the test host, from announcement to a Done session.
tickets.motivation: Announce, refuse a duplicate, reject a bad body, reject a mismatched delivery, accept a delivery with flags, refuse a second delivery, poll to Done and read the analysis with its continuity note. Each step is a mechanism; passing them in sequence proves they compose.
tickets.goal: Steps one to eight of the scenario green.
tickets.value: The product works end to end, and there is a single test that says so.
tickets.description: Create `AdventureTime.Tests/EndToEnd/StationScenarioTests.cs` (same `[Collection]` and factory lifecycle as T1) with one `[Fact] public async Task Station_EndToEnd_Scenario()` that calls `ResetAsync()` first and keeps every step in this single method, because TR-70 is the one demo every epic composes (T3 appends steps 9-12 to the same method). Steps 1-3 use the TR-16 example body `{season:11, episodeNumber:1, title:"The Unfinished Map", focusCharacter:"Finn", expectedCharacters:["Finn","Jake","BMO"], expectedLocations:["Tree Fort"], ttlSeconds:600}`: 201 (capture `id`), then 409 with `manifestId == id` (TR-16 live conflict), then 400 when `"transcriptText":"x"` is added (`JsonUnmappedMemberHandling.Disallow`, TR-16). Build the delivery body as a mutable `JsonObject` with the same member names as `AdventureTime/Episodes/s11e01__the_unfinished_map.json` but hand-built values (do NOT send the seed file verbatim; its cast differs and would add extra flags): title, season 11, episodeNumber 1, productionCode `FAN-1101`, airDate `2026-09-14T00:00:00Z`, runtimeMinutes 11.0, focusCharacter Finn, synopsis, plot, majorCharacters [Finn, Jake], minorCharacters [BMO], locations [Tree Fort], dialogueLineCount, non-empty transcriptText. Steps 4-5 mutate copies (season 12; `transcriptText` member removed) and expect 422 with the TR-19 messages and the row still Waiting; step 6 delivers with title `The Unfinished Map (Part 1)` and minorCharacters [BMO, Marceline] and expects 202 with `TitleMismatch` and `UnannouncedCharacter` (TR-24); step 7 repeats it for 409 (A12); step 8 polls to Done and checks the episode, its analysis (`GET api/episodes/{id:int}/analysis`, re-routed by TR-22, returns the domain `EpisodeAnalysis` so `continuityNotes` is top-level) and `/api/station`. Gotchas: the worker is driven by the channel, not the fake clock, and `StubDelay` is zero, so step 8 needs no `Advance`; all bodies are camelCase and `state` is a string; read responses with `JsonDocument`/`JsonNode`, never the production DTO types; keep the manifest id and episode id in locals for T3.
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests --filter FullyQualifiedName~StationScenarioTests` passes and the test makes real HTTP calls through `StationWebApplicationFactory` against the Testcontainers database (TR-70).

Step 1 asserts status 201, `state == "Waiting"`, `occupancy == 1`, `capacity == 2` and a `Location` header ending in `/api/manifests/{id}`; step 2 asserts 409 and `manifestId == id`; step 3 asserts 400 for the announce body containing `transcriptText` (TR-70 steps 1-3; TR-16).

Step 4 asserts 422 with `reasons` containing `season 12 does not match manifest season 11` and a subsequent `GET /api/manifests/{id}` showing `Waiting`; step 5 asserts the status is 422 and explicitly not 400, `reasons` contains `transcriptText is required`, and the row is still `Waiting` (TR-70 steps 4-5; TR-15, TR-19, TR-20).

Step 6 asserts 202, `flags[].code` includes both `TitleMismatch` and `UnannouncedCharacter`, `workingDeadlineAt` is non-null, and `Location` ends in `/api/manifests/{id}`; step 7 asserts 409 with `state` equal to `Working` or `Done` (TR-70 steps 6-7; TR-20, TR-24).

Step 8 polls `GET /api/manifests/{id}` every 100 ms for at most 10 s with `PollUntilAsync` until `state == "Done"`, then asserts `episodeId` is an int, `GET /api/episodes/{episodeId}` has `sessionId == id` and `title == "The Unfinished Map (Part 1)"`, `GET /api/episodes/{episodeId}/analysis` has `continuityNotes == []`, and `GET /api/station` has `occupancy == 0` and `recent[0].id == id` (TR-70 step 8; TR-17, TR-21, TR-22).

The test class carries the shared Postgres `[Collection]` attribute from T1, and the whole `dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests` run (unit + integration + E2E) passes twice in a row, proving `ResetAsync()` leaves no state behind (TR-67).

Assertions read responses as `JsonDocument`/`JsonNode` only; no `AdventureTime.Application` DTO type is referenced from the test file (reviewer greps `StationScenarioTests.cs` for `Dtos.Manifests` and finds nothing).

tickets.title: Extend Station_EndToEnd_Scenario with steps 9-12: 429, cancel, sweeper expiry, 410s
tickets.context: The second half of the scenario: capacity, cancellation, expiry under the fake clock, and the 410 outcomes.
tickets.motivation: Backpressure and expiry are the mechanisms that only show themselves under load and time. Filling the station to get a 429 with Retry-After, cancelling to free a slot, advancing the clock so the sweeper times a manifest out, and then delivering to it to get a 410 exercises everything the first half could not.
tickets.goal: Steps nine to twelve green.
tickets.value: The complete contract, full station, release, timeout and late delivery, demonstrated over HTTP.
tickets.description: Append steps 9-12 to `Station_EndToEnd_Scenario` in `AdventureTime.Tests/EndToEnd/StationScenarioTests.cs`, continuing from the Done S11E01 manifest of T2. Step 9 announces S11E02 `{season:11, episodeNumber:2, title:"Jake's Nap", focusCharacter:"Jake", expectedCharacters:["Jake","Finn","BMO"], ttlSeconds:600}` and S11E03 `{season:11, episodeNumber:3, title:"Low Battery", focusCharacter:"BMO", expectedCharacters:["BMO","Finn","Jake"], ttlSeconds:600}` (focus character must be in `expectedCharacters`, TR-16), then a third announce for S11E04 (`The Butler Did It`) that must hit 429 with `Retry-After` (A3, TR-16, TR-52: emitted from `RetryAfterSeconds` as a delta, so read `response.Headers.RetryAfter.Delta` or parse the raw header as an integer). Step 10 exercises the idempotent cancel of TR-18 on S11E02 and the 409 on the Done S11E01. Step 11 runs `UPDATE "Sessions" SET "ExpiresAt" = now() - interval '1 second' WHERE "Id" = '{S11E03}'` through `ExecuteSqlAsync` (scoped to S11E03 so the Done and Cancelled rows are untouched), calls `factory.Time.Advance(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(16))` — one tick over the 15 s `Station:SweepInterval` pinned in T1 (TR-41) — and polls to `TimedOut`, because the tick only releases the sweeper loop whose `ExpireOverdueAsync(null)` runs asynchronously on the hosted service; the following delivery to S11E03 reuses the step-6 body with season 11 / episodeNumber 3 and is asserted immediately without polling, because the handler's id-scoped `ExpireOverdue` and state check run before validation (TR-28), so the body content cannot change the 410. Step 12 posts `{}` to `POST /api/episodes` for the TR-22 410 and finishes with `GET /api/station` showing an empty `live` array. Gotchas: keep the advance at exactly 16 s so exactly one sweeper tick fires and the worker's 30 s orphan scan (TR-43) stays idle; the 10 min `ProcessingTimeout` deadline CTS is untouched; use only the bounded `PollUntilAsync` helper for waiting, never bare `Task.Delay`.
acceptance_criteria: Step 9 asserts 201 for S11E02 and S11E03 and, for the third announce, status 429, a `Retry-After` header that parses to an integer >= 1, and body `capacity == 2`, `occupancy == 2` (TR-70 step 9; TR-16, TR-52).
Step 10 asserts 204 for the first `DELETE /api/manifests/{S11E02}`, 204 again for the repeated `DELETE`, and 409 with `state == "Done"` for the `DELETE` of the S11E01 manifest (TR-70 step 10; TR-18).

Step 11 executes the `UPDATE "Sessions" SET "ExpiresAt" = now() - interval '1 second'` statement scoped to S11E03, calls `factory.Time.Advance(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(16))`, polls `GET /api/manifests/{S11E03}` every 100 ms for at most 5 s until `state == "TimedOut"`, asserts `reason == "ttl elapsed"`, and asserts a delivery to S11E03 returns 410 with `state == "TimedOut"` and `message == "manifest expired"` without any polling (TR-70 step 11; TR-20, TR-41).
Step 12 asserts `POST /api/episodes` returns 410 with `manifests == "/api/manifests"` and a `message` containing `announce a manifest` (TR-70 step 12; TR-22).

The final `GET /api/station` assertion shows `occupancy == 0`, an empty `live` array, and `recent` containing the S11E01 (Done), S11E02 (Cancelled) and S11E03 (TimedOut) ids with those states (TR-21, TR-70).

`dotnet test AdventureTime.Tests` passes with all twelve steps in the single `Station_EndToEnd_Scenario` test, the test's reported duration in the `dotnet test` output is under 60 s, and it passes on a second consecutive run (TR-70).

The only `factory.Time.Advance` call in the test is the 16 s advance of step 11, and no assertion in steps 9-12 depends on wall-clock sleeps other than the bounded `PollUntilAsync` helper (reviewer greps `StationScenarioTests.cs` for `Task.Delay` and `Advance` outside the helper).

review_notes: F5.4-T1: the justification for `AllowAutoRedirect = false` was wrong (HttpClient never auto-follows 201/202; only 3xx). Replaced `CreateApiClient()` with plain `CreateClient()` and stated the real fact: `app.UseHttpsRedirection()` in `AdventureTime/Program.cs` is a no-op under TestServer because no https port is configured, so no redirects ever occur.

F5.4-T1: the E2E relied on `Station:SweepInterval = 00:00:15` reaching the test host through the API project's `appsettings.json` content root; T3's `Advance(16 s)` depends on it. Added an explicit `UseSetting("Station:SweepInterval", "00:00:15")` so the single sweeper tick is deterministic regardless of appsettings.

F5.4-T1: the smoke test `Factory_Boots_WithStubAndFakeClock` had no file, and the factory lifecycle was unspecified (xunit v2 class fixtures cannot inject collection fixtures, so `IClassFixture<StationWebApplicationFactory>` cannot receive `PostgresFixture`). Named the file `AdventureTime.Tests/EndToEnd/StationFactorySmokeTests.cs` and specified per-class construction from the injected `PostgresFixture` with disposal in `IAsyncLifetime.DisposeAsync`.
F5.4-T1: acceptance criterion on the shared `[Collection]` attribute named no requirement; added (TR-67), which defines the `PostgresFixture` collection fixture.

F5.4-T2: the step-6 criterion asserted `Location` equals `/api/manifests/{id}`; `CreatedAtAction`/`AcceptedAtAction` emit an absolute URL (`http://localhost/api/manifests/{id}`) under TestServer. Changed both the 201 and 202 checks to `Location` ending in `/api/manifests/{id}` (the path form given in TR-16/TR-20).

F5.4-T2: the description said the delivery body is 'shaped like' `AdventureTime/Episodes/s11e01__the_unfinished_map.json` but listed a different cast; the real file carries majorCharacters [Finn, Jake, Princess Bubblegum] and minorCharacters [Banana Guard, Cartographer Snail, Cinnamon Bun], which would add extra `UnannouncedCharacter`/`CharacterAbsent` flags. Clarified that the body is hand-built with the same member names, not the seed file verbatim.

F5.4-T2: step-9 announce bodies for S11E02/S11E03 were unspecified; TR-16 requires `focusCharacter` to be one of `expectedCharacters`, so a careless body yields 400 instead of 201. Added bodies consistent with `s11e02__jake_s_nap.json` and `s11e03__low_battery.json` (moved to T3 where step 9 lives).

F5.4-T3: the gotcha 'do not Advance past 30 s or the orphan scan will log adoptions mid-test' is inaccurate: at step 11 no Working rows exist, so `GetWorkingIdsAsync` returns nothing and no adoption is logged. Reworded to the accurate reason: keep exactly one sweeper tick (15 s period, TR-41) and leave the 30 s orphan scan (TR-43) idle.

F5.4-T3: the 410 delivery after expiry did not say what body to send; per TR-28 the state check (410) precedes `DeliveryValidator` (422), so any syntactically valid body works. Stated that the step-6 body with season 11 / episodeNumber 3 is reused and why its content is irrelevant.
F5.4-T3: the final `GET /api/station` criterion named no requirement; added (TR-21, TR-70).

F5.4-T3: 'completes in under 60 s wall-clock' was ambiguous because the Testcontainers start is attributed to the collection fixture, not the test; clarified as the test's reported duration in `dotnet test` output.
F5.4-T2/T3: descriptions were far longer than the 3-8 sentence convention; condensed them and moved per-step assertions into the acceptance criteria, keeping every step and every gotcha.

features.title: Seed script and README
features.summary: Write `scripts/seed.sh` (bash, `set -euo pipefail`, curl + jq) that orders `AdventureTime/Episodes/*.json` by `(season, episodeNumber)` read from file contents (`s1e8__dungeon.json` carries `episodeNumber: 18`), builds each manifest with the mandated jq expression, announces with 429 sleep/retry and 409-episode-exists skip, delivers the file verbatim expecting 202, and polls to a terminal state, exiting non-zero unless Done. Add README sections "Upgrading to migrations" (the `down -v` reset of TR-14, no baseline path), a `Station` configuration table mirroring TR-63, and the single-instance statement of TR-66 (no local `dotnet run` against the compose database while the container runs).
