tickets.title: Write scripts/seed.sh: content-ordered announce, deliver and poll loop
tickets.context: The only way data enters the system is announce then deliver, and the seed must obey that rule like any other client.
tickets.motivation: A sequential script that announces, delivers, polls, and experiences 429 and 409 like any sender proves the design can seed itself through its own front door. Sequential order also makes continuity reproducible: episode ten always sees one to nine.
tickets.goal: A script that seeds all twenty-one episode files to Done through the public API.
tickets.value: A fresh clone gets a full database offline with the stub, and the script doubles as a worked example of how a client should behave.
tickets.description: Create the directory `scripts/` (it does not exist) and `/Users/steven/AdventureTime/scripts/seed.sh`, executable, `#!/usr/bin/env bash` with `set -euo pipefail`, requiring only `curl` and `jq` (fail fast with a message if either is missing). Defaults: `BASE_URL=${BASE_URL:-http://localhost:5256}` (the compose port mapping `5256:8080` in `docker-compose.yml`) and `EPISODES_DIR=${EPISODES_DIR:-AdventureTime/Episodes}` resolved against the repo root (`$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)`) so the script works from any cwd. Order the 21 files by `(season, episodeNumber)` read from the JSON contents, never by filename: `jq -r '[.season, .episodeNumber, input_filename] | @tsv' "$EPISODES_DIR"/*.json | sort -t$'\t' -k1,1n -k2,2n`; `s1e8__dungeon.json` carries `episodeNumber: 18` and must be the first file processed (S01E18), before `s11e01`. For each file, in this order: (1) build the manifest body with exactly the TRD jq expression `{season, episodeNumber, title, focusCharacter, expectedCharacters: ((.majorCharacters // []) + (.minorCharacters // []) + (if .focusCharacter then [.focusCharacter] else [] end) | unique), expectedLocations: (.locations // []), ttlSeconds: 600}` (the union guarantees the focusCharacter rule of TR-16) and `POST $BASE_URL/api/manifests`; on 429 read the `Retry-After` response header (capture headers with `curl -D`), `sleep` that many seconds and retry the same file; on 409 whose body `.message == "episode exists"` print a skip line and continue to the next file; any other status (including a 409 live conflict) is a hard failure with the body echoed to stderr and exit 1; otherwise take `.id` from the 201 body. (2) `POST $BASE_URL/api/manifests/$id/episode` with the file sent verbatim (`--data-binary @"$file"`, `Content-Type: application/json`) and require 202. (3) poll `GET $BASE_URL/api/manifests/$id` every 2 s until `.state` is one of `Done|Failed|TimedOut|Cancelled` (no artificial poll cap is needed: the working deadline of TR-4 bounds Working), then print one line `<id> <state> <reason> <flagCount>` with `flagCount = (.flags | length)`. Process files strictly sequentially so the continuity order is reproducible, keep done/failed/skipped counters, print `summary: done=<n> failed=<n> skipped=<n>` as the last line, and exit 1 unless every delivered session ended Done (skipped files do not count as failures). The header comment must document the one-time upgrade of TR-14 (`docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d --build && scripts/seed.sh`, for databases created by `EnsureCreated`) so the script is self-describing. Depends on the manifests API (F4.1) and the episodes controller rewrite (F4.2) being merged and the host booting through `MigrateAsync` + rehydration (F5.3).
acceptance_criteria: `scripts/seed.sh` exists at the repo root, is executable (`test -x scripts/seed.sh`), starts with `set -euo pipefail`, and `bash -n scripts/seed.sh` exits 0; the script exits non-zero with a clear message when `jq` or `curl` is not on PATH (TR-56)

With the API up and an empty database, the first announce line the script prints refers to season 1 episode 18 (`s1e8__dungeon.json`) and the remaining 20 follow in S11E01..S11E20 order, proving ordering comes from the `jq -r '[.season, .episodeNumber, input_filename] | @tsv' | sort -t$'\t' -k1,1n -k2,2n` pipeline over file contents, not filenames (TR-56)

For every seed file the announce body is produced by the exact jq expression from TRD 8.4 (reviewer diffs the expression), so `expectedCharacters` contains the focus character and `ttlSeconds` is 600; `jq '<expr>' AdventureTime/Episodes/s11e01__the_unfinished_map.json` outputs an object whose keys are exactly season, episodeNumber, title, focusCharacter, expectedCharacters, expectedLocations, ttlSeconds (TR-56, TR-16)

Announce handling: a 429 response causes the script to log the `Retry-After` value, sleep exactly that many seconds and retry the same file; a 409 with body `.message == "episode exists"` logs a skip and moves on; any other non-201 status (including a 409 live conflict) aborts the run with exit 1 and the response body on stderr (TR-56)
Delivery sends the file bytes unchanged (`--data-binary @"$file"`) to `POST /api/manifests/{id}/episode` and aborts with exit 1 on any status other than 202 (TR-56)

Polling hits `GET /api/manifests/{id}` every 2 s until `.state` is terminal and prints `<id> <state> <reason> <flagCount>` per session; the last line printed is `summary: done=<n> failed=<n> skipped=<n>`; when a session ends Failed, TimedOut or Cancelled the script still processes the remaining files and exits 1 at the end; when all delivered sessions end Done it exits 0 (TR-56)

The header comment of the script contains the three-command upgrade sequence `docker compose down -v`, `docker compose up -d --build`, `scripts/seed.sh` and states it is for databases created by `EnsureCreated` (TR-56, TR-14)

tickets.title: Verify seed.sh retry, skip and failure paths against the running API
tickets.context: The four branches a seed takes when things are not clean: retry on full, skip on episode exists, abort on a live conflict, exit non-zero on failure.
tickets.motivation: The non-happy branches are the ones that matter when a seed goes wrong at the worst moment. Exercising each once against the running stack and recording the output makes the script trustworthy rather than hopeful.
tickets.goal: Each branch observed firing, with commands and output recorded.
tickets.value: The seed will neither silently skip an episode nor loop forever, and a reviewer can see each branch behave.
tickets.description: Exercise the four non-happy branches of `scripts/seed.sh` (F6.1-T1) against the compose stack so a reviewer can see each branch fire, and record the exact commands and outputs in a comment block at the bottom of the script or in the PR description. Start from a fresh volume (`docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d --build`) and run the branches in this order, because the live-conflict and failure branches are only reachable while their (season, episodeNumber) is absent from `Episodes` (otherwise announce returns 409 `episode exists` and the script skips instead). (a) 409 live-conflict path: `curl -X POST localhost:5256/api/manifests` for S11E01 by hand (`ttlSeconds: 600`) and leave it Waiting, then run `scripts/seed.sh`: it seeds S01E18 to Done, then aborts with exit 1 on S11E01's `a live manifest exists for S11E01` body (the "otherwise require 201" branch of TR-56); afterwards `DELETE /api/manifests/{id}` the hand-made manifest (204). (b) 429 path: with `Station:Capacity` at its default 3, announce three throw-away manifests by hand for S99E01..S99E03 with `ttlSeconds: 60` (never delivered), then run `scripts/seed.sh`: S01E18 is skipped as `episode exists`, S11E01 must log the 429 with the `Retry-After` from the response, sleep, retry and get 201 once the 60 s TTL has elapsed (announce step 2 of TR-37 or the sweeper expires the three rows to TimedOut), and the run continues to 20 Done sessions. (c) 409-skip path: run `scripts/seed.sh` again on the now-seeded database; every file must be skipped with `episode exists` and the exit status must be 0. (d) Failure path: copy `AdventureTime/Episodes/s11e01__the_unfinished_map.json` into a scratch directory as the only file, rewrite it with `jq 'del(.transcriptText) | .season = 99 | .episodeNumber = 50'`, and run `EPISODES_DIR=<scratch> scripts/seed.sh`: the delivery must get 422 and the script must exit 1 with the `reasons` array on stderr; the rejected manifest stays Waiting (TR-20: nothing changes) and is cancelled by hand afterwards. No production code changes are expected; if a branch misbehaves, fix it in `scripts/seed.sh` under this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: With a hand-announced Waiting manifest for S11E01 on a fresh database, `scripts/seed.sh` seeds S01E18 to Done and then aborts with exit 1, printing the 409 body containing `a live manifest exists for S11E01` on stderr instead of skipping it (TR-56)

With three undelivered hand-made S99E01..S99E03 manifests (ttlSeconds 60) holding all 3 slots, `scripts/seed.sh` prints a line containing the 429 status and the numeric `Retry-After` it will sleep, does not exit, and after that sleep continues to a 201 for the same file and finishes the remaining files Done (TR-56)

Second run of `scripts/seed.sh` on an already-seeded database prints 21 `skip` lines mentioning `episode exists`, makes no delivery requests (no 202 lines), ends with `summary: done=0 failed=0 skipped=21`, and exits 0 (TR-56)

`EPISODES_DIR` pointing at a directory holding one S99E50 file with `transcriptText` removed yields a 422 from `POST /api/manifests/{id}/episode`, the script echoes the `reasons` array containing `transcriptText is required`, and `echo $?` is 1 (TR-56, TR-20)

After the failure-path run `GET /api/station` shows `occupancy == 1` with the S99E50 manifest in `live` with `state == "Waiting"` (the 422 wrote nothing); `DELETE /api/manifests/{id}` returns 204 and `GET /api/station` then shows `occupancy == 0` (TR-56, TR-20)

tickets.title: Create README: migrations upgrade, Station config and single-instance sections
tickets.context: The repository has no README. The three things an operator must know live only in the requirements document.
tickets.motivation: The one-time migration upgrade, the Station configuration keys, and the single-instance constraint are exactly the facts that will bite the next person who runs this on a machine with an old volume or tries a second instance against the same database.
tickets.goal: A README with a running section and the three mandated sections.
tickets.value: The upgrade step and the deployment constraint are where the next person will look, not buried in a design document.
tickets.description: The repository has no `README.md`; create `/Users/steven/AdventureTime/README.md` at the repo root. Give it a short "Running" section (`docker compose up -d --build`, API at `http://localhost:5256`, Swagger only in Development per `AdventureTime/Program.cs`, the manifest flow `POST /api/manifests` -> `POST /api/manifests/{id}/episode` -> poll `GET /api/manifests/{id}`, and `scripts/seed.sh` with its `BASE_URL`/`EPISODES_DIR` overrides for seeding), then three mandated sections. (1) H2 exactly `Upgrading to migrations` (TR-14): explain that schema is now managed by EF Core migrations and applied by `MigrateAsync` at boot, that a database created earlier by `EnsureCreated` has no `__EFMigrationsHistory` table and cannot be migrated in place, that the only supported path is the reset `docker compose down -v`, `docker compose up -d --build`, `scripts/seed.sh` (the `-v` removes the `adventuretime-data` volume named in `docker-compose.yml`), that for a local non-compose database the operator drops and recreates the `adventuretime` database, and state explicitly that no baseline-insert path is provided. (2) H2 `Configuration` with a `Station` table mirroring TR-63 row for row: `Station:Capacity` (int, 3, read at startup only, >= 1), `Station:SweepInterval` (TimeSpan, 00:00:15, > 0), `Station:ProcessingTimeout` (TimeSpan, 00:10:00, deadline CTS; DB deadline = +30 s), `Station:TtlDefault` (int s, 1800, TtlMin <= TtlDefault <= TtlMax), `Station:TtlMin` (60), `Station:TtlMax` (86400), `Station:AnalysisProvider` (`Stub|Claude|OpenAi`, default Stub, replaces the old `Claude` bool), plus the `Anthropic:ApiKey`/`Anthropic:Model`/`OpenAi:ApiKey`/`OpenAi:Model` row (required when that provider is selected outside Development) and `ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection`; show the compose environment spelling (`Station__Capacity`, and `STATION_ANALYSIS_PROVIDER` mapped to `Station__AnalysisProvider` per TR-55) and note that lowering Capacity never evicts live sessions (A4). (3) H2 `Single instance` (TR-66): exactly one application instance may run against a database; admission, expiry, delivery, cancel and Complete are DB-serialized, but the orphan scan and rehydration assume one instance (a second instance's boot fails the first instance's Working rows as `interrupted by restart`); therefore running `dotnet run` locally against the compose database while the `adventuretime-api` container is running is unsupported. Link each mandated section to the published TRD anchors (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2dc9531c-3f0b-499f-8ec6-fb2cf3271341#TR-14`, `#TR-63`, `#TR-66`) so the source of truth is one click away.
acceptance_criteria: `README.md` exists at the repo root and contains an H2 titled exactly `Upgrading to migrations` whose text includes the three commands `docker compose down -v`, `docker compose up -d --build` and `scripts/seed.sh` in that order, the local alternative of dropping and recreating the `adventuretime` database, and the sentence that no baseline-insert path is provided (TR-14)

The `Configuration` section contains a Markdown table with one row per key of TR-63: the seven `Station:*` keys with type, default and notes matching the TRD (Capacity 3, SweepInterval 00:00:15, ProcessingTimeout 00:10:00, TtlDefault 1800, TtlMin 60, TtlMax 86400, AnalysisProvider Stub), the Anthropic/OpenAi key+model row, and `ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection` (TR-63)

The configuration section documents the compose environment-variable spelling with double underscores (e.g. `Station__Capacity`) and the `STATION_ANALYSIS_PROVIDER` variable that `docker-compose.yml` maps to `Station__AnalysisProvider` (TR-63, TR-55)

The `Single instance` section states that exactly one application instance runs against a database, names the orphan scan and rehydration as the reasons, and states verbatim that running `dotnet run` locally against the compose database while the `adventuretime-api` container is running is unsupported (TR-66)
The README's seeding paragraph names `scripts/seed.sh`, its `BASE_URL` and `EPISODES_DIR` overrides, and states that it exits non-zero unless every delivered session ends Done (TR-56)

Every mandated section links to the corresponding TRD anchor (`#TR-14`, `#TR-63`, `#TR-66`) on the published artifact, and a Markdown preview shows the configuration table renders as a table (no broken pipes)

tickets.title: Run the full compose reset plus seed acceptance and record the results
tickets.context: The definition of done for the last epic: the README sequence run on a clean state and the results recorded.
tickets.motivation: The instructions have to actually work. Twenty-one Done sessions, twenty-one episodes carrying a session id, and continuity notes from the second stub analysis onward are the observable proof that schema, store, handlers, hosted services and seed work as one system.
tickets.goal: Recorded evidence of the full reset and seed completing exactly as the README prescribes.
tickets.value: The final proof, from an empty volume to a populated database, that the station works end to end.
tickets.description: Execute the WP6 definition of done end to end on a clean machine state and record the evidence in the PR: from the repo root run exactly the README upgrade sequence `docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d --build && scripts/seed.sh` (this doubles as the verification of the TR-14 procedure written in F6.1-T3). Watch `docker compose logs api` (compose sets `Logging__LogLevel__Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore=Information`, so EF logs each applied migration) for the `AddStation` migration being applied on the fresh volume and the `rehydration: 0 Working sessions failed as 'interrupted by restart'` line before the first request is served, and for the `analysis provider: Stub` line (the compose file sets `Station__AnalysisProvider=${STATION_ANALYSIS_PROVIDER:-Stub}` per TR-55). The script must end with `summary: done=21 failed=0 skipped=0` and exit 0. Then verify the data: `curl -s localhost:5256/api/episodes | jq 'length'` is 21 and every row has a non-null `sessionId`; `GET /api/station` shows `occupancy == 0`, an empty `live` array and 20 `recent` rows all `Done` (recent is capped at 20 by TR-21); `GET /api/episodes/{id}/analysis` (the re-routed action of TR-22) for the first seeded episode (S01E18 `Dungeon`) returns `continuityNotes == []`, for S11E01 `The Unfinished Map` (whose expected cast shares Finn/Jake/Princess Bubblegum with S01E18) returns the single note `follows S01E18 'Dungeon'`, and every other season-11 episode returns exactly one note under the stub (TR-47 emits one note for the first of the up-to-10 priors whose cast intersects). Do not start a second application instance (no local `dotnet run`) at any point during the run: the README `Single instance` section and TR-48/TR-66 explain that its boot would fail the container's Working rows, and the PR must cite that section as the reason. Paste the script's final summary line, the `jq` counts and the analysis responses into the PR description; fix any discrepancy in `scripts/seed.sh` or `README.md` under this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: `docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d --build && scripts/seed.sh`, run from the repo root exactly as the README section `Upgrading to migrations` prescribes, completes with exit status 0 and the final line `summary: done=21 failed=0 skipped=0` (TR-14, TR-56)

`docker compose logs api` shows the migration `AddStation` being applied on the fresh volume and the `rehydration: 0 Working sessions failed as 'interrupted by restart'` line before any manifest request is logged (TR-14, TR-48)
`curl -s http://localhost:5256/api/episodes | jq '[.[] | select(.sessionId != null)] | length'` prints 21 (TR-56, TR-22)

`curl -s http://localhost:5256/api/station | jq '{occupancy, live: (.live|length), recent: (.recent|length), states: ([.recent[].state]|unique)}'` prints `occupancy 0`, `live 0`, `recent 20`, `states ["Done"]` (TR-56, TR-21)

`GET /api/episodes/{id}/analysis` for the episode with season 1 / episodeNumber 18 returns `continuityNotes: []`, for season 11 / episodeNumber 1 returns exactly one note equal to `follows S01E18 'Dungeon'`, and for every season-11 episode `(.continuityNotes | length) == 1`, showing the sequential seed order made continuity reproducible (TR-56, TR-47)

A second invocation of `scripts/seed.sh` without resetting the volume exits 0 with `summary: done=0 failed=0 skipped=21`, confirming the documented upgrade sequence is the only path that re-seeds (TR-14, TR-56)

The PR description contains the pasted evidence (summary line, jq outputs, the S01E18 and S11E01 analysis responses) and cites the README `Single instance` section as the reason no concurrent local `dotnet run` was started during the run (TR-66)

review_notes: F6.1-T2 AC5 contradicted TR-20: it expected `GET /api/station` to show `occupancy == 0` after the 422 failure path, but a 422 delivery changes nothing, so the manifest stays Waiting and occupancy is 1 until its TTL elapses or it is cancelled. Rewritten to assert occupancy 1 with the Waiting row in `live`, then `DELETE` -> 204 -> occupancy 0.

F6.1-T2 branch sequencing was unreachable as written: the live-conflict path and the failure path both announced S11E01 against an already-seeded database, where announce returns 409 `episode exists` and the script skips the file instead of reaching the branch under test. Re-sequenced all four branches onto a single fresh volume (live conflict first, then 429, then second-run skip, then failure path) and pointed the failure-path scratch file at S99E50 so no second reset is needed.

F6.1-T2 credited the sweeper alone with expiring the three hand-made manifests; announce step 2 (TR-37) also runs the set-based ExpireOverdue under the advisory lock, so the retry succeeds as soon as the 60 s TTL elapses regardless of the 15 s sweep tick. Wording corrected.
F6.1-T3 title was 88 characters (limit 80). Shortened to 78.

F6.1-T1 gave an imprecise ordering command (`@tsv` without the filename, `sort -n -k1,1 -k2,2`). Pinned to `jq -r '[.season, .episodeNumber, input_filename] | @tsv'` piped to `sort -t$'\t' -k1,1n -k2,2n`, and specified the exact final summary line (`summary: done=<n> failed=<n> skipped=<n>`) that F6.1-T4 asserts on.

F6.1-T4 single-instance paragraph was incoherent (it proposed 'delivering one extra hand-made manifest with StubDelay unavailable in compose'). Rewritten: no second instance is started during the run; the PR cites the README `Single instance` section and TR-48/TR-66.

F6.1-T4 did not cover the WP6 definition of done 'the second analysis onward carries a continuity note under the stub'; added a criterion that every season-11 episode's analysis has exactly one continuity note (every S11 cast shares Finn, Jake or Princess Bubblegum with S01E18 and S11E01, verified against the seed files).

Verified against the repo: no README.md or scripts/ exists; docker-compose.yml maps 5256:8080, names the volume adventuretime-data, the container adventuretime-api and the database adventuretime; Program.cs enables Swagger only in Development; GET api/Episodes returns a plain array; all 21 seed files carry a focusCharacter; s1e8__dungeon.json is season 1 episodeNumber 18. Cross-feature dependencies reference F4.1-T1, F4.2-T1 and F5.3-T1; if those features number their completing ticket differently, remap to the ticket that lands the manifests API, the episodes rewrite and the MigrateAsync+rehydration boot respectively.
